items.title: Vanilla Birthday Layer Cake
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice (1/16 of the cake), unfrosted
items.body: A tender, buttery two-layer vanilla cake, the classic birthday cake. Frost it with vanilla or chocolate buttercream.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the middle. Grease the pans, line the bottoms with parchment circles, and grease the parchment. Flour the sides lightly, tapping out the extra.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Beat the butter and sugar on medium-high speed for 3 to 4 minutes, until pale and fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

On low speed, add the flour mixture in three parts and the milk in two, starting and ending with flour. Mix just until no flour shows. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Divide the batter between the pans and smooth the tops. Bake 28 to 32 minutes, until the tops spring back and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool in the pans 10 minutes, then turn the layers out onto racks, peel off the parchment and cool completely, about 1 hour, before frosting.
To frost, see “Frost a layer cake” on the Birthday parties page: a thin crumb coat, 20 minutes in the refrigerator, then the final coat.

swaps.cupcakes: This batter makes about 30 cupcakes; bake 18 to 20 minutes.
swaps.sheet: Bake it in a 9-by-13-inch pan for 35 to 40 minutes.
swaps.gluten_free: A cup-for-cup gluten-free flour blend that contains xanthan gum works in this cake.

items.title: Chocolate Birthday Layer Cake
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice (1/16 of the cake), unfrosted
items.body: A dark, moist one-bowl chocolate cake made with cocoa, oil and hot water. No mixer needed.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the pans, line the bottoms with parchment circles, and grease the parchment. Flour the sides lightly, tapping out the extra.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt in a large bowl until no lumps of cocoa remain.
Add the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla and whisk 2 minutes, until smooth.

A grown-up pours in the boiling water while whisking slowly. The batter will be thin; that’s right. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Pour into the pans and bake 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs but no wet batter.
Cool 10 minutes in the pans, then turn out onto racks and cool completely before frosting.

swaps.deeper_flavor: Use hot coffee instead of boiling water.
swaps.dairy_free: Use any plant milk with 1 tablespoon vinegar stirred in.
swaps.cupcakes: Makes about 30 cupcakes; bake 18 to 22 minutes.

items.title: Vanilla Sheet Cake for a Crowd
items.subtitle: snack · 1 square (1/24 of a half-sheet), unfrosted
items.body: One big, flat vanilla cake for a class or a crowd. Frost it right in the pan; no stacking or leveling.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the half-sheet pan, line it with parchment, and grease the parchment.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat the butter and sugar 4 minutes, until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

On low speed, add the flour in three parts and the milk in two, mixing just until smooth. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Spread the batter evenly in the pan. Bake 28 to 32 minutes, until golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool completely in the pan on a rack. Frost the top with 1½ batches of buttercream and cut 4 by 6 for 24 squares (or 6 by 8 for 48 small ones).
equipment: half-sheet pan (13 by 18 inches, 1 inch deep)

swaps.smaller: Halve everything and bake in a 9-by-13-inch pan for 30 to 35 minutes.

items.title: Chocolate Sheet Cake with Fudge Frosting
items.subtitle: snack · 1 square, frosted
items.body: A thin, fudgy chocolate cake in a half-sheet pan, with a glossy cocoa frosting poured over while it’s warm. Feeds a crowd, ready in about an hour.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease the half-sheet pan.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In a saucepan, bring the butter, cocoa and water to a boil, stirring. Pour it over the flour mixture and whisk until smooth.
Whisk in the buttermilk, eggs and vanilla. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Pour into the pan and spread it to the corners. Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.

About 5 minutes before the cake is done, make the frosting: melt the butter with the cocoa and milk in a saucepan, bring just to a simmer, take it off the heat and whisk in the powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the warm frosting over the hot cake and spread it quickly; it sets as it cools. Cool at least 30 minutes before cutting into 24 squares.

swaps.nuts: Many families scatter chopped pecans over the frosting; leave them off for a nut-free party.
swaps.buttermilk: Use ½ cup milk with 1½ teaspoons vinegar stirred in.

items.title: Vanilla Cupcakes
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cupcake, unfrosted
items.body: Soft vanilla cupcakes, 24 to a batch. Easy to carry to school, easy to hand out, no slicing.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line 24 muffin cups.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat the butter and sugar 3 minutes until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

On low, mix in the flour in three parts and the milk in two, just until smooth. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Fill the liners two-thirds full (a scant ¼ cup each). Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until the tops spring back and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool 5 minutes in the pans, then on racks. Frost when completely cool: swirl on buttercream with a knife, or pipe it from a zip-top bag with a corner snipped off.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a cup-for-cup gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant-based butter stick and plant milk; check the butter label for milk.

items.title: Chocolate Cupcakes
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cupcake, unfrosted
items.body: Moist one-bowl chocolate cupcakes made with cocoa and oil. They stay soft for days.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line 24 muffin cups.
Whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt.

Whisk in the eggs, milk, oil and vanilla until smooth. A grown-up whisks in the boiling water; the batter will be thin. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Fill the liners about half full (a pitcher or measuring cup makes it easy). Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely before frosting.

swaps.dairy_free: Use plant milk.

items.title: Egg-Free, Dairy-Free Chocolate Cake (Wacky Cake)
items.subtitle: snack · 1 square (1/9 of an 8-inch cake)
items.body: The old “wacky cake”: no eggs, milk or butter, mixed right in the pan, risen with baking soda and vinegar. Handy when a guest can’t have eggs or dairy.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. You don’t need to grease the pan.
Stir the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda and salt together right in the pan with a fork, and smooth it out.
Poke three wells in the dry mixture: a big one, a medium one and a small one. Pour the oil into the big one, the vinegar into the medium one and the vanilla into the small one.

Pour the water over everything and stir with the fork until no dry spots remain, getting into the corners. Don’t eat or taste the raw batter, and don’t let kids lick the spoon: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA). Bake it first.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool in the pan.
Dust with powdered sugar, or frost with a dairy-free buttercream (see the swaps).

swaps.frosting: For a dairy-free frosting, make the vanilla buttercream with vegetable shortening or a plant-based butter stick and plant milk. Check every label for milk.
swaps.cupcakes: Doubled, it makes about 20 cupcakes; bake 18 to 20 minutes.
swaps.gluten_free: Use a cup-for-cup gluten-free flour blend.

items.title: Vanilla Buttercream
items.subtitle: snack · about 3 tablespoons (makes about 3½ cups)
items.body: Fluffy American buttercream: butter beaten with powdered sugar, cream and vanilla. Enough to fill and frost a two-layer cake or 24 cupcakes.

steps: Beat the butter on medium-high for 3 minutes, until pale and creamy.
On low speed, add the powdered sugar a cup at a time. Add the cream, vanilla and salt.
Beat on medium-high 2 to 3 minutes, until light and fluffy. Add a spoonful more cream if it’s too stiff, or more sugar if too soft.
To tint it, stir in food coloring a drop at a time; gel colors give stronger color with less liquid.

swaps.dairy_free: Use vegetable shortening or a plant-based butter stick and plant milk; check labels for milk.

items.title: Chocolate Buttercream
items.subtitle: snack · about 3 tablespoons (makes about 3½ cups)
items.body: Creamy cocoa buttercream for filling and frosting a two-layer cake or 24 cupcakes.

steps: Beat the butter on medium-high for 3 minutes, until creamy.
On low speed, add the powdered sugar and cocoa alternately with the cream, a little at a time.
Add the vanilla and salt and beat on medium-high 2 to 3 minutes, until fluffy. Adjust with a spoonful of cream or sugar.

swaps.dairy_free: Use shortening or a plant-based butter stick and plant milk; check labels for milk.

items.title: Cream Cheese Frosting
items.subtitle: snack · about 3 tablespoons (makes about 3 cups)
items.body: Tangy, smooth frosting for chocolate, vanilla or carrot cake. A cake frosted with it lives in the refrigerator.

steps: Beat the cream cheese and butter together until smooth, about 2 minutes. Both should be soft, or you’ll get lumps.
On low speed, beat in the powdered sugar a cup at a time, then the vanilla and salt. Beat just until creamy; overbeating makes it runny.
Chill 15 minutes if it’s too soft to spread.
Keep a cake or cupcakes with this frosting in the refrigerator, and set it out for the party for no more than 2 hours (USDA).

items.title: Hot Fudge Sauce (and a Sundae Bar)
items.subtitle: snack · 2 tablespoons (makes about 1½ cups)
items.body: Thick, glossy chocolate sauce in 10 minutes, for an ice cream sundae bar at the party or a scoop next to the cake.

steps: Whisk the cream, corn syrup, brown sugar, cocoa and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a simmer, whisking, and simmer 1 minute.
Take it off the heat. Add the chocolate chips and butter, wait 1 minute, then whisk until smooth. Stir in the vanilla.
Serve warm. A grown-up should check that it’s warm, not hot, before kids spoon it on.
For a sundae bar, set out scoops of ice cream in cups just before serving, with the fudge, berries, sliced bananas, sprinkles and whipped cream. Put the ice cream back in the freezer between rounds.

swaps.dairy_free: Use full-fat coconut milk, coconut oil and dairy-free chips.

items.title: Make-Your-Own Mini Pizzas
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 2 mini pizzas
items.body: English muffin halves the guests top themselves with sauce, cheese and toppings. A party activity and lunch in one.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. If you like a crisper base, toast the muffin halves on the sheets for 4 minutes first.

Set out the muffin halves, sauce, cheese and toppings in bowls. Each guest spreads a spoonful of sauce, sprinkles cheese and adds toppings. Write names on the parchment with a pencil so everyone gets their own.
A grown-up bakes them 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese melts and bubbles.
Cool 3 minutes; melted cheese is very hot. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA).

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free English muffins or bagels.
swaps.from_scratch: Use the from-scratch pizza dough, rolled into 4-inch rounds; bake 10 to 12 minutes.
swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free cheese.

items.title: Party Pigs in a Blanket
items.subtitle: snack · 3 pieces (makes 24)
items.body: Little pieces of hot dog wrapped in biscuit dough and baked golden. The snack that disappears first.

ingredients.prep: refrigerated biscuits, each cut in 3 strips

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Cut each biscuit into 3 strips and stretch each strip a little. Wrap one around each piece of hot dog, pinching the end underneath.
Set them seam side down on the sheet and brush with egg if you like.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until golden. The hot dogs should be steaming hot, 165°F (USDA).

Cool 5 minutes. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA). For guests under 4, cut them into small pieces; hot dogs are a choking hazard for young children (CDC).

swaps.puff_pastry: Use a sheet of thawed puff pastry cut in strips; bake at 400°F.
swaps.from_scratch: Use a half batch of from-scratch biscuit dough.

items.title: Crispy Baked Chicken Tenders
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 3 tenders
items.body: Chicken tenders coated in Parmesan panko and baked until crunchy. Everyone’s party favorite, without frying.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Set a rack on each baking sheet if you have them and brush with oil.
Set out three dishes: flour with half the salt; eggs beaten with a spoonful of water; panko mixed with the Parmesan, garlic powder, paprika, the rest of the salt and the oil.
Pat the chicken dry. Dip each tender in flour, then egg, then press it into the crumbs. Lay them on the racks. Wash your hands, and anything raw chicken touched.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, turning once, until golden and a food thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest tender (USDA).
Serve with ranch, ketchup or honey mustard. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA).

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free flour and crushed corn flakes.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the Parmesan and add ½ teaspoon more salt.

items.title: Baked Ham and Cheese Party Sliders
items.subtitle: lunch,snack · 1 slider
items.body: A whole tray of soft sweet rolls filled with ham and Swiss, brushed with butter and mustard and baked until melty.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Without pulling the rolls apart, slice the whole slab in half horizontally with a serrated knife. Set the bottom in the baking dish.
Layer the ham and cheese over the bottom, then put the top back on.
Stir the butter, mustard and onion powder together and brush it over the tops.
Cover with foil and bake 15 minutes, then uncover and bake 5 minutes more, until the cheese melts and the centers are hot.
Cut into 12 sliders. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA).

swaps.mustard: Leave out the mustard for picky eaters.

items.title: Veggie Cups with Ranch Dip
items.subtitle: snack,side · 1 cup
items.body: Each guest gets a cup with ranch in the bottom and vegetable sticks standing up in it. No double-dipping, and it looks bright on the table.

steps: Cut the celery, cucumber and pepper into sticks about 4 inches long, so they stand up above the rim.
Spoon 2 tablespoons of ranch into the bottom of each cup.
Stand 4 carrots and a few sticks of each vegetable in each cup.
Keep the cups in the refrigerator until serving, then set them out on a tray of ice. At the party, set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate what’s left (USDA).

swaps.hummus: Use hummus in some cups for guests who can’t have milk or eggs (it contains sesame).
swaps.from_scratch: Make the ranch dressing from scratch.

items.title: Fresh-Squeezed Party Lemonade
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cup
items.body: Real lemonade from fresh lemons and a simple syrup, a gallon pitcher for the party. Not too sweet; add more syrup to taste.

steps: Make a syrup: heat the sugar with 1 cup of the water, stirring, until it dissolves. Let it cool.
Squeeze the lemons and strain out the seeds.
In a pitcher, stir the lemon juice, syrup and the remaining 6 cups of cold water. Taste and add a little more water or sugar.
Chill, and serve over ice with lemon slices.

swaps.pink: Stir in ½ cup of strawberry purée.
swaps.sparkling: Use sparkling water for half of the water.

items.title: Foil-Packet Hamburger Dinners
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 packet
items.body: The classic campfire supper: a seasoned beef patty on sliced potatoes, carrots and onion, sealed in foil and cooked in the coals.

steps: At home or at camp: mix the beef with half the salt, the pepper and garlic powder, and shape 4 patties about ¾ inch thick. Wash your hands before and after handling raw meat; bring soap and water, or wipes, if there’s no tap (USDA).

Tear four sheets of heavy-duty foil about 18 inches long. (Or double up regular foil.) Divide the potatoes, carrots and onion among them, sprinkle with the rest of the salt and dot with butter. Lay a patty on top.
Bring the long sides of the foil together and fold them down twice, then fold the ends in tightly, so the steam stays in.

Cook over a bed of glowing coals in an established fire ring or on a camp grill, not over tall flames. Use long tongs and heat-proof gloves, and open packets away from your face: the steam is very hot. Cook 30 to 40 minutes, turning the packets over halfway.
Open one packet carefully and check: the potatoes should be tender and the beef should read 160°F in the center (USDA). If not, reseal it and cook 5 minutes more.

swaps.stove: No fire? Cook the packets on a camp grill over medium heat, or in a covered skillet on the camp stove.
swaps.turkey: Use ground turkey and cook to 165°F.

items.title: Foil-Packet Italian Chicken and Vegetables
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 packet
items.body: Chunks of chicken with zucchini, peppers and onion, olive oil and Italian herbs, cooked in foil packets over the coals.

steps: At home, put the chicken in a sealed container or zip-top bag with half the oil, the seasoning, garlic powder and salt. Put the vegetables in another bag with the rest of the oil and the pepper. Keep the raw meat in the cooler at 40°F or below, sealed and packed below ready-to-eat food, until it goes on the fire (USDA).

Tear four sheets of heavy-duty foil about 18 inches long. (Or double up regular foil.) Divide the vegetables and chicken among them. Fold the long sides together twice and crimp the ends. Wash your hands before and after handling raw meat; bring soap and water, or wipes, if there’s no tap (USDA).

Cook over a bed of glowing coals in an established fire ring or on a camp grill, not over tall flames. Use long tongs and heat-proof gloves, and open packets away from your face: the steam is very hot. Cook 20 to 25 minutes, turning once.
Open one packet carefully and check the biggest piece of chicken: it must read 165°F (USDA). Sprinkle with Parmesan.

swaps.rice: Serve over instant rice made on the camp stove.
swaps.shrimp: Use peeled shrimp and cook 8 to 10 minutes, until opaque.

items.title: Foil-Packet Sausage, Potatoes and Corn
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 packet
items.body: Smoked sausage, little potatoes, corn on the cob and green beans with butter and paprika. Like a shrimp boil without the pot.

steps: At home, microwave or boil the halved potatoes 5 minutes, until just starting to soften, so they finish in the fire with everything else. Cool and pack them in the cooler.
Toss the potatoes, corn, green beans and sausage with the butter, paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Tear four sheets of heavy-duty foil about 18 inches long. (Or double up regular foil.) Divide everything among them and seal: long sides folded together twice, ends crimped.

Cook over a bed of glowing coals in an established fire ring or on a camp grill, not over tall flames. Use long tongs and heat-proof gloves, and open packets away from your face: the steam is very hot. Cook 25 to 35 minutes, turning once, until the potatoes are tender. Smoked sausage is already cooked; heat it until steaming, 165°F (USDA).

swaps.veggie: Use plant-based sausage, or a drained can of chickpeas.

items.title: Campfire Banana Boats
items.subtitle: snack · 1 banana
items.body: A banana split in its peel, stuffed with chocolate chips and marshmallows and warmed in the coals until gooey. Eat it with a spoon.

ingredients.prep: cut in half, or 1 cup minis

steps: With the peel on, cut a slit down the inside curve of each banana, through the fruit but not the bottom peel. Open it a little to make a pocket.
Stuff the pocket with chocolate chips and marshmallows. Wrap each banana in foil.
Set them on the grate or at the edge of the coals for 5 to 8 minutes, until the chocolate melts.
Let them cool 2 minutes before opening; melted marshmallow is very hot. Top with graham crumbs and eat from the peel with a spoon.

swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free chocolate chips.
swaps.smores: Make classic s’mores from scratch too.

items.title: Campfire Dutch-Oven Chili
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1½ cups
items.body: A big pot of beef and bean chili, simmered over the fire or a camp stove. Warms everyone up on a cool night.

steps: At home, chop the onion and pepper and mix the spices in a small bag. Keep the raw meat in the cooler at 40°F or below, sealed and packed below ready-to-eat food, until it goes on the fire (USDA).

Set the Dutch oven on a grate over the fire (or a camp stove over medium-high heat) and add the oil. Brown the beef with the onion and pepper, breaking it up, 8 to 10 minutes, until no pink remains and it reads 160°F (USDA). Spoon off extra fat into a can to pack out.
Stir in the spices, then the beans, tomatoes and tomato sauce.
Bring to a simmer, then move the pot to a cooler part of the grate (or turn the stove to low). Cover and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes so it doesn’t catch on the bottom.
Serve with cheese, over walking-taco chips or with bannock.
equipment: 12-inch cast-iron Dutch oven or large pot

swaps.veggie: Skip the beef and add a third can of beans plus a can of corn.

items.title: Camp Skillet Breakfast Hash
items.subtitle: breakfast · about 1½ cups with 2 eggs
items.body: Bacon, crispy hash browns, peppers and onion in one big skillet, with eggs cooked right on top. Breakfast for the whole campsite.

ingredients.prep: kept in the cooler; thawed is fine

steps: Cook the bacon in the skillet over medium heat until crisp. Lift it out, leaving about 2 tablespoons of fat in the pan. Pour the rest into a can to cool and pack out.
Add the hash browns, onion and pepper. Spread them out and leave them alone 5 minutes to brown, then stir and cook 8 to 10 minutes more, until crisp and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir the bacon back in. Make 8 wells and crack an egg into each. Cover with a lid or foil and cook on low 6 to 8 minutes, until the whites and yolks are firm (USDA).
Sprinkle with cheese, cover a minute to melt it, and serve from the pan.
equipment: 12-inch cast-iron skillet with a lid (or foil)

swaps.veggie: Skip the bacon and use 2 tablespoons of oil; add mushrooms or spinach.
swaps.burritos: Scoop it into tortillas for breakfast burritos.

items.title: Shake-and-Pour Camp Pancakes
items.subtitle: breakfast · 3 pancakes
items.body: Mix the dry ingredients at home in a bottle with powdered milk. At camp, add water and oil, shake, and pour. No eggs to keep cold.

steps: At home: put the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and dry milk in a clean, dry 1-quart bottle or jar (a funnel helps). Close it and label it “add 1½ cups water + 3 tbsp oil.”
At camp: add the water and oil, close the lid tightly and shake hard for about 30 seconds, until there are no dry pockets. A few small lumps are fine.
Heat an oiled griddle over medium-low on the camp stove. Pour ¼-cup pancakes straight from the bottle.
Cook until bubbles cover the top and the edges look dry, about 2 minutes, then flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until golden and cooked through. Don’t taste the raw batter (FDA).
equipment: 1-quart wide-mouth bottle or jar with a tight lid

swaps.blueberries: Drop a few blueberries onto each pancake after pouring.
swaps.from_scratch: Use 2 cups of the from-scratch pancake mix.

items.title: Dutch-Oven Peach Cobbler
items.subtitle: snack · about ¾ cup
items.body: Canned peaches under a buttery batter, baked in a Dutch oven with coals underneath and on the lid. The classic campout dessert.

ingredients.prep: in juice, drained (save ½ cup juice)

steps: At home, mix the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and half the cinnamon in a bag.
Light about 26 briquettes in a chimney starter in the fire ring or on bare ground cleared of anything that can burn. When they are covered in gray ash (15 to 20 minutes), they are ready.
Line the Dutch oven with foil if you like (for easy cleanup). Spread the peaches and saved juice in the bottom and sprinkle with the rest of the cinnamon.
Stir the milk and melted butter into the dry mix just until combined, and spoon the batter over the peaches.

Put on the lid. Set the oven over 9 briquettes in a ring and put 17 on the lid, spread evenly. This is about 350°F for a 12-inch oven (diameter × 2, plus 2 for each 25°F, two-thirds on top for baking).

Bake 35 to 45 minutes, turning the oven a quarter turn one way and the lid a quarter turn the other every 15 minutes so it browns evenly. Lift the lid carefully, brushing ash away, to check: the top should be golden and a knife come out clean.
Let it cool 10 minutes; the fruit is very hot. When done, put the used coals in the fire ring and put them out completely: drown, stir, drown and feel.
equipment: 12-inch camp Dutch oven with legs and a flat, rimmed lid
charcoal briquettes and a chimney starter

swaps.oven: At home, bake it in a 9-by-13-inch dish at 350°F for 40 to 45 minutes.
swaps.dry_milk: Use ¼ cup dry milk in the bag and ¾ cup water at camp, so nothing needs the cooler.

items.title: Campfire Bannock (Skillet or Stick)
items.subtitle: side,breakfast · 1 wedge
items.body: A simple flatbread of flour, baking powder, fat and water, cooked in a skillet or wrapped around a stick over the coals. A camp staple for centuries.

steps: At home, mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt and rub in the shortening with your fingers until it looks like coarse crumbs. Pack it in a zip-top bag; it keeps 2 weeks.
At camp, add the water a little at a time, squeezing the bag or stirring in a bowl, until it makes a soft dough that isn’t sticky. Knead it a few times.

Skillet: pat the dough into a round about ¾ inch thick. Heat the oil in the skillet over low coals or a low stove flame and cook 8 to 10 minutes per side, until golden and it sounds hollow when tapped. Keep the heat low so the middle cooks before the outside burns.
On a stick: roll pieces of dough into ropes and wind them around clean sticks. Hold them over glowing coals, turning, 8 to 10 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Don’t eat raw dough (FDA).
Cut into wedges and eat warm, with butter, jam or the chili.
equipment: mixing bowl or a sturdy zip-top bag
clean green sticks or metal roasting sticks (optional)

swaps.sweet: Add a handful of raisins or berries and a pinch of cinnamon.
swaps.traditional: Lard is the traditional fat in many families; butter works too.

items.title: Walking Tacos
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 bag of chips with toppings
items.body: Taco meat spooned straight into a bag of tortilla chips, topped and eaten with a fork. Hardly any dishes to wash at camp.

ingredients.prep: in 6 single-serving bags or zip-top bags

steps: Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat on the camp stove, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reads 160°F (USDA). Spoon off extra fat into a can to pack out.
Stir in the seasoning and water and simmer 5 minutes, until thick.
Crush the chips a little in each bag, open it, and spoon in the meat. Let everyone add cheese, lettuce, tomato, salsa and sour cream, then eat out of the bag with a fork.
Keep the cheese, lettuce, salsa and sour cream in the cooler until serving and put them back within 2 hours, or 1 hour on a day above 90°F (USDA).

swaps.veggie: Use the seasoned lentil taco filling or black beans.

items.title: Pie-Iron Pizza Pockets
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1 pocket
items.body: Buttered bread around pizza sauce, mozzarella and pepperoni, toasted in a pie iron over the coals until crisp and melty.

steps: Butter one side of each slice of bread.
Open a pie iron and lay a slice, butter side down, in one half. Spread with 2 tablespoons of sauce, add a quarter of the cheese and 4 slices of pepperoni, and top with another slice, butter side up.
Close the iron, latch it, and trim any bread sticking out.
Hold it over glowing coals (not in the flames) 2 to 4 minutes per side, peeking once, until golden. Open it carefully: the iron and filling are very hot. Cool 2 minutes before eating.

swaps.dessert: Fill with canned pie filling or chocolate chips and marshmallows.
swaps.skillet: No pie iron? Cook them like grilled cheese in a skillet.

items.title: One-Pot Camp Stove Mac and Cheese
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1¼ cups
items.body: Macaroni cooked in just enough water to soak up, then stirred with milk, butter and cheddar. One pot, no draining.

steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil in the pot over the camp stove.
Add the macaroni and cook, stirring often, 8 to 10 minutes, until tender and most of the water is soaked up. Add a splash more water if it gets dry before the pasta is done.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the milk and butter until hot, then the cheese a handful at a time until creamy. Season with pepper.

swaps.shelf_stable: Use a can of evaporated milk instead of fresh milk; it needs no cooler until opened.
swaps.add_ins: Stir in chopped hot dogs or leftover chili.

items.title: Cinnamon Sugar Biscuits on a Stick
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 twist
items.body: Biscuit dough twisted around a roasting stick, toasted over the coals, then rolled in butter and cinnamon sugar.

steps: Mix the sugar and cinnamon on a plate. Melt the butter in a small pot at the edge of the fire.
Roll each biscuit into a rope about 8 inches long and wind it around the end of a stick, pinching the ends.
Hold it a few inches above glowing coals, turning slowly, 8 to 12 minutes, until golden all over and cooked through; it should slide off easily and feel light. Don’t eat raw dough (FDA).
Slide it off, brush with butter and roll in cinnamon sugar. Let it cool a minute before biting.
equipment: clean roasting sticks or long metal skewers
small pot or foil pan for butter

items.title: Nut-Free Camp Trail Mix
items.subtitle: snack · ½ cup
items.body: Seeds, oat cereal, pretzels, raisins, cranberries and a few chocolate chips. All the crunch of trail mix, without peanuts or tree nuts.

steps: Stir everything together in a big bowl.
Scoop ½-cup portions into small bags, one per hiker per snack, so nobody reaches into a shared bag with unwashed hands.
equipment: bags or containers for each hiker

swaps.nut_free: Check the seed, cereal and chocolate labels for “may contain” warnings if someone has a severe allergy.
swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pretzels and cereal.

items.title: Homemade Hot Cocoa Mix
items.subtitle: snack · ⅓ cup mix (1 mug)
items.body: Powdered milk, cocoa and sugar mixed at home. At camp, stir a scoop into a mug of hot water for cocoa by the fire.

steps: Whisk the dry milk, powdered sugar, cocoa and salt together until no lumps remain, and pack it in a jar or bag.
At camp, heat safe drinking water. If your water comes from a lake or stream, bring it to a rolling boil for 1 minute first (USDA).
Stir ⅓ cup of mix into 1 cup of hot water. Let it cool to sipping temperature before handing it to kids.

swaps.richer: Add ½ cup of chocolate chips, finely chopped.
swaps.dairy_free: Use powdered coconut milk.

items.title: Sugar Cookie Cutouts with Royal Icing
items.subtitle: snack · 1 iced cookie (about 3 inches)
items.body: Buttery cutouts that hold their shape in the oven, iced with smooth royal icing that dries hard enough to stack. The cookie most people picture for decorating day.

steps: Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the egg and vanilla.

Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then mix them in on low speed just until no dry flour shows. Don’t taste the raw dough: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA and CDC). Bake first, then taste.
Divide the dough in half, flatten each into a disk, wrap, and chill at least 1 hour (up to 3 days). Cold dough keeps sharp edges.

Heat the oven to 350°F and line the sheets with parchment. Roll one disk between two sheets of parchment, or on a floured counter, to ¼ inch thick. Cut shapes and set them 1 inch apart. Gather the scraps, chill, and roll again.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges are just turning golden. Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then on a rack until completely cool before icing.

Make the icing: beat the powdered sugar, egg whites and lemon juice on medium-high for 4 to 5 minutes, until thick and glossy. Use pasteurized egg whites, because this icing is never cooked (FDA advises pasteurized eggs for raw-egg recipes).

For outlines, keep the icing thick. For filling in (“flooding”), stir in water a few drops at a time until a ribbon of icing sinks back in about 10 seconds. Tint small bowls with gel food coloring. Keep the bowls covered with a damp towel; the icing crusts fast.

Pipe an outline, let it set 10 minutes, then flood the middle and nudge it into the corners with a toothpick. Add sprinkles while it’s wet. Let the cookies dry, uncovered, 6 hours or overnight before stacking.

swaps.meringue_powder: Use 2 tablespoons meringue powder and 5 to 6 tablespoons water instead of the egg whites.
swaps.egg_free_icing: For a simple glaze, stir 2 cups powdered sugar with 3 tablespoons milk; it stays softer than royal icing.

items.title: Gingerbread People
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie (about 4 inches)
items.body: Dark, spicy molasses cookies, soft in the middle with crisp edges. Decorate with royal icing buttons and smiles.

steps: Beat the butter and brown sugar until fluffy. Beat in the egg, then the molasses.

Whisk the flour, baking soda, salt and spices, and mix them in on low speed. The dough will be soft. Don’t taste the raw dough: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA and CDC). Bake first, then taste.
Divide in half, flatten into disks, wrap and chill at least 2 hours, or up to 3 days.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Roll the dough ¼ inch thick on a floured counter and cut out people. Set them 1 inch apart on parchment-lined sheets. Press in raisins for eyes if you like.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes: shorter for soft cookies, longer for crisp ones. They firm up as they cool. Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then on a rack.
Decorate with royal icing (see the sugar cookie recipe) or a simple powdered-sugar glaze once they’re completely cool.

swaps.stronger: For a bolder cookie, add ½ teaspoon black pepper and use dark brown sugar.

items.title: Gingerbread House
items.subtitle: snack · 1 piece when you break it up (it’s mostly for looking at)
items.body: A sturdy construction gingerbread, baked flat and hard, glued together with stiff royal icing and covered in candy. A family project for a December weekend.

steps: Cut paper templates: two side walls 7 by 4 inches, two end walls 6 inches wide and 4 inches tall at the sides rising to a peak of 7 inches, and two roof panels 7½ by 5 inches.
Heat the shortening, brown sugar, molasses and water in a saucepan just until the shortening melts. Cool 10 minutes.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, salt and spices in a big bowl. Stir in the molasses mixture to make a stiff dough; knead it smooth with your hands.

Heat the oven to 350°F. Roll the dough ⅛ to ¼ inch thick right on sheets of parchment. Lay the templates on top and cut around them; pull away the scraps. Cut windows and a door if you like. Slide the parchment onto baking sheets.

Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until firm and a little darker at the edges. While still warm, lay the templates back on and trim any edges that spread, so the walls fit. Cool completely on the sheets, at least 2 hours or overnight.
Beat the powdered sugar and pasteurized egg whites for 5 minutes until very thick, like toothpaste. Keep it covered with a damp towel.

Build: pipe a thick line of icing on the board and stand a side wall in it. Pipe icing up the edge and press an end wall against it. Add the other walls the same way, propping them with cans. Let them set 1 hour before adding the roof panels, then let the whole house set 2 hours before decorating.
Decorate with icing “snow” and candy. This house is for display: after a few days on the table it’s dry and dusty. Break off a piece the first day if you want a taste.
equipment: ruler and sharp knife or pizza cutter
a cake board or tray to build on
small cans or jars to prop the walls

swaps.kit: Short on time? Bake gingerbread people instead and let everyone decorate one.
swaps.graham: For little kids, build mini houses from graham crackers glued to a milk carton with the same icing.

meta.servings: 1 piece when you break it up (it’s mostly for looking at)

items.title: Scottish-Style Butter Shortbread
items.subtitle: snack · 1 finger
items.body: Three main ingredients, butter, sugar and flour, pressed into a pan and baked low and slow until pale gold and sandy-crisp. Keeps for weeks and packs well for gifts.

ingredients.prep: or rice flour, for extra tenderness

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Beat the butter, ¾ cup sugar and vanilla until creamy but not fluffy, about 1 minute.
Whisk the flour, cornstarch and salt and mix them in on low until the dough just comes together in crumbly clumps.
Press it evenly into the ungreased pan with your fingers, then smooth it with the back of a spoon. Prick all over with a fork and sprinkle with the 1 tablespoon sugar.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until pale golden at the edges and firm in the middle.
Right away, cut into 24 fingers (3 rows by 8). Cool completely in the pan before lifting them out; they crisp as they cool.

swaps.dipped: Dip one end of each finger in melted dark chocolate.
swaps.brown_butter: Brown the butter, chill it until soft-solid, then go on as written.

items.title: Snickerdoodles
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie
items.body: Soft, crackly cookies rolled in cinnamon sugar. Cream of tartar gives them their slight tang and pillowy middle.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line the sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy, then beat in the eggs one at a time.
Whisk the flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt, and mix them in on low. Don’t taste the raw dough: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA and CDC). Bake first, then taste.
Stir the cinnamon sugar together. Roll the dough into balls about 1½ inches across, roll them in the cinnamon sugar, and set them 2 inches apart.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges are set and the tops crackled but still soft. Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then on a rack.

swaps.no_cream_of_tartar: Use 2 teaspoons baking powder instead of the cream of tartar and baking soda; the cookies will be a little less tangy.

items.title: Jam Thumbprint Cookies
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie
items.body: Tender butter cookies with a thumb-pressed well of bright jam. Use raspberry and apricot for a red-and-gold tray.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line the sheets with parchment.

Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy. Beat in the yolks and vanilla, then the flour and salt on low until a soft dough forms. Don’t taste the raw dough: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA and CDC). Bake first, then taste.
Roll into 1-inch balls and set them 2 inches apart. Press a deep well in each with your thumb or the back of a ½-teaspoon measure. Chill the trays 15 minutes.
Fill each well with about ½ teaspoon jam; don’t overfill.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes, until the bottoms are light golden. Cool on the sheet 5 minutes, then on a rack. The jam stays sticky for a while, so let them sit before stacking.

swaps.nutty: Roll the balls in finely chopped walnuts or pecans before pressing (this adds tree nuts).
swaps.egg_free: Leave out the yolks and add 2 tablespoons milk.

items.title: Spritz Butter Cookies
items.subtitle: snack · 2 small cookies
items.body: Little pressed butter cookies in wreaths, trees and flowers. Their name comes from the German word for “to squirt,” which is what the press does.

ingredients.prep: or 1 teaspoon vanilla and ½ teaspoon almond extract

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Use cool, bare baking sheets: the dough has to stick to the pan to come off the press.

Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy. Beat in the egg and vanilla, then the flour and salt on low. Don’t taste the raw dough: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA and CDC). Bake first, then taste.
Tint the dough with gel food coloring if you like. Pack it into the press with your chosen disk.
Hold the press upright against the sheet, squeeze once, and lift. Space cookies 1 inch apart. If they don’t stick, chill the pan 5 minutes.
Decorate with sprinkles and bake 7 to 9 minutes, until the edges just start to color. Cool 2 minutes, then move to a rack.

swaps.chocolate: Replace ¼ cup of the flour with cocoa powder.

items.title: Chocolate Crinkle Cookies
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie
items.body: Fudgy cocoa cookies rolled in powdered sugar that cracks into a snowy pattern as they bake.

steps: Whisk the cocoa, sugar and oil. Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.

Stir in the flour, baking powder and salt. The dough will be soft and sticky. Cover and chill at least 3 hours or overnight. Don’t taste the raw dough: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA and CDC). Bake first, then taste.
Heat the oven to 350°F and line the sheets with parchment.
Roll tablespoons of dough into balls and roll them thickly in powdered sugar. Set 2 inches apart.
Bake 10 to 11 minutes, until the edges are set and the tops cracked. They look soft but firm up as they cool.

swaps.mint: Add ½ teaspoon peppermint extract with the vanilla.

items.title: Peppermint Bark
items.subtitle: snack · 1 piece (about 1 oz)
items.body: A layer of dark chocolate, a layer of white chocolate and a shower of crushed candy canes. No baking, and it makes a pretty gift.

steps: Line the pan with parchment, leaving some hanging over the sides.

Melt the dark chocolate in a heatproof bowl set over a pan of barely simmering water, stirring until smooth (or microwave in 20-second bursts, stirring each time). Spread it in the pan and refrigerate 15 minutes, until just set.
Melt the white chocolate the same way, gently: it scorches easily. Let it cool a few minutes so it doesn’t melt the dark layer, then spread it on top.
Scatter the crushed candy canes over it right away and press them in lightly.
Refrigerate 30 to 45 minutes until firm. Lift out with the parchment and break or cut into 24 pieces.
equipment: saucepan for a water bath (or a microwave)

swaps.gift: Pack in cellophane bags or small tins with a label listing milk and soy (from the chocolate).

items.title: Easy Chocolate Fudge
items.subtitle: snack · 1 square (about 1¼ inches)
items.body: Smooth, rich fudge from chocolate chips and sweetened condensed milk, with no candy thermometer needed. Add nuts if your family eats them.

steps: Line the pan with foil or parchment, leaving overhang to lift it out.
Put the chocolate chips, condensed milk and butter in the saucepan over low heat. Stir constantly until melted and smooth, about 5 minutes. Keep the heat low so it doesn’t scorch.
Off the heat, stir in the vanilla, salt and walnuts if using.
Spread in the pan and smooth the top. Refrigerate about 2 hours until firm.
Lift out and cut into 36 squares, or 24 larger ones. Wipe the knife between cuts for neat edges.

swaps.peppermint: Use white chocolate chips and top with crushed candy canes.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the walnuts; top with sprinkles instead.

items.title: Standing Rib Roast (Prime Rib)
items.subtitle: dinner · about ⅔ lb as bought (one thick slice)
items.body: A bone-in beef rib roast with a garlic, herb and black-pepper crust, roasted at 325°F the USDA way. The bones make their own rack and the drippings make the Yorkshire puddings.

steps: For the best crust, salt the roast a day ahead: pat it dry, rub the salt all over, and refrigerate it uncovered on a rack over a tray, away from ready-to-eat foods.
Heat the oven to 325°F (USDA advises roasting meat at 325°F or higher). Mix the pepper, garlic, rosemary, thyme and oil and rub it over the fat and cut sides.

Set the roast fat side up, bones down, in the pan. Roast. USDA’s guide time for a 4- to 8-lb bone-in rib roast at 325°F is 23 to 30 minutes per pound; a 5½-lb roast takes about 2 to 2¾ hours. Start checking an hour before the shortest time.
Check with a food thermometer in the thickest part, not touching bone. Take it out at 145°F for medium-rare, or 160°F for medium. USDA’s safe minimum for beef roasts is 145°F with a 3-minute rest.
Tent loosely with foil and rest 20 to 30 minutes (at least 3). The temperature rises a few degrees as it rests, and the oven is free for the Yorkshire puddings.

Pour the drippings from the pan for the puddings and gravy. To carve, cut along the bones to free the meat in one piece, then slice it across the grain about ¾ inch thick. Serve the ribs alongside for anyone who likes to gnaw.
equipment: heavy roasting pan with a rack (or the rib bones as the rack)

swaps.boneless: A 4-lb boneless rib roast takes 39 to 43 minutes per pound at 325°F (USDA); tie it so it keeps its shape.
swaps.smaller: Figure about 1 rib for every 2 people.

meta.servings: about ⅔ lb as bought (one thick slice)

items.title: Yorkshire Puddings
items.subtitle: side · 1 pudding
items.body: Tall, crisp, hollow puddings baked in sizzling beef drippings. The classic partner for roast beef, from northern England.

ingredients.prep: beef drippings from the roast, or vegetable oil

steps: Whisk the eggs, milk, flour and salt until smooth, or blend 10 seconds. Pour into a pitcher and let the batter rest at least 30 minutes at room temperature (or up to a day in the refrigerator).
When the roast comes out, turn the oven to 450°F. Put 1 teaspoon drippings in each muffin cup and heat the tin in the oven 10 minutes, until the fat is very hot.
Working fast, open the oven, pull the rack out a little, and pour batter into the cups about halfway. Hot fat can spit, so pour carefully and keep your face back.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes without opening the door, until puffed high and deep golden. Serve right away.

swaps.toad_in_hole: Pour the batter over browned sausages in a hot baking dish for “toad in the hole.”
swaps.no_drippings: Use vegetable oil or lard instead of beef drippings.

items.title: Horseradish Cream Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 2 tablespoons
items.body: Cool sour cream with a sharp bite of horseradish and a little lemon. The sauce for prime rib.

steps: Stir everything together. Taste and add more horseradish if you like it hotter.
Chill at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 days, so the flavors blend.

swaps.lighter: Use plain Greek yogurt for half the sour cream.

items.title: Beef Pan Gravy
items.subtitle: side · about ¼ cup
items.body: A smooth brown gravy made from the roast’s drippings and beef broth while the meat rests.

ingredients.prep: fat from the roast's drippings, or butter

steps: Pour the drippings into a cup and let the fat rise. Spoon 3 tablespoons fat back into the pan; save the dark juices underneath.
Set the pan over medium heat (across two burners if it’s big). Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring, 2 minutes, until it smells toasty.
Whisk in the broth and the saved juices a little at a time, scraping up the browned bits. Simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until it coats a spoon.
Stir in the Worcestershire, then taste before salting: drippings can be salty. Strain if you like it very smooth.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 1½ tablespoons cornstarch stirred into ¼ cup cold broth instead of the flour; skip the cooking-the-flour step.

items.title: Extra-Crisp Roast Potatoes
items.subtitle: side · about 1 cup
items.body: Potatoes boiled until just tender, shaken in the colander to rough up their edges, then roasted in hot fat until glassy-crisp outside and fluffy inside.

ingredients.prep: or Yukon-type, peeled and cut in 2-inch chunks
for the cooking water (most is poured away)
or beef drippings, duck fat or lard

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Put the potatoes in the pot, cover with cold water, add 1 tablespoon salt, and bring to a boil. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes, until the outsides are soft but the centers still firm.
While they boil, put the oil in the roasting pan and heat it in the oven 5 minutes.
Drain the potatoes well and let them steam 2 minutes. Shake the colander hard so the edges turn fluffy and rough.
Carefully tip the potatoes into the hot oil (it will sizzle), turn them to coat, and sprinkle with the kosher salt.
Roast 45 to 55 minutes, turning every 15 minutes, adding the rosemary and garlic for the last 15. They’re done when deep golden and crunchy.
equipment: large roasting pan or rimmed baking sheet

swaps.shared_oven: Roasting alongside the beef at 325°F? Give them 70 to 80 minutes, then crisp them at 450°F with the Yorkshire puddings.

items.title: Honey-Roasted Carrots and Parsnips
items.subtitle: side · about ¾ cup
items.body: Sweet root vegetables roasted until caramelized, then tossed with honey and thyme. A classic on British and American holiday tables.

ingredients.prep: peeled, halved lengthwise and cut in 3-inch sticks
peeled, cut like the carrots (core removed if woody)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the carrots and parsnips with the oil, salt and pepper and spread them on the sheet in one layer.
Roast 25 minutes, stir, and roast 10 minutes more, until browned and tender.
Drizzle with honey, scatter the thyme over and toss on the hot pan.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

items.title: Berry and Custard Trifle
items.subtitle: snack · about 1 cup
items.body: Layers of soft sponge cake, raspberry jam, berries, homemade vanilla custard and whipped cream in a glass bowl. A British Christmas classic, made family-style with orange juice instead of sherry.

ingredients.prep: fresh or thawed frozen, plus strawberries

steps: Bake the sponge: heat the oven to 350°F and grease and flour the pan. Beat the eggs and sugar on high until pale and thick, 5 minutes. Beat in the vanilla. Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt. Spread in the pan and bake 18 to 20 minutes, until springy. Cool.
Make the custard: heat the milk until steaming. Whisk the yolks, sugar and cornstarch in a bowl, then slowly whisk in the hot milk. Pour it back into the pan.

Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until it bubbles and thickens, then whisk 1 minute more. It will be well past 160°F, the temperature for egg dishes. Stir in the vanilla, press plastic wrap on the surface, and chill until cold.
Cut the sponge in 1-inch cubes. Toss half with half the jam and orange juice and pack it into the bowl. Add half the berries, then half the custard. Repeat.
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar to soft peaks and spread it on top. Chill at least 4 hours or overnight so the cake softens. Top with more berries to serve.
equipment: glass trifle bowl or large glass bowl

swaps.shortcut: Use a store-bought pound cake or ladyfingers instead of the sponge.
swaps.fruit: Use sliced peaches or mandarin oranges instead of berries.

items.title: Bûche de Noël (Yule Log Cake)
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice
items.body: A rolled chocolate sponge filled with whipped cream and frosted with chocolate ganache scored to look like bark. Paris pastry shops made the log famous in the late 1800s.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Line the pan with parchment and grease the paper.
Beat the yolks with half the sugar until thick and pale, 3 minutes; beat in the vanilla. In a clean bowl, beat the whites to soft peaks, then add the rest of the sugar and beat to firm, glossy peaks.
Sift the cocoa, flour and salt over the yolks and fold gently, then fold in the whites in three parts. Spread evenly in the pan.

Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until it springs back. Dust a towel with powdered sugar, turn the cake out onto it, peel off the paper, and roll the warm cake up in the towel from a short end. Cool rolled, about 1 hour. Rolling it warm keeps it from cracking later.
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla to firm peaks. Unroll the cake, spread the cream to within 1 inch of the edges, and roll it up again without the towel. Chill seam side down.
For the ganache, heat the cream until steaming and pour it over the chocolate. Wait 3 minutes, then stir smooth. Cool until thick enough to spread, about 30 minutes.

Cut a short diagonal piece off one end and set it against the side as a branch. Spread the ganache over everything and drag a fork through it to look like bark. Chill at least 1 hour. Dust with powdered sugar “snow” to serve.

swaps.mocha: Add 1 teaspoon instant coffee to the cream for the filling.

items.title: Christmas Morning Sausage Strata
items.subtitle: breakfast · 1 square
items.body: Bread, browned sausage, cheese and eggs assembled the night before. In the morning it goes straight into the oven while presents are opened.

ingredients.prep: bulk, or links removed from casings

steps: Cook the sausage in the skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Add the onion and pepper and cook until soft. Drain off the fat and cool 10 minutes.
Grease the dish. Layer half the bread, half the sausage mixture and half the cheese, then repeat.
Whisk the eggs, milk, mustard, salt and pepper and pour over everything. Press the bread down so it soaks. Cover and refrigerate overnight (8 to 24 hours).

In the morning, heat the oven to 350°F and let the dish stand while it heats. Uncover and bake 50 to 55 minutes, until puffed and golden and a knife in the center comes out clean. The center should read 160°F.
Let it stand 10 minutes before cutting.

swaps.meatless: Use 3 cups sautéed mushrooms and spinach instead of sausage.
swaps.ham: Use 2 cups diced leftover ham; it’s already cooked.

items.title: Béchamel Sauce
items.subtitle: side · ¼ cup (makes 2 cups)
items.body: Escoffier’s white sauce: milk thickened with a butter-and-flour roux and simmered with onion and bay. The base for mac and cheese, lasagna and creamed vegetables.

steps: Warm the milk with the onion and bay leaf in the small saucepan until it steams and small bubbles form at the edge. Turn off the heat and let it steep while you make the roux.
Melt the butter in the heavy saucepan over medium-low heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, whisking, 2 minutes. It should bubble and smell nutty but stay pale: this is Escoffier’s white roux.
Take the pan off the heat and let the roux cool for a minute. Lift out the onion and bay, then pour the hot milk into the roux a little at a time, whisking hard so no lumps form.
Bring it to a gentle boil, whisking, then turn the heat to low and simmer 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often and reaching into the corners, until it coats a spoon and no longer tastes floury.
Season with the salt, nutmeg and pepper. Strain it if any lumps remain. Press plastic wrap on the surface or dot it with butter so a skin doesn’t form.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed into ¼ cup of the cold milk instead of the roux; whisk it into the rest of the hot milk and simmer 2 minutes.
swaps.cheese_sauce: Off the heat, stir in 1 cup shredded cheddar or Gruyère-style cheese for a Mornay-style cheese sauce.

items.title: Chicken Velouté
items.subtitle: side · ¼ cup (makes 2 cups)
items.body: A silky sauce of good chicken stock thickened with a pale roux and skimmed as it simmers. Spoon it over chicken, fish or vegetables, or use it to start a pot pie.

ingredients.prep: more if the stock is unsalted

steps: Melt the butter in the saucepan over medium-low heat, whisk in the flour, and cook 3 to 4 minutes, whisking, until it turns the color of straw: a pale roux. Let it cool a few minutes.
Whisk in the cold stock a little at a time, then bring to a boil, whisking so it doesn’t catch on the bottom.
Add the mushrooms if using. Turn the heat down so the sauce bubbles on one side of the pan only, and simmer 25 minutes, skimming off the skin and foam that gather on the quiet side.
When it has reduced to about 2 cups and coats a spoon, strain it. Season with salt, nutmeg and pepper. Stir now and then as it cools so a skin doesn’t form.

swaps.gluten_free: Thicken with 2 tablespoons cornstarch stirred into ¼ cup cold stock instead of the roux; simmer 2 minutes.
swaps.meatless: Use vegetable stock for a vegetable velouté.

items.title: Espagnole and Demi-Glace (Brown Sauce)
items.subtitle: side · ¼ cup (makes 2 cups)
items.body: Escoffier’s brown sauce: brown stock, a browned roux, vegetables, bacon and tomato, simmered and skimmed. Reduce it with more stock and it becomes demi-glace, the base of steak sauces.

ingredients.prep: homemade brown stock is best, unsalted

steps: Cook the bacon in the saucepan over medium heat until it gives up its fat, about 4 minutes. Add the carrot, onion and celery and cook until golden, 8 to 10 minutes. This bacon-and-vegetable mix is Escoffier’s mirepoix.

Add the butter. When it melts, stir in the flour and keep stirring over medium-low heat 6 to 8 minutes, until the roux turns the brown of a paper bag and smells toasty. Don’t let it scorch; burnt roux is bitter.
Whisk in the stock a cup at a time, then the tomato paste, bay leaf, thyme and pepper. Bring to a boil, whisking.
Turn it down so it bubbles gently on one side of the pan. Simmer 1½ hours, skimming the foam and fat from the quiet side every 15 minutes, until it has reduced to about 2 cups and coats a spoon.
Strain, pressing on the vegetables. Taste; add salt only at the end, since it concentrates as it cooks. This is espagnole.

For demi-glace: simmer 1 cup of the espagnole with 1 cup more stock in the small saucepan until it is reduced by about half, 20 to 25 minutes, and is glossy and thick enough to coat a spoon. Escoffier finished his with a little sherry; we leave it out.

swaps.gluten_free: Skip the roux; thicken the strained sauce with 2 tablespoons cornstarch stirred into ¼ cup cold stock and simmer 2 minutes.
swaps.no_pork: Leave out the bacon and brown the vegetables in 1 tablespoon more butter; Escoffier did the same for meatless days, using mushroom trimmings instead.

items.title: Escoffier’s Tomato Sauce
items.subtitle: side · ½ cup (makes about 6 cups)
items.body: The French classic tomato sauce: bacon, carrot and onion, a little flour, tomatoes and stock, cooked slowly in the oven, then passed through a sieve. Smooth, rich and mild.

ingredients.prep: 28-oz cans, with juice, crushed by hand (or 5 lb ripe tomatoes, chopped)

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. In the pot over medium heat, cook the bacon in the butter until the fat runs, about 4 minutes.
Add the carrot, onion, bay leaf and thyme and cook, stirring, until soft, about 8 minutes. Sprinkle in the flour and stir 2 to 3 minutes, until it just begins to brown.
Stir in the tomatoes and stock, scraping the bottom, then the garlic, sugar, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil.
Cover and move the pot to the oven. Cook 1½ hours, stirring once halfway.
Take out the bay leaf. Pass the sauce through a food mill or press it through a sieve (or blend it smooth). Bring it back to a boil on the stove, stirring, and taste for salt.
equipment: heavy ovenproof pot with a lid (5 quarts)

swaps.gluten_free: Leave out the flour and cook the sauce uncovered for the last 30 minutes so it thickens by reducing.
swaps.meatless: Leave out the bacon, use 2 tablespoons butter or olive oil, and use vegetable broth.

items.title: Hollandaise Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 3 tablespoons
items.body: Egg yolks whisked over gentle heat until thick, then beaten with warm butter and lemon. Rich and tangy, for eggs Benedict, asparagus and fish.

steps: Simmer the vinegar, water and pepper in the small saucepan until only about 1 tablespoon is left. Let it cool a minute.
Bring an inch of water to a bare simmer in a saucepan. In the heatproof bowl, whisk the yolks with the vinegar reduction and 1 tablespoon cold water.

Set the bowl over the barely simmering water (it shouldn’t touch the water) and whisk constantly, lifting the bowl off the heat now and then, until the yolks are thick, pale and foamy and reach 160°F, 3 to 5 minutes. If they start to look grainy, lift the bowl off and keep whisking.
Off the heat, pour in the warm butter in a thin stream, whisking all the time, until the sauce is thick and smooth.
Whisk in the lemon juice, salt and cayenne. If it’s too thick, whisk in a teaspoon of warm water. Serve right away, or keep it in a warm (not hot) spot for up to 1 hour, whisking now and then.
equipment: heatproof bowl that sits over a saucepan

swaps.blender: Cook the yolks to 160°F as above, then pour them into a blender, and with it running pour in the hot butter.

items.title: Peach Melba
items.subtitle: snack · 1 peach with ice cream and sauce
items.body: Escoffier’s famous dessert: peaches poached in vanilla syrup, served on vanilla ice cream under a fresh raspberry purée.

steps: Bring the water and sugar to a boil in the saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the vanilla.

Lower the peaches into the syrup and simmer gently 5 to 8 minutes, turning them, until a knife slides in easily. Lift them out, let them cool a few minutes, and slip off the skins. Halve and pit them.
Cool the peaches in a little of the syrup, then chill at least 1 hour. (Save the rest of the syrup for iced tea or fruit salad.)
For the sauce, purée the raspberries with the powdered sugar and lemon juice, then press through a sieve to remove the seeds. Chill.
To serve, put a scoop of ice cream in each bowl, set two peach halves on top, and spoon the raspberry sauce over.
equipment: saucepan wide enough for the peaches

swaps.shortcut: Out of season, use canned peach halves in juice, drained, and skip the poaching.

meta.servings: 1 peach with ice cream and sauce

items.title: Pears Belle-Hélène
items.subtitle: snack · 1 pear with ice cream and sauce
items.body: Pears poached in vanilla syrup, chilled, and served on vanilla ice cream with hot chocolate sauce poured over at the table.

steps: Bring the water, sugar and lemon juice to a boil in the saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Add the vanilla.
Peel the pears, leaving the stems on. Scoop out the cores from the bottom with the melon baller.
Simmer the pears in the syrup, turning now and then, 15 to 25 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Let them cool in the syrup, then chill at least 1 hour.
Just before serving, heat the cream in the small saucepan until it steams, take it off the heat, add the chocolate, and stir until smooth.
Set each pear on a scoop of ice cream and pour the warm chocolate sauce over it.
equipment: saucepan that holds the pears upright or on their sides

swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut milk in the sauce and a dairy-free frozen dessert.

meta.servings: 1 pear with ice cream and sauce

items.title: Crêpes Suzette
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 3 crêpes
items.body: Thin crêpes warmed in a buttery orange sauce. Escoffier’s 1907 version brushes them with orange butter; ours makes it a glossy pan sauce, with no liqueur and no flames.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus a little for the pan
or the juice of clementines or tangerines

steps: Blend or whisk the flour, eggs, milk, melted butter, sugar and salt until smooth. Rest the batter 30 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).

Heat the 8-inch skillet over medium and brush it with butter. Pour in 3 tablespoons of batter and swirl to coat the pan thinly. Cook about 1 minute, until the edges lift and the bottom is lightly browned, then flip and cook 20 seconds. Stack the crêpes on a plate. You’ll have about 12.
For the sauce, mash the soft butter with the sugar and orange zest. Melt it in the large skillet over medium heat, add the orange and lemon juice, and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until slightly syrupy.
Fold each crêpe in quarters, lay them in the sauce, and spoon it over. Warm 1 to 2 minutes, turning once, and serve with the sauce.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk in the batter and a dairy-free butter in the pan and the sauce.

items.title: Melba Toast
items.subtitle: snack,side · 4 crisp halves
items.body: Toast split into paper-thin slices and baked until crisp and curled. A light partner for soup, pâté or cheese.

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Toast the bread lightly in the toaster.
While it’s warm, cut off the crusts. Lay a slice flat and, holding it with your palm, slice it in half through the middle with a serrated knife to make two thin slices.
Lay the slices on the baking sheet, untoasted side up. Bake 8 to 12 minutes, until dry, golden and curling at the edges. Watch the last few minutes; they brown fast.
Cool completely; they crisp as they cool.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free sandwich bread; it splits more easily when cold.

items.title: Potato and Leek Soup (Potage Parmentier)
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1⅓ cups
items.body: Leeks softened in butter, simmered with potatoes and stock, puréed and finished with cream. Escoffier topped it with butter-fried croutons.

ingredients.prep: white and light green parts, sliced and well rinsed

steps: Melt the butter in the pot over medium-low heat. Cook the leeks, stirring, until soft but not browned, about 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes, broth and water. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart when poked.
Purée the soup in the pot with an immersion blender, or in batches in a blender with the lid vented and covered with a towel (hot liquid expands). For a rustic soup, mash it instead.
Stir in the cream, bring just back to a simmer, and season with salt and pepper.
For the croutons, fry the bread cubes in the butter in the skillet, stirring, until golden, 4 to 5 minutes. Serve the soup topped with croutons and chives.
equipment: blender, immersion blender or potato masher

swaps.escoffier_style: Use chicken broth, closer to the white consommé Escoffier used.
swaps.gluten_free: Leave off the croutons or use gluten-free bread.
swaps.cold_soup: Chill it, thin with a little more cream or milk, and serve cold with chives. Served cold this way, it is close to vichyssoise.

items.title: Hunter’s Chicken (Chicken Chasseur)
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 thighs with sauce
items.body: Chicken browned in butter and oil, then finished in a sauce of mushrooms, shallots, tomato and parsley. A classic French bistro dinner.

steps: Pat the chicken dry and season with the salt and pepper. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Heat the oil and butter in the skillet over medium-high. Brown the chicken skin side down, 6 to 8 minutes, then turn and brown 3 minutes more. Move it to a plate.
Pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat. Cook the mushrooms over medium-high until browned, about 6 minutes. Add the shallots and cook 1 minute, then stir in the flour.
Stir in the broth, tomato paste and lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits. Return the chicken, skin side up, with its juices.
Cover and simmer gently 20 to 25 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest thigh (not touching bone) reads 165°F. Move the chicken to a platter.
Simmer the sauce 2 to 3 minutes to thicken, then swirl in the last tablespoon of butter and the parsley. Spoon over the chicken.
equipment: large heavy skillet with a lid

swaps.gluten_free: Leave out the flour and simmer the sauce a few minutes longer to thicken.
swaps.dairy_free: Use all olive oil instead of butter.

items.title: Fish Bonne Femme
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 fillet with sauce
items.body: White fish fillets poached on a bed of shallots and mushrooms, then coated with the pan juices made into a creamy sauce. Escoffier’s “good wife’s” sole, for any mild white fish.

ingredients.prep: about 6 oz each, or sole, flounder or tilapia

steps: Butter the skillet with 1 tablespoon of the butter and scatter the shallots, mushrooms and half the parsley over the bottom.
Season the fish with the salt and pepper and lay it on the vegetables. Pour in the broth and lemon juice.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, cover, and poach gently 6 to 10 minutes, until the fish flakes and reaches 145°F in the thickest part. Lift the fish to warm plates with the spatula.
Turn the heat to high and boil the pan juices and mushrooms until reduced by half, about 4 minutes. Add the cream and boil 2 minutes more, until it coats a spoon. Swirl in the rest of the butter.
Spoon the sauce over the fish and sprinkle with the rest of the parsley.

swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the cream and finish the sauce with 1 tablespoon olive oil.
swaps.glazed_top: For Escoffier’s finish, set the plates under a hot broiler for a minute to glaze the sauce.

items.title: Lobster Newberg
items.subtitle: dinner · about ¾ cup on toast
items.body: Cooked lobster warmed in butter, simmered in cream, and thickened with egg yolks and a pinch of cayenne. Delmonico’s showpiece, served on toast.

ingredients.prep: toasted and cut in triangles, or 2 cups cooked rice

steps: Melt the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Add the lobster and warm it gently 2 minutes, turning, without letting it brown.
Pour in 1¼ cups of the cream and simmer until it has reduced by about a third, 5 to 6 minutes.
Whisk the yolks with the remaining ¼ cup cream in the bowl. Whisk a ladle of the hot cream into the yolks, then pour it all back into the pan.
Stir over low heat without letting it boil, until the sauce thickens and reaches 160°F, 2 to 3 minutes. Season with salt, cayenne, paprika and lemon juice.
Spoon over the toast and serve right away.

swaps.shrimp: Use 1 lb cooked, peeled shrimp, or a mix of shrimp and scallops seared through first.
swaps.gluten_free: Serve over rice instead of toast.

items.title: Eggs Benedict
items.subtitle: breakfast · 2 halves
items.body: Toasted English muffins topped with ham, a poached egg and hollandaise. Delmonico’s chef printed it in 1894 as “Eggs à la Benedick.”

ingredients.prep: thick-sliced cooked ham or Canadian bacon

steps: Make the hollandaise: in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water, whisk the yolks, lemon juice and 1 tablespoon water constantly until thick and foamy and they reach 160°F. Off the heat, whisk in the warm butter in a thin stream, then the salt and cayenne. Keep it in a warm spot.
Heat the oven to 200°F. Toast the muffin halves lightly, top each with ham, and keep them warm on the baking sheet in the oven.

Bring 3 inches of water and the vinegar to a gentle simmer in the deep skillet. Crack each egg into a cup and slide it in. Poach 4 to 5 minutes, until the whites are completely set and the yolks have begun to thicken. USDA advises cooking eggs until both the yolk and white are firm; for runny yolks, use pasteurized eggs.
Lift the eggs out with the slotted spoon, drain them on a towel, and set one on each muffin. Spoon hollandaise over and serve.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free English muffins.
swaps.meatless: Use sautéed spinach or sliced tomato instead of ham (eggs Florentine).

items.title: Baked Alaska
items.subtitle: snack · 1 wedge
items.body: Ice cream on sponge cake, sealed in meringue and browned in a very hot oven for just a few minutes. Delmonico’s “Alaska, Florida”: cold inside, warm outside.

ingredients.prep: from pasteurized eggs, or carton whites labeled for whipping

steps: Line the bowl with plastic wrap. Soften the ice cream a few minutes, pack it into the bowl, cover, and freeze until very firm, at least 4 hours.

Heat the oven to 350°F and line the cake pan with parchment. Beat the eggs, sugar and vanilla on high 5 to 7 minutes, until thick, pale and tripled. Sift the flour and salt over and fold in gently. Spread in the pan and bake 15 to 18 minutes, until springy. Cool completely.
Set the cake on the ovenproof platter and brush it with the jam. Unmold the ice cream dome onto the cake and peel off the plastic. Return to the freezer.
Heat the oven to 475°F. Beat the egg whites and cream of tartar to soft peaks, then beat in the sugar a spoonful at a time and keep beating to stiff, glossy peaks.
Spread the meringue over the ice cream and cake right down to the platter, sealing it completely; swirl the top. (You can freeze it now, up to 1 day.)
Bake 3 to 5 minutes, until the peaks are golden brown, or brown it with a torch. Slice with a hot knife and serve at once.

swaps.shortcut: Use a store-bought pound cake, sliced ½ inch thick, in place of the sponge.

items.title: Delmonico Steak with Parsley Butter
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 oz of steak
items.body: A thick sirloin steak, salted, brushed with butter and broiled, served with lemony parsley butter. Ranhofer’s plain steak, the way Delmonico’s served it.

steps: Mash the butter with the parsley, lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Shape into a log on plastic wrap and chill.
Pat the steaks dry, season both sides with the salt and pepper, and brush with the oil. Let them sit while the broiler, grill or skillet heats.
Broil 3 to 4 inches from the heat, or cook on a hot grill or skillet, 5 to 7 minutes per side, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 145°F.
Rest the steaks 3 minutes, then slice and top with coins of the parsley butter.
equipment: broiler pan, grill or heavy skillet

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the parsley butter and serve with lemon and olive oil.

items.title: The Original Waldorf Salad (1896)
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about ¾ cup
items.body: The Waldorf’s first version: just apples and celery in mayonnaise. Walnuts and grapes came later.

ingredients.prep: crisp and tart-sweet, peeled and cored

steps: Cut the apples into ½-inch cubes and toss them with the lemon juice so they don’t brown. Check that no seeds or core are left.
Cut the celery into pieces about the same size.
Fold the apples, celery and salt into the mayonnaise. Serve right away on lettuce leaves, or chill up to 2 hours.

swaps.walnuts_and_grapes: Add ½ cup toasted walnuts and a handful of halved grapes for the salad most people know today.

items.title: Celery Victor
items.subtitle: side · about 4 oz of celery
items.body: Celery hearts simmered in stock, cooled in it, and dressed with oil, vinegar and herbs. A cool, savory salad from San Francisco’s Hotel St. Francis.

ingredients.prep: the pale inner stalks (hearts) of 2 bunches, halved lengthwise
or chicken broth, closer to the original

steps: Trim the celery hearts so they lie flat, leaving the base on to hold the stalks together. Lay them in the pan and pour in the broth.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently 15 to 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Let the celery cool in the broth, then chill at least 1 hour.
Lift the celery out and press it gently to squeeze out the broth (save the broth for soup). Lay it on plates.
Shake the oil, vinegar, salt and pepper together, spoon over the celery, and scatter with the parsley and chives.
equipment: wide saucepan or skillet with a lid

swaps.original_flavor: Simmer the celery in chicken broth, as Hirtzler did with his hen-and-veal stock.

items.title: Delmonico Potatoes
items.subtitle: side · about ⅔ cup
items.body: Diced potatoes simmered in cream, topped with Parmesan and baked until golden. The St. Francis version of a Delmonico’s favorite.

ingredients.prep: or 1 cup cream and ½ cup milk

steps: Boil the whole potatoes in salted water until just tender, 20 to 25 minutes. Drain, cool until you can handle them, and cut into ¼-inch dice.
Heat the oven to 400°F and butter the baking dish.

Simmer the half-and-half with the butter, salt, pepper and nutmeg in the skillet. Add the potatoes and simmer, stirring gently, until the cream thickens and coats them, 5 to 8 minutes. (This is “hashed in cream” potatoes.)
Spread in the dish, sprinkle with the Parmesan, and bake 15 to 20 minutes, until bubbling and golden brown.

items.title: Grilled Hot Dogs with All the Toppings
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 hot dog in a bun, with toppings
items.body: Hot dogs grilled until they blister, in toasted buns, with a toppings bar so everyone builds their own: mustard, ketchup, relish, onions, sauerkraut and cheese.

steps: Heat the grill to medium. Set out the toppings in small bowls; keep the sauerkraut warm and the cheese cold until serving.

Grill the hot dogs, turning every minute or two with tongs, for 6 to 8 minutes, until they are browned and heated through. Hot dogs are already cooked, but USDA advises reheating them until steaming hot, 165°F in the center.
Lay the buns cut side down on the edge of the grill for 30 to 60 seconds to toast.
Take the cooked food off the grill onto a clean platter, not the one that held it raw (USDA). Tuck each hot dog into a bun and let everyone add toppings.
Cut hot dogs lengthwise and then into small pieces for young children, since round slices are a choking risk.

swaps.turkey_or_chicken: Use turkey or chicken hot dogs; grill them the same way.
swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns and check the hot dog label.
swaps.vegetarian: Grill plant-based hot dogs per the package.

meta.servings: 1 hot dog in a bun, with toppings

items.title: Grilled Barbecue Chicken
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 pieces
items.body: Bone-in thighs and drumsticks cooked over gentle heat until tender, then brushed with barbecue sauce at the end so it turns sticky instead of burning.

steps: Set up the grill for two zones: on a gas grill, one side on medium and the other side off or on low; with charcoal, push the hot coals to one side. You want about 350 to 400°F under the lid.
Pat the chicken dry. Mix the rub, toss the chicken with the oil, then with the rub. Wash your hands and anything the raw chicken touched.
Brown the chicken skin side down over the hotter side, 2 to 3 minutes, watching for flare-ups. Move it to the cooler side, close the lid and cook 25 to 35 minutes, turning once or twice.

Pour about half the sauce into a small bowl for brushing; keep the rest clean for the table. Brush the chicken in the last 10 minutes, turning and brushing two or three times. Sugar in the sauce burns fast, so keep it on the cooler side.
Check with a food thermometer in the thickest part, not touching bone: the chicken is safe at 165°F (USDA). Dark meat gets more tender if you take it a little further, to about 175°F.
Take the cooked food off the grill onto a clean platter, not the one that held it raw (USDA). Cook it all the way through in one go: never partly grill meat or poultry to finish later (USDA).

swaps.oven: Bake at 400°F on a rack over a foil-lined pan for 40 to 45 minutes, brushing with sauce for the last 10, until 165°F.
swaps.boneless: Use boneless thighs; grill them over direct medium heat 5 to 6 minutes per side before saucing.

items.title: Lemon-Herb Grilled Chicken Breasts
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 breast half (about 5 oz cooked)
items.body: Chicken breasts pounded to an even thickness and marinated in lemon, garlic, oregano and olive oil, so they grill fast and stay juicy. Good hot, or sliced cold onto salads.

steps: Put the chicken between sheets of plastic wrap and pound the thick ends until the pieces are an even ¾ inch. Wash your hands and the work surface.
