Whisk the marinade in a bag or dish, add the chicken and turn to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator, never on the counter. Throw out the used marinade, or boil it first if you want to brush it on cooked food (USDA). Marinate 1 to 4 hours; longer and the lemon makes the meat mushy.
Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates. Lift the chicken out of the marinade and throw the marinade away.
Grill 5 to 6 minutes per side, without moving it until it releases easily, until a food thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F (USDA).
Take the cooked food off the grill onto a clean platter, not the one that held it raw (USDA). Rest 5 minutes, slice, and sprinkle with parsley.

swaps.thighs: Boneless thighs stay juicier and need no pounding; grill 5 to 7 minutes per side to 165°F.
swaps.herbs: Use 2 tablespoons fresh oregano or thyme instead of dried.

items.title: Grill-Smoked Baby Back Ribs
items.subtitle: dinner · about ⅓ rack
items.body: Two racks of ribs cooked low and slow beside the fire, not over it, then wrapped to turn tender and brushed with sauce at the end. A cookout afternoon project.

steps: Pat the ribs dry. On the bone side, slide a butter knife under the thin membrane at one end, grab it with a paper towel and pull it off. Mix the rub and pat it over both sides. Wash your hands.

Set up the grill for indirect heat at 250 to 275°F: on a gas grill, light one side on low and leave the other off; with charcoal, bank a small fire on one side. Add a pan of water under the cool side if you like, which helps keep the heat steady.
Lay the ribs bone side down on the cool side, close the lid and cook 2 hours. Check the lid temperature now and then and adjust the burner or add a few coals to stay near 250 to 275°F.
Wrap each rack in a double layer of foil with 2 tablespoons of apple juice, and return to the cool side for 45 minutes to 1 hour, until a toothpick slides between the bones easily.
Unwrap the ribs (careful of steam), brush with sauce and cook uncovered on the cool side 15 to 20 minutes more, brushing once or twice, until sticky.

Pork is safe at 145°F with a 3-minute rest (USDA); ribs are cooked far past that to become tender, and the meat pulls back from the bone ends. Take the cooked food off the grill onto a clean platter, not the one that held it raw (USDA). Rest 5 minutes and cut between the bones.
equipment: grill with a lid (gas or charcoal)
grill thermometer, or the lid gauge

swaps.oven: No grill time? Use our oven baby back ribs and finish them on the grill for 10 minutes.
swaps.spare_ribs: Spare ribs are bigger: add about an hour in step 3.

items.title: Grilled Vegetable Skewers
items.subtitle: side,dinner · 2 skewers
items.body: Zucchini, peppers, red onion, mushrooms and cherry tomatoes tossed in garlic and herbs and grilled until charred at the edges. A side for everyone, and a main for vegetarians.

steps: Whisk the dressing in a large bowl. Add the vegetables and toss to coat. Let them sit 15 minutes, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Thread the vegetables onto the skewers, mixing colors. Put tomatoes on their own skewers if you like, since they cook faster.
Heat the grill to medium-high and oil the grates. Grill the skewers 10 to 12 minutes, turning every few minutes, until tender and charred in spots; tomato skewers need only 4 to 5 minutes.
Brush with any dressing left in the bowl and serve hot or at room temperature.
equipment: 12 skewers (soak wooden ones in water 30 minutes)

swaps.halloumi_or_tofu: Add cubes of firm tofu or halloumi for protein.
swaps.no_skewers: Use a grill basket and toss the vegetables now and then.

items.title: Classic Mustard Potato Salad
items.subtitle: side · about ⅔ cup
items.body: The yellow, old-fashioned kind: tender potatoes dressed while warm with vinegar, then mixed with mayonnaise, mustard, pickles, celery, onion and chopped egg.

ingredients.prep: for the cooking water (most drains away)

steps: Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water by an inch and add the salt. Bring to a boil and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, until a knife slides in easily but they still hold their shape. Drain well, spread in a large bowl and sprinkle with the vinegar while warm.
Meanwhile, cover the eggs with water in a small pot, bring to a boil, cover, take off the heat and let stand 12 minutes. Cool in ice water, peel and chop.
Stir the mayonnaise, mustard, relish, celery, onion, salt and pepper together. When the potatoes are no longer steaming, fold in the dressing and eggs gently.

Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, until cold. Dust with paprika before serving. Keep it cold until serving: 40°F or below in the refrigerator or a cooler with plenty of ice. Put it away within 2 hours of setting it out, or within 1 hour if it’s above 90°F outside (USDA).

swaps.no_egg: Leave out the eggs and use an egg-free mayonnaise for egg allergies.
swaps.red_potatoes: Use red potatoes with the skins on; no peeling needed.

items.title: Picnic Macaroni Salad
items.subtitle: side · about ⅔ cup
items.body: Elbow macaroni in a creamy, tangy dressing with crunchy celery, bell pepper and a little sweet pickle. A cookout classic kids reach for.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most drains away)

steps: Cook the macaroni in boiling salted water 1 minute past the package time, so it stays tender when cold. Drain, rinse with cold water until cool, and drain well.
Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, mustard, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the macaroni, celery, pepper, onion and relish and stir well. The pasta drinks up dressing as it sits, so it will thicken.

Refrigerate at least 1 hour. Stir in a splash of milk or a spoonful of mayonnaise before serving if it seems dry. Keep it cold until serving: 40°F or below in the refrigerator or a cooler with plenty of ice. Put it away within 2 hours of setting it out, or within 1 hour if it’s above 90°F outside (USDA).

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free elbow pasta, cooked just to the package time.

items.title: Homemade Baked Beans with Bacon
items.subtitle: side · about ½ cup
items.body: Navy beans baked slowly with bacon, onion, molasses, brown sugar and mustard until the sauce turns thick and glossy. Made from canned beans, so no overnight soak.

ingredients.prep: navy or great northern, 15 oz each, drained and rinsed

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F.

Cook the bacon in an oven-safe pot or skillet over medium heat until it starts to crisp, about 6 minutes. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes, until soft. Spoon off all but about a tablespoon of the fat.
Stir in the ketchup, molasses, brown sugar, mustard, vinegar, Worcestershire, pepper and water, then the beans. Bring to a simmer. (Pour into a baking dish now if your pot can’t go in the oven.)
Bake uncovered 1 hour, stirring once or twice, until the sauce is thick and bubbling at the edges. It thickens more as it cools a little. Taste for salt; the bacon adds plenty.

swaps.vegetarian: Skip the bacon, cook the onion in 2 tablespoons oil, and add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika.
swaps.slow_cooker: After step 3, cook in a slow cooker on low 4 to 5 hours.

items.title: Tangy Vinegar Coleslaw
items.subtitle: side · about ¾ cup
items.body: A crunchy, mayonnaise-free slaw dressed with cider vinegar, a little sugar and celery seed. It holds up better than creamy slaw on a hot day and belongs on a pulled pork sandwich.

ingredients.prep: about 2 lb, cored and thinly sliced, or 2 bags coleslaw mix

steps: Warm the vinegar and sugar just until the sugar dissolves (a minute in the microwave). Whisk in the oil, salt, celery seed and pepper.
Toss the cabbage, carrots and onion with the dressing in a large bowl.
Refrigerate at least 1 hour, tossing once or twice. The cabbage softens a little and gives off liquid; toss again and serve with a slotted spoon.

items.title: Grilled Street-Style Corn
items.subtitle: side · 1 ear
items.body: Corn grilled until charred, then coated with a creamy lime sauce, crumbled cheese and chili powder, in the style of Mexican elote sold by street vendors.

steps: Heat the grill to medium-high. Stir the mayonnaise, sour cream, lime zest and 1 tablespoon lime juice together.
Grill the corn 10 to 12 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until tender and charred in spots.
While hot, brush or spoon the sauce over each ear, roll or sprinkle with the cheese, and dust with chili powder and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

swaps.off_the_cob: Grill, cut the kernels off, and toss with the sauce in a bowl for an easy-to-serve salad.
swaps.no_egg: Use all sour cream or plain yogurt instead of mayonnaise.

items.title: Homemade Barbecue Sauce
items.subtitle: side · 2 tablespoons (makes about 2 cups)
items.body: A sweet, tangy, lightly smoky sauce from ketchup, molasses, vinegar and spices. Twenty minutes on the stove, and it keeps for weeks.

steps: Whisk everything in a small saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Lower the heat and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, stirring often (it spatters), until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Cool and pour into a clean jar. Keep a separate small bowl for brushing raw or cooking meat, so the jar stays clean.

swaps.fish_free: Worcestershire usually contains anchovies; use soy sauce for a fish-free sauce.
swaps.spicier: Add the cayenne and a few dashes of hot sauce.

items.title: Fresh-Squeezed Lemonade
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cup
items.body: Real lemons, sugar dissolved into a quick syrup so it never sits gritty at the bottom, and cold water. Easy to make less sweet, or pink with berries.

ingredients.prep: juiced, for about 1½ cups juice (or 1½ cups bottled lemon juice)

steps: Heat the sugar and 1 cup water, stirring, just until the sugar dissolves. Let the syrup cool.
Roll the lemons on the counter, cut them in half and squeeze; strain out the seeds.
Stir the syrup, lemon juice and cold water together in a pitcher. Taste and add more water if it’s too tart or sweet. Chill and serve over ice with lemon slices.

swaps.pink: Blend 1 cup strawberries or raspberries with a little of the water, strain, and stir it in.

items.title: Flag Sheet Cake with Berries
items.subtitle: snack · 1 piece (1/20 of a 9x13 cake)
items.body: A tender vanilla sheet cake spread with a light cream cheese whipped frosting, with blueberries in the corner and rows of raspberries or strawberries for stripes.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter and flour the pan.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt. In a large bowl, beat the butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Mix in the flour in three parts, alternating with the milk, just until smooth. Spread in the pan.
Bake 28 to 32 minutes, until golden and a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool completely in the pan, at least an hour.
Beat the cream cheese, powdered sugar and vanilla until smooth. In another bowl whip the cream to stiff peaks, then fold it into the cream cheese. Spread over the cooled cake.
Make the flag: a rectangle of blueberries in the top left corner, and rows of raspberries or strawberries across for stripes, leaving white frosting between them.
Refrigerate until serving; the frosting is made with cream and cream cheese, so put leftovers back in the refrigerator within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F).

swaps.cupcakes: Bake 24 cupcakes, 18 to 20 minutes, and top each with a swirl of frosting and a few berries.
swaps.quicker: Frost with plain whipped cream from scratch; serve the same day.

items.title: Strawberry Shortcakes
items.subtitle: snack · 1 shortcake with berries and cream
items.body: Tender, lightly sweet biscuits split and piled with juicy sugared strawberries and softly whipped cream. A summer dessert that tastes best the day you make it.

steps: Toss the strawberries with the sugar and let them sit 30 minutes, stirring once, to make their own syrup.

Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet. Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Cut in the butter with a pastry cutter or your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with some pea-size bits.
Whisk the ¾ cup cream with the egg and stir it in with a fork just until the dough comes together. Pat it out ¾ inch thick on a floured counter and cut 8 rounds, pressing scraps together once.
Set them on the sheet, brush the tops with cream and sprinkle with a little sugar. Bake 13 to 16 minutes, until golden. Cool 10 minutes.
Whip the cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla to soft peaks.
Split each shortcake, spoon berries and their syrup over the bottom, add cream, and set the top on.

swaps.other_berries: Use a mix of strawberries, blueberries and raspberries for red, white and blue with the cream.
swaps.buttermilk: Use our from-scratch biscuits instead, with 2 tablespoons sugar added.

items.title: Red, White and Blue Yogurt Parfaits
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 parfait (about 1 cup)
items.body: Layers of vanilla yogurt, strawberries, blueberries and crunchy granola in clear cups. No oven, and kids can make them.

ingredients.prep: or plain Greek yogurt with honey

steps: Spoon a layer of yogurt into each cup, then strawberries, then more yogurt, then blueberries.
Top with granola right before serving so it stays crunchy, and drizzle with honey if you like.
Keep the parfaits in the refrigerator or a cooler on ice until serving.

swaps.nut_free: Check the granola label; many contain nuts. Use crushed graham crackers or toasted oats instead.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a coconut or soy yogurt.

items.title: Sweet Noodle Kugel
items.subtitle: side,breakfast · 1 square (about 3 by 3 inches)
items.body: A Jewish holiday favorite: egg noodles baked in a sweet, creamy custard of cottage cheese, sour cream and cream cheese with a cinnamon top.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the dish

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and butter the baking dish. Cook the noodles in boiling salted water 2 minutes less than the package time. Drain.
In a large bowl, whisk the cream cheese, butter and sugar until smooth. Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the cottage cheese, sour cream, milk, vanilla and salt.
Fold in the noodles and raisins. Spread in the dish. Mix the topping sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over.
Bake 55 to 60 minutes, until set in the center, golden on top and 160°F inside. Cool 15 minutes before cutting.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free wide noodles.

items.title: Hot Spinach Artichoke Dip
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/3 cup
items.body: A bubbly, cheesy dip of spinach, artichoke hearts, cream cheese, sour cream, mozzarella and Parmesan.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Stir the cream cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise, garlic, pepper and pepper flakes until smooth. Fold in the spinach, artichokes, 3/4 cup mozzarella and the Parmesan.
Spread in the baking dish and top with the remaining mozzarella.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and lightly browned. Serve hot with chips, crackers or vegetables.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with vegetables or corn chips.

items.title: Crustless Spinach and Feta Pie
items.subtitle: breakfast,lunch,dinner · 1 wedge
items.body: The flavors of Greek spanakopita (spinach, feta, dill and green onions) baked in an easy egg and cottage cheese custard with no crust.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and oil the pie dish.
Whisk the eggs in a large bowl. Stir in the cottage cheese, feta, green onions, dill, parsley, Parmesan, pepper and nutmeg, then the spinach. (Feta is salty, so no salt is added.)
Spread in the dish. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until puffed, golden at the edges and set in the center (160°F). Cool 10 minutes before slicing.

swaps.gluten_free: Already gluten-free.

items.title: Cottage Cheese Pancakes
items.subtitle: breakfast · 3 small pancakes
items.body: Tender, high-protein pancakes made with cottage cheese and eggs. Blend the batter smooth or leave it a little lumpy.

steps: Blend or whisk the cottage cheese, eggs, milk, sugar and vanilla. Stir in the flour, baking powder and salt just until mixed.

Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat and brush with butter. Pour scant 1/4 cups of batter. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, until the bottoms are golden and the edges look set, then flip and cook 2 minutes more, until cooked through.
Serve with fruit and syrup.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.

items.title: Lazy Pierogi (Cottage Cheese Dumplings)
items.subtitle: dinner,breakfast · about 12 dumplings
items.body: A Polish family favorite: soft dumplings of cottage cheese, egg and flour, boiled and tossed with butter. Serve them sweet with cinnamon sugar or savory with onions.

steps: Mash the cottage cheese with a fork until the curds are small. Stir in the eggs, salt and sugar, then the flour, until a soft, sticky dough forms.
Divide the dough in 4. On a well-floured counter, roll each piece into a rope about 1 inch thick, then press it slightly flat and cut on an angle into 1-inch pieces.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the dumplings in 2 batches: once they float, cook 2 minutes more, until puffed and cooked through. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Toss with melted butter and sprinkle with the cinnamon and sugar. Serve with sour cream if you like.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend; the dough will be softer.

items.title: Creamy Cottage Cheese Dill Dip
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/4 cup
items.body: Cottage cheese blended smooth with fresh dill, chives and lemon. A high-protein dip for vegetables and crackers.

steps: Blend the cottage cheese and lemon juice until smooth and creamy, about 1 minute.
Add the dill, chives, garlic, salt and pepper and pulse a few times.
Chill 30 minutes so the flavors blend. Serve with vegetables or crackers.

items.title: Spinach Lasagna Roll-Ups
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 roll-ups
items.body: Lasagna noodles rolled around a ricotta, spinach and basil filling and baked in marinara under melted mozzarella. Easy to portion.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the noodles in boiling salted water by the package directions. Drain and lay flat on oiled foil so they do not stick.
Mix the ricotta, spinach, egg, Parmesan, basil, garlic, salt and pepper.
Spread 1 cup marinara in the baking dish. Spread about 3 tablespoons filling along each noodle and roll it up. Set them seam side down in the dish.
Spoon the rest of the sauce over and sprinkle with mozzarella. Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 minutes more, until bubbling and 165°F in the center.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free lasagna noodles.

items.title: Lemon Ricotta Pancakes
items.subtitle: breakfast · 3 pancakes
items.body: Light, moist pancakes with ricotta and fresh lemon zest. Special enough for a weekend, easy enough for a weekday.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the pan

steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl whisk the ricotta, milk, eggs, melted butter, lemon zest, lemon juice and vanilla. Fold into the dry ingredients just until mixed; the batter will be thick.
Heat a griddle over medium heat and brush with butter. Cook 1/4-cup scoops 2 to 3 minutes, until golden underneath and set at the edges. Flip and cook 2 minutes more.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.

items.title: Spinach and Ricotta Calzones
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 calzone
items.body: Store-bought pizza dough folded around ricotta, mozzarella, spinach and Parmesan, baked golden and served with marinara for dipping.

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and line the baking sheets with parchment. Mix the ricotta, mozzarella, Parmesan, spinach, garlic and Italian seasoning.
Cut the dough into 4 pieces. On a floured counter, roll each into an 8-inch circle.
Spoon a quarter of the filling onto half of each circle, leaving a 1-inch border. Fold over, press the edges and crimp with a fork. Cut 2 small slits in the top and brush with oil.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until deep golden. Cool 5 minutes (the filling is very hot) and serve with marinara.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free pizza dough.

items.title: Broccoli Alfredo Penne
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Penne and broccoli in a homemade Alfredo sauce of cream, butter, garlic and Parmesan. Add leftover chicken if you like.

steps: Cook the penne in a large pot of boiling salted water by the package directions. Add the broccoli for the last 3 minutes. Save 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic for 1 minute. Add the cream and simmer gently 4 to 5 minutes, until slightly thick.
Lower the heat and whisk in the Parmesan a handful at a time until smooth. Add the salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Toss the pasta, broccoli and chicken in the sauce, adding pasta water a splash at a time until creamy. If using chicken, heat until it reaches 165°F.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta.

items.title: Classic Cream Scones
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 scone
items.body: Tender, lightly sweet scones made with heavy cream. Add dried fruit or chocolate chips if you like.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs with a few pea-size pieces.
Stir in the cream, vanilla and dried fruit with a fork just until a shaggy dough forms. Turn out and gently pat into an 8-inch circle about 3/4 inch thick.
Cut into 8 wedges, set them on the sheet and brush with cream. Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until golden. Cool 10 minutes.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum.

items.title: Flaky Buttermilk Biscuits
items.subtitle: breakfast,side · 1 biscuit
items.body: Tall, tender Southern-style biscuits from flour, cold butter and buttermilk. Fold the dough a few times for flaky layers.

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F. Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and sugar in a large bowl.
Cut in the cold butter until it is the size of peas. Stir in the buttermilk with a fork just until the dough comes together.
Turn out onto a floured counter and pat into a rectangle. Fold it in thirds like a letter, pat it out again and repeat twice. Pat to 3/4 inch thick.
Cut biscuits straight down without twisting and set them touching on the baking sheet. Re-pat the scraps once. Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until golden. Brush with melted butter.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend made for biscuits.

items.title: Mini Cheesecakes
items.subtitle: snack · 1 mini cheesecake
items.body: Little cheesecakes with a graham cracker crust baked in a muffin tin. Top them with fresh berries.

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F and line a muffin tin with paper liners. Mix the cracker crumbs, butter and sugar and press about 1 tablespoon into each liner.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar until smooth. Beat in the eggs one at a time on low, then the sour cream, vanilla and lemon juice. Do not overbeat.
Divide the filling among the cups. Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until the edges are set and the centers just jiggle (they reach 160°F).
Cool in the pan 30 minutes, then refrigerate at least 2 hours. Top with berries.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free graham crackers or skip the crust.

items.title: Honey-Orange Glazed Bone-In Ham
items.subtitle: dinner · about ⅓ lb as bought (with bone)
items.body: A fully cooked bone-in half ham, scored in diamonds, warmed slowly at 325°F and lacquered with honey, orange and mustard. The bone goes into soup afterward.

ingredients.prep: fully cooked half ham (shank or butt end)

steps: Read the label. This recipe is for a fully cooked ham. A ham labeled “cook before eating” must reach 145°F and rest 3 minutes; it takes 22 to 25 minutes per pound for a half ham (USDA).
Heat the oven to 325°F. Trim the skin off if there is any, leaving a ¼-inch layer of fat. Score the fat in a diamond pattern, ¼ inch deep.
Set the ham cut side down on the rack in the pan, pour the water into the pan, and cover the ham loosely with foil so it doesn’t dry out.

Bake. USDA’s guide for a fully cooked bone-in half ham at 325°F is 18 to 24 minutes per pound: 2 to 2¾ hours for 7 lb. Fully cooked ham is safe cold; you’re warming it to 140°F, USDA’s temperature for reheating a ham packaged at an inspected plant.
While it bakes, simmer the honey, brown sugar, orange juice, zest, mustard and ground cloves 3 to 4 minutes until syrupy.

About 30 minutes before it’s done, take off the foil, turn the oven to 400°F, and brush the ham with a third of the glaze. Brush twice more, 10 minutes apart, until glossy and browned at the edges. Watch it: sugar burns quickly.
Check that the thickest part reads 140°F on a food thermometer, not touching bone. Rest 15 minutes, then carve: cut along the bone to free large pieces, then slice them across the grain.

swaps.spiral: For a spiral-cut ham, see our brown sugar glazed spiral ham: it heats in 10 to 18 minutes per pound (USDA) and needs no scoring.
swaps.pineapple: Use pineapple juice instead of orange juice and pin pineapple rings to the ham for the last 30 minutes.

meta.servings: about ⅓ lb as bought (with bone)

items.title: Garlic and Rosemary Roast Leg of Lamb
items.subtitle: dinner · about 6 oz as bought
items.body: A bone-in leg studded with garlic and rubbed with rosemary, lemon and mustard, roasted at 325°F to a rosy 145°F. Serve with mint sauce.

steps: Pat the lamb dry. Trim any thick fat cap to about ¼ inch. With a small knife, make 12 slits about 1 inch deep all over and push a garlic slice into each.
Mix the grated garlic, rosemary, lemon zest and juice, mustard, oil, salt and pepper and rub it all over. You can do this up to a day ahead and refrigerate it.
Heat the oven to 325°F. Set the lamb fat side up on the rack in the pan.
Roast. USDA’s guide for a bone-in leg of lamb at 325°F is 20 to 26 minutes per pound: about 2 to 2½ hours for 6 lb. Start checking 30 minutes before.
It’s done at 145°F (medium-rare) in the thickest part, not touching the bone; go to 160°F for medium. USDA’s minimum for lamb roasts is 145°F with a 3-minute rest.
Tent with foil and rest 15 to 20 minutes. Carve slices across the grain, working around the bone.

swaps.boneless: A 4- to 7-lb boneless leg also takes 20 to 26 minutes per pound at 325°F (USDA). Tie it with string so it cooks evenly.
swaps.no_mustard: Leave out the mustard and add another tablespoon of oil.

items.title: Fresh Mint Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 2 tablespoons
items.body: The bright, sharp British sauce for lamb: chopped mint steeped in sweetened vinegar. Nothing like the green jelly.

steps: Chop the mint leaves finely with the sugar sprinkled over them; the sugar keeps the mint from bruising and helps it chop.
Scrape into a bowl, pour the boiling water over, and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Stir in the vinegar and salt. Let it stand at least 30 minutes. Taste: add a little more sugar if it’s too sharp.

swaps.honey: Use 3 tablespoons honey instead of the sugar.

items.title: Hard-Cooked Eggs for Dyeing and Eating
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 egg
items.body: Firm, evenly set eggs with no green ring, ready to dye, devil or slice. Steaming makes them easier to peel.

steps: Check every egg and set aside any with cracks; cracked eggs let germs in and shouldn’t be dyed (USDA).
Boil method: lay the eggs in one layer in the pan and cover with cold water by 1 inch. Bring to a full boil, cover, turn off the heat, and let them stand 12 minutes for large eggs.
Steam method (easier to peel): bring 1 inch of water to a boil in the pan, set the eggs in a steamer basket or right in the water, cover, and steam 12 to 13 minutes.
Lift the eggs into ice water and cool 15 minutes. The yolks and whites should be firm all the way through.
Dry them and refrigerate right away in the carton. To dye them, use food-grade dyes and keep them out of the refrigerator only while you work (see the egg-dyeing guide on the Easter page).
Refrigerate within 2 hours of cooking and eat within 1 week (FDA and USDA).

swaps.older_eggs: Eggs a week or two old peel more easily than very fresh ones.

items.title: Classic Egg Salad Sandwiches
items.subtitle: lunch · 1 sandwich
items.body: Creamy egg salad with celery and chives on soft bread. A good use for the eggs you dyed and kept in the refrigerator, not the ones that went on the hunt.

steps: Use eggs that stayed in the refrigerator (and were out no more than 2 hours in all). FDA advises not eating eggs that were hidden or played with.
Chop or mash the eggs with a fork. Stir in the mayonnaise, mustard, celery, chives, salt and pepper.
Spread on 6 slices of bread, add lettuce, and top with the rest.

swaps.lighter: Use plain Greek yogurt for half the mayonnaise.
swaps.gluten_free: Serve in lettuce cups.

items.title: Classic Scalloped Potatoes
items.subtitle: side · about 1 cup
items.body: Thin potato slices baked in a garlicky cream sauce until tender, with a golden top. No cheese: that would make them au gratin.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter the dish. Slice the potatoes; use the mandoline’s guard, never bare fingers.
Melt the butter in the saucepan, cook the shallot and garlic 2 minutes, then whisk in the flour for 1 minute.
Whisk in the milk and cream and bring to a simmer, whisking, until it thickens slightly. Stir in the salt, pepper, nutmeg and thyme.
Layer a third of the potatoes in the dish, overlapping, and pour over a third of the sauce. Repeat twice.
Cover with foil and bake 45 minutes. Uncover and bake 25 to 30 minutes more, until a knife slides through easily and the top is golden. Rest 10 minutes.
equipment: mandoline with its hand guard, or a sharp knife

swaps.au_gratin: Scatter 1½ cups shredded Gruyère or cheddar between the layers and on top.
swaps.lighter: Use all milk and no cream.

items.title: Honey Butter Glazed Carrots
items.subtitle: side · about ¾ cup
items.body: Carrots simmered in a little water, then glazed with butter and honey until shiny. Use slim spring carrots with their tops trimmed if you find them.

ingredients.prep: peeled, cut on the diagonal ½ inch thick

steps: Put the carrots, water, butter, honey and salt in the skillet. Cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, until just tender.
Uncover and boil, stirring, until the liquid cooks down to a glaze that coats the carrots, 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the parsley and lemon juice.

swaps.vegan: Use olive oil and maple syrup.

items.title: Buttered Peas with Mint
items.subtitle: side · about ½ cup
items.body: Sweet peas warmed with butter, shallot and fresh mint: the classic spring partner for lamb, ready in 15 minutes.

steps: Melt the butter in the pan and cook the shallot until soft, 2 minutes.
Add the peas and water, cover, and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until hot and bright green.
Stir in the mint, salt and lemon juice.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil.

items.title: Strawberry Spinach Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 2 cups
items.body: Baby spinach, sliced strawberries, red onion and crumbled feta with a honey-balsamic dressing. Add toasted almonds if your table eats nuts.

steps: Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the spinach, strawberries and onion in a big bowl.
Just before serving, toss with the dressing and scatter the feta and almonds on top.

swaps.nut_free: Leave out the almonds or use toasted sunflower seeds.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta.

items.title: Hot Cross Buns
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 bun
items.body: Soft spiced buns with raisins and orange zest, marked with a cross and glazed with warm apricot jam. Traditionally eaten on Good Friday.

steps: Stir the warm milk, yeast and a pinch of the sugar together; if using active dry yeast, wait 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in the rest of the sugar, the flour, salt, spices, egg and butter. Knead 8 to 10 minutes (5 in a mixer), until smooth and springy. Knead in the raisins and zest.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot until doubled, 1 to 1½ hours.
Grease the pan. Divide the dough into 12 pieces, roll each into a tight ball, and set them in rows. Cover and let rise until puffy and touching, 45 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375°F. Stir the ½ cup flour and water into a thick paste, pipe lines down each row and then across to make crosses.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until deep golden. Brush the hot buns with the warmed jam. Cool a little and pull apart.
equipment: stand mixer with a dough hook, or a big bowl and your hands

swaps.icing_cross: Pipe crosses of powdered-sugar icing on the cooled buns instead of the flour paste.
swaps.chocolate: Use chocolate chips instead of raisins.

items.title: Carrot Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice
items.body: A moist, spiced two-layer cake full of grated carrots, with tangy cream cheese frosting. Walnuts are optional.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the pans, line the bottoms with parchment, and grease again.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and spices.

In another bowl whisk the eggs, both sugars, oil and vanilla until smooth. Stir in the dry ingredients, then the carrots and walnuts. Don’t taste the raw batter: raw flour and raw eggs can carry germs (FDA and CDC).
Divide between the pans and bake 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes, turn out, and cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth, then beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla until fluffy.
Set one layer on a plate, spread with a third of the frosting, top with the second layer, and frost the top and sides. Chill 30 minutes before slicing.

swaps.sheet_cake: Bake in a 9-by-13-inch pan for 40 to 45 minutes and frost the top only.
swaps.pineapple: Add ½ cup well-drained crushed pineapple with the carrots.

items.title: Lemon Bars
items.subtitle: snack · 1 bar (2 inches square)
items.body: A buttery shortbread crust under a tart, silky lemon layer, dusted with powdered sugar. Sunny on a spring table.

ingredients.prep: zest of 1, juice of both (about ½ cup)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line the pan with parchment, leaving overhang.
Stir the flour, powdered sugar, salt and melted butter into a soft dough. Press it evenly into the pan and bake 18 to 20 minutes, until light golden.
Whisk the eggs, sugar, flour, zest and lemon juice until smooth.
Pour over the hot crust and bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the filling is set and doesn’t wobble in the center. A thermometer in the center reads above 160°F, the temperature for egg dishes.
Cool, then chill at least 2 hours. Lift out, cut into 16 squares, and dust with powdered sugar.

items.title: Baked Ham and Swiss Sliders
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 2 sliders
items.body: A tray of soft rolls filled with leftover ham and Swiss cheese, brushed with mustard butter and baked until melty. The day-after lunch everyone asks for.

ingredients.prep: or other soft dinner rolls, in one slab
cooked leftover ham, thinly sliced (weighed without the bone)

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Without separating the rolls, slice the whole slab in half horizontally. Set the bottom in the dish.
Layer on the ham, then the cheese, and put the top back on.
Mix the butter, mustard, Worcestershire, sesame seeds and onion powder and brush it over the top.

Cover with foil and bake 15 minutes, then uncover and bake 8 to 10 minutes more, until the cheese melts, the tops are golden and the ham in the middle reaches 165°F (USDA’s temperature for reheating leftovers).
Cut along the roll lines and serve warm.

swaps.sesame_free: Use poppy seeds or leave them off.

items.title: Apple Cinnamon Baked Oatmeal
items.subtitle: breakfast · 1 square (about 1 cup)
items.body: A pan of soft, cinnamon-spiced oats with apples, walnuts and raisins. Bake once and reheat all week.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.
In a large bowl, mix the oats, flaxseed, brown sugar, baking powder, cinnamon and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla.
Spread the apples, walnuts and raisins in the dish. Scatter the oat mixture over them, then pour the milk mixture evenly over the top. Press gently so the oats are wet.
Bake 38 to 42 minutes, until golden and set in the center (160°F on a thermometer). Cool 10 minutes before cutting.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and oil instead of butter.
swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of walnuts.

items.title: Apple Pear Crisp
items.subtitle: snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Tender apples and pears under a buttery oat and pecan topping. Good warm with a scoop of ice cream.

ingredients.prep: ripe but firm, cored and sliced

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Toss the apples and pears with the lemon juice, sugar, 1 tablespoon flour and cinnamon. Spread in the baking dish.
In a bowl, mix the oats, 1/2 cup flour, brown sugar, pecans and salt. Cut in the cold butter until the mixture forms small clumps.
Sprinkle the topping over the fruit. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fruit bubbles at the edges.
Cool at least 10 minutes so the juices thicken.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut oil instead of butter and skip the ice cream.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the pecans and add 1/4 cup more oats.

items.title: Waldorf Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Crisp apples, grapes, celery and toasted walnuts in a light, creamy dressing.

steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes until fragrant. Let them cool.
Toss the apples with the lemon juice so they stay white.
Stir together the mayonnaise, yogurt, honey and salt.
Add the grapes, celery, walnuts and dressing to the apples and fold together. Serve cold.

swaps.dairy_free: Use all mayonnaise.
swaps.egg_free: Use all yogurt instead of mayonnaise.
swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of walnuts.

items.title: Harvest Apple Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 2 cups
items.body: Greens with crisp apple, dried cranberries, toasted pecans and pumpkin seeds in a cider vinaigrette.

steps: Toast the pecans and pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes, until the seeds start to pop. Cool.
Shake the vinaigrette ingredients in a jar until creamy.
Rinse the apple, then slice it just before serving so it stays crisp.
Toss the greens with most of the vinaigrette. Top with the apple, cranberries, nuts, seeds and feta if using, and drizzle with the rest.

swaps.nut_free: Leave out the pecans and double the pumpkin seeds.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta.

items.title: Apple Nachos
items.subtitle: snack · about 3/4 apple
items.body: Apple slices on a plate, drizzled with sunflower seed butter and topped with raisins and granola. A nut-free snack kids can build.

steps: Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice and spread them on a large plate, overlapping a little.
Warm the sunflower seed butter in the microwave 10 to 15 seconds so it drizzles, then drizzle it over the apples with a spoon.
Scatter the raisins, granola and chocolate chips (if using) on top. Dust with cinnamon and serve right away.

swaps.nut_free: Sunflower seed butter is nut-free; check that the granola is too.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the chocolate chips or use dairy-free ones.

items.title: Cranberry Orange Muffins
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 muffin
items.body: Tart cranberries and fresh orange in a tender muffin. Freezes well for busy mornings.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line the muffin tin.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Zest the orange into a second bowl, then squeeze in the juice (about 1/3 cup). Whisk in the milk, egg, melted butter and vanilla.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry just until no flour shows. Fold in the cranberries.
Fill the cups about three-quarters full. Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and oil instead of butter.

items.title: Homemade Cranberry Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 1/4 cup
items.body: Fresh cranberries simmered with orange and sugar until they burst. Ready in 15 minutes.

steps: Put the sugar, orange juice, water and salt in the saucepan and bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cranberries. Simmer, stirring now and then, 8 to 10 minutes, until most of the berries burst.
Stir in the orange zest and cinnamon. The sauce looks loose but thickens as it cools.
Cool to room temperature, about 1 hour, then serve or refrigerate.

items.title: Orange Sesame Chicken
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/4 cups with rice
items.body: Crisp-edged chicken bites tossed in a fresh orange, ginger and sesame sauce. A takeout favorite made at home.

steps: Start the rice. Whisk the orange zest and juice, soy sauce, honey, vinegar, ginger, garlic and 2 teaspoons cornstarch in a small bowl.
Toss the chicken with 3 tablespoons cornstarch and the salt.

Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in a single layer, turning, 7 to 9 minutes, until browned and a thermometer reads 165°F. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Stir the sauce and pour it into the pan. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Stir in the sesame seeds. Serve over rice with green onions.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.

items.title: Winter Citrus Salad
items.subtitle: side,breakfast,snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Grapefruit, oranges and kiwi with pomegranate seeds, honey and mint. Bright fruit for the darkest months.

steps: Rinse the fruit. Slice the top and bottom off each grapefruit and orange, then cut away the peel and white pith, following the curve of the fruit.
Slice the grapefruit and oranges into rounds, or cut between the membranes to free the segments. Save the juice.
Arrange the citrus and kiwi on a platter. Scatter the pomegranate seeds over the top.
Stir the honey into 2 tablespoons of the saved juice and drizzle over. Finish with the mint.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

items.title: Broiled Brown Sugar Grapefruit
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1/2 grapefruit
items.body: Grapefruit halves with a bubbly, caramelized brown sugar top. A warm breakfast treat in 10 minutes.

steps: Set an oven rack about 4 inches from the broiler and heat the broiler.
Rinse the grapefruit before cutting. Run a paring knife around each segment so it lifts out easily later.
Set the halves cut side up on the baking sheet. Brush with butter if using. Mix the brown sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over the tops.
Broil 4 to 6 minutes, watching closely, until the sugar bubbles and browns. Cool 2 minutes and serve with a spoon.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the butter.

items.title: Grapefruit Avocado Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Juicy grapefruit and creamy avocado over peppery greens with a honey-citrus dressing.

steps: Rinse the grapefruit. Cut away the peel and pith, then cut out the segments over a bowl to catch the juice.
Whisk 2 tablespoons of the grapefruit juice with the olive oil, honey, salt and pepper.
Spread the arugula on a platter. Top with the grapefruit, avocado and onion.
Drizzle with the dressing and serve right away.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

items.title: Salmon with Grapefruit Avocado Salsa
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 fillet with salsa
items.body: Roasted salmon topped with a fresh salsa of grapefruit, avocado, lime and cilantro.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and line the baking sheet with parchment.
Set the salmon skin side down on the sheet. Rub with the oil and sprinkle with salt, pepper and chili powder.
Roast 12 to 14 minutes, until the fish flakes easily and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F.
While it roasts, gently stir together the grapefruit, avocado, onion, jalapeño (if using), cilantro, lime juice and salt.
Spoon the salsa over the salmon to serve.

items.title: Grapefruit Granita
items.subtitle: snack · about 2/3 cup
items.body: Fresh grapefruit juice frozen and scraped into icy, sweet-tart flakes. Only three ingredients.

steps: Rinse the grapefruit, then cut in half and squeeze out the juice. Strain out the seeds.
Warm the water and sugar in a small pan or the microwave, stirring, just until the sugar dissolves. Stir it into the juice.
Pour into the pan and freeze 45 minutes, until ice forms at the edges. Scrape and stir with a fork.
Freeze, scraping every 30 to 45 minutes, until it is all fluffy ice crystals, about 3 hours in all.
Scrape once more and spoon into chilled glasses. Top with mint if you like.

items.title: Tropical Smoothie
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Pineapple, mango and banana blended with yogurt and orange juice. Tastes like vacation.

steps: Put the orange juice and yogurt in the blender first, then the banana, pineapple and mango.
Blend on high until smooth, about 1 minute. Add a splash more juice if it is too thick to pour.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt or more juice.

items.title: Fresh Mango Salsa
items.subtitle: snack,side · about 1/2 cup
items.body: Sweet mango with red pepper, onion, cilantro and lime. Scoop with chips or spoon over tacos, chicken or fish.

steps: Rinse the mangoes, pepper and cilantro. Wear gloves or wash your hands well after seeding the jalapeño.
Combine the mango, bell pepper, onion, jalapeño and cilantro in a bowl.
Stir in the lime juice and salt. Let it sit 10 minutes for the flavors to mix, then taste and add more salt or lime if needed.

items.title: Mango Coconut Chia Pudding
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 jar (about 3/4 cup)
items.body: Chia seeds soaked overnight in coconut milk, layered with fresh mango. Make jars for the week.

steps: Whisk the coconut milk, milk, chia seeds, maple syrup and vanilla in a bowl.
Let stand 10 minutes, then whisk again to break up clumps.
Divide among the jars, cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight, until thick.
Toss the mango with the lime juice and spoon on top before serving. Sprinkle with coconut if using.

swaps.dairy_free: Use more coconut milk or another plant milk instead of the milk.

items.title: Peach Mango Smoothie
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Peaches and mango blended thick with yogurt and a little honey. Use fresh, frozen or canned peaches.

ingredients.prep: pitted and sliced, or 1 1/2 cups frozen

steps: Rinse fresh peaches before slicing.
Put the milk and yogurt in the blender, then the peaches, mango, honey and vanilla.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Add a few ice cubes if you used fresh peaches and want it colder.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Mango Lime Chicken Rice Bowls
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 bowl
items.body: Chili-lime chicken over rice with black beans, fresh mango and a squeeze of lime.

steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Toss the chicken with the lime zest and juice, oil, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt.
Cook the chicken in a skillet over medium-high heat, 5 to 6 minutes per side, until a thermometer reads 165°F. Rest 5 minutes, then slice. Wash your hands and anything that touched the raw chicken.
Warm the beans in a small pan or the microwave. Mix the mango, onion and cilantro.
Fill bowls with rice, beans, chicken and the mango mixture. Serve with lime wedges and avocado if you like.

swaps.meatless: Use a second can of black beans instead of chicken.

items.title: Tropical Fruit Salad
items.subtitle: side,snack,breakfast · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Pineapple, mango and kiwi tossed with lime juice, honey and fresh mint.

steps: Rinse the fruit before peeling and cutting.
Combine the pineapple, mango and kiwi in a large bowl.
Stir the lime juice and honey together, pour over and toss gently. Add the banana and mint just before serving.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

items.title: Sheet-Pan Pineapple Pork Tacos
items.subtitle: dinner · 3 tacos
items.body: Chili-rubbed pork and pineapple roasted on one pan, tucked into warm tortillas with onion, cilantro and lime. Inspired by tacos al pastor.

ingredients.prep: boneless, sliced 1/4 inch thick and cut in strips

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F. Mix the chili powder, paprika, cumin, oregano, garlic, salt, vinegar and oil in a bowl. Add the pork and toss to coat. Wash your hands after handling raw pork.
Spread the pork on one side of the baking sheet and the pineapple on the other, each in a single layer.
Roast 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once, until the pork is browned at the edges and a thermometer reads at least 145°F. Rest 3 minutes, then chop the pork and pineapple together.
Fill the warm tortillas with the pork and pineapple. Top with onion and cilantro, and squeeze lime over each taco.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are usually gluten-free; check the package.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained black beans, warmed with the spices, instead of pork.

items.title: Pineapple Cashew Fried Rice
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Day-old rice stir-fried with pineapple, eggs, peas and carrots, and finished with toasted cashews.

ingredients.prep: cooked a day ahead and chilled (makes about 4 cups)

steps: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Scramble the eggs until no liquid egg remains (egg dishes are done at 160°F). Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and raise the heat to medium-high. Cook the onion 3 minutes, then the garlic 30 seconds.
Add the peas and carrots and cook 2 minutes. Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and cook, stirring now and then, until hot, about 5 minutes.
Push the rice aside, add the pineapple and let it brown 2 minutes. Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, eggs, cashews and green onions.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the cashews; add diced cooked chicken or ham.

items.title: Carrot Raisin Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 2/3 cup
items.body: Shredded carrots, plump raisins and crushed pineapple in a light, tangy dressing. A potluck classic.

steps: Shred the carrots and put them in a bowl with the raisins and pineapple.
Stir together the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, sugar and salt.
Fold the dressing into the carrots. Chill at least 30 minutes, or serve right away.

swaps.dairy_free: Use all mayonnaise.

items.title: Watermelon Cucumber Feta Salad
items.subtitle: side · about 1 cup
items.body: Cold watermelon and cucumber with salty feta, mint and lime. A cool side for hot days.

steps: Rinse the outside of the watermelon and cucumber before cutting.
Put the watermelon, cucumber and onion in a large bowl.
Drizzle with the lime juice and oil, add a pinch of salt and toss gently.
Top with the feta and mint and serve cold.

swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the feta.

items.title: Watermelon Agua Fresca
items.subtitle: snack · about 1 cup
items.body: Fresh watermelon blended with water and lime, then strained. A light Mexican-style fruit drink.

steps: Rinse the watermelon before cutting.
Blend the watermelon and water until smooth, in two batches if needed.
Pour through a strainer into a pitcher, pressing on the pulp. Stir in the lime juice. Taste and stir in sugar if the melon is not very sweet.
Serve over ice with mint if you like.

items.title: Watermelon Fruit Pizza
items.subtitle: snack · 2 wedges
items.body: Thick rounds of watermelon spread with honey yogurt and topped with berries and kiwi, cut into wedges.

ingredients.prep: 2 round slices, 1 inch thick, from the middle of the melon

steps: Rinse the watermelon and fruit. A grown-up cuts the round slices and trims off the rind.
Stir the honey into the yogurt and spread it over each round, leaving a little edge.
Top with strawberries, blueberries and kiwi.
Cut each round into 6 wedges and serve right away.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Summer Melon Salad
items.subtitle: side,snack,breakfast · about 1 cup
items.body: Watermelon, cantaloupe and honeydew with a honey-lime dressing and mint.

steps: Scrub the outside of each melon under running water before cutting; a knife can carry germs from the rind into the fruit.
Cut or scoop the melons and combine in a large bowl.
Stir the lime juice and honey together, pour over and toss. Scatter the mint over the top.

swaps.vegan: Use maple syrup instead of honey.

items.title: Watermelon Lime Ice Pops
items.subtitle: snack · 1 ice pop
items.body: Blended watermelon and lime frozen into pops. Only three ingredients and no added dye.

steps: Rinse the watermelon before cutting.
Blend the watermelon, lime juice and honey until smooth.
Pour into the molds, add the sticks and freeze at least 6 hours, until solid.
Run the molds under warm water for a few seconds to loosen the pops.

items.title: Cantaloupe Cottage Cheese Bowls
items.subtitle: breakfast,lunch,snack · 1/4 cantaloupe with filling
items.body: A diner classic: wedges of cantaloupe filled with cottage cheese, blueberries and a little granola.

steps: Scrub the cantaloupe under running water and dry it before cutting.
Cut the melon into quarters and scoop out the seeds.
Fill each quarter with 1/2 cup cottage cheese. Top with blueberries and granola, and drizzle with honey if you like.

items.title: Honeydew Mint Smoothie
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Cool, pale green smoothie of honeydew, banana, yogurt, lime and fresh mint.

steps: Scrub the honeydew under running water before cutting.
Blend everything until smooth, about 1 minute. Add a few ice cubes for a colder, thicker drink.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Fruit Kabobs with Yogurt Dip
items.subtitle: snack,side · 2 kabobs with dip
items.body: Melon, pineapple, strawberries and grapes on skewers with a honey-vanilla yogurt dip. Party food that disappears.

steps: Scrub the melons and pineapple under running water before cutting. Rinse the berries and grapes.
Thread the fruit onto the skewers in a pattern, about 6 or 7 pieces each.
Stir the yogurt, honey, vanilla and cinnamon together for the dip. Serve the kabobs cold with the dip.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Cantaloupe Mozzarella Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Sweet cantaloupe with fresh mozzarella, arugula and basil, finished with olive oil and a little balsamic.

steps: Scrub the cantaloupe under running water before cutting.
Spread the arugula on a platter. Top with the cantaloupe and mozzarella.
Drizzle with the oil and vinegar, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and scatter the basil over the top.

swaps.dairy_free: Use diced avocado instead of mozzarella.

items.title: Sausage with Roasted Grapes and Onions
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 1/2 sausages with grapes
items.body: Italian sausages roasted on one pan with red grapes and onion until the grapes turn jammy. An Italian farmhouse dish.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the grapes and onion with the oil, salt and pepper on the baking sheet. Nestle in the sausages and rosemary sprigs.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, turning the sausages once, until they are browned, a thermometer in the center reads 160°F, and the grapes are soft and starting to burst.
Drizzle the balsamic over the grapes and onions, stir, and serve.

swaps.meatless: Use plant-based sausages and cook by the package directions.

items.title: Broccoli Grape Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Crunchy raw broccoli with grapes, sunflower seeds and dried cranberries in a sweet-tangy dressing. A cookout favorite.

steps: Rinse the broccoli and grapes and pat dry.
Whisk the mayonnaise, yogurt, vinegar, sugar and salt.
Toss the broccoli, grapes, onion and cranberries with the dressing.
Chill at least 30 minutes. Stir in the sunflower seeds just before serving so they stay crunchy.

swaps.dairy_free: Use all mayonnaise.

items.title: Green Kiwi Smoothie
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Spinach, kiwi, banana and pineapple blended with milk and chia. Sweet enough that kids ask for it.

steps: Pour the milk into the blender and add the spinach. Blend until no leaf bits remain.
Add the kiwi, banana, pineapple and chia seeds and blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Serve right away.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk.

items.title: Banana Walnut Bread
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 slice (about 3/4 inch)
items.body: A moist loaf with plenty of ripe banana and toasted walnuts. The best use for spotty bananas.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the loaf pan.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl. Whisk in the melted butter, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla.
Add the flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon and stir just until combined. Fold in the walnuts.
Scrape into the pan. Bake 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out with only a few moist crumbs. Cover loosely with foil after 40 minutes if the top browns too fast.
Cool 15 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use 1/3 cup vegetable oil instead of butter.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the walnuts or use chocolate chips.

items.title: Lemon Blueberry Muffins
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 muffin
items.body: Bursting with blueberries and bright with fresh lemon zest and juice.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line the muffin tin.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Zest the lemon into a second bowl, then squeeze in the juice (about 3 tablespoons). Whisk in the yogurt, eggs, melted butter and vanilla.
Stir the wet mixture into the dry just until no flour shows. Gently fold in the blueberries.
Fill the cups about three-quarters full. Bake 20 to 24 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt and oil instead of butter.

items.title: Mixed Berry Cobbler
items.subtitle: snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Blueberries, raspberries and blackberries baked under soft, golden biscuit topping.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Rinse the berries gently and drain well.
Toss the berries with 1/2 cup sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice. Spread in the baking dish.
Mix the flour, 3 tablespoons sugar, baking powder and salt. Cut in the butter until it looks like coarse crumbs. Stir in the milk and vanilla just until a soft dough forms.
Drop spoonfuls of dough over the berries, leaving gaps for steam. Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fruit bubbles in the center.
Cool 15 minutes so the filling thickens.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and cold coconut oil.

items.title: Berry Chia Jam
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 2 tablespoons
items.body: A quick fridge jam: raspberries and blackberries simmered soft and thickened with chia seeds. No pectin, much less sugar.

steps: Put the berries in the saucepan over medium heat. Cook, stirring, 5 to 8 minutes, until they break down and bubble.
Mash to the texture you like. Stir in the maple syrup and lemon juice.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the chia seeds. Let stand 10 minutes, then stir again.
Spoon into the jar. It thickens more as it chills, about 30 minutes.

items.title: Berry Oat Crumble Bars
items.subtitle: snack · 1 bar (2-inch square)
items.body: A buttery oat crust and crumble with a layer of raspberries and blackberries and a few sliced almonds.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Line the pan with parchment, leaving some hanging over the sides.
Mix the flour, oats, brown sugar, baking powder and salt. Stir in the melted butter until crumbly.
Press two-thirds of the mixture firmly into the pan. Stir the almonds into the rest.
Toss the berries with the sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice, mashing a few. Spread over the crust and sprinkle the almond crumble on top.
Bake 38 to 42 minutes, until golden and bubbling at the edges. Cool completely, about 1 hour, before lifting out and cutting.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend and oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the almonds.
swaps.dairy_free: Use melted coconut oil instead of butter.

items.title: Berry Yogurt Ice Pops
items.subtitle: snack · 1 ice pop
items.body: Creamy yogurt swirled with mashed raspberries and blackberries, frozen on a stick.

steps: Stir the yogurt, 2 tablespoons honey and vanilla together.
Mash the berries with the rest of the honey in another bowl.
Spoon yogurt and berries into the molds in layers, then swirl with a skewer.
Add sticks and freeze at least 6 hours. Run the molds under warm water to release.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a thick dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Summer Berry Pecan Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 2 cups
items.body: Greens with strawberries, raspberries, blackberries, toasted pecans and goat cheese in a balsamic dressing.

steps: Toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes. Cool and chop.
Rinse the berries gently and pat dry.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the greens with most of the dressing. Top with the berries, pecans and goat cheese if using, and drizzle with the rest.

swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of pecans.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the goat cheese.

items.title: Mixed Berry Flax Smoothie
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Frozen berries, banana and yogurt with ground flaxseed for fiber. Thick, purple and quick.

steps: Pour the milk and yogurt into the blender, then add the banana, berries and flaxseed.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Add a splash more milk if it is too thick.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Pear Walnut Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 2 cups
items.body: Sliced ripe pears, toasted walnuts and a little blue cheese over greens with a maple-dijon vinaigrette.

steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes. Cool and chop.
Shake the vinaigrette ingredients in a jar.
Rinse the pears, then slice them just before serving.
Toss the greens and onion with most of the vinaigrette. Top with pears, walnuts and blue cheese if using, and drizzle with the rest.

swaps.nut_free: Use pumpkin seeds instead of walnuts.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the blue cheese.

items.title: Pear and Cheddar Grilled Cheese
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1 sandwich
items.body: Sharp cheddar and thin slices of sweet pear grilled until golden, with a little honey mustard.

steps: Stir the mustard and honey together and spread thinly on 4 slices of bread.
Sprinkle each with 1/4 cup cheese, then a layer of pear slices and another 1/4 cup cheese. Top with the remaining bread.
Butter the outsides. Cook in a skillet over medium-low heat 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden and the cheese melts.
Cut in half and serve warm.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.
swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free cheese and oil.

items.title: Baked Pears with Walnuts and Maple
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 2 pear halves
items.body: Pear halves baked soft with a maple, oat and walnut filling. Serve warm with yogurt.

ingredients.prep: ripe but firm, halved and cored

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Rinse the pears. Halve them, scoop out the cores and set them cut side up in the dish.
Mix the walnuts, oats, 1 tablespoon maple syrup, butter and cinnamon. Spoon into the hollows.
Drizzle the rest of the maple syrup over the pears and pour the water into the dish.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the pears. Serve warm with yogurt and the pan juices.

swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut oil and a dairy-free yogurt.
swaps.nut_free: Use more oats and sunflower seeds instead of walnuts.

items.title: Spiced Pear Oatmeal
items.subtitle: breakfast · about 1 cup
items.body: Creamy stovetop oats cooked with diced pear, cinnamon and ginger.

steps: Bring the water, milk and salt to a simmer in the saucepan over medium heat. Watch so it does not boil over.
Stir in the oats, pear, cinnamon and ginger. Cook, stirring often, 5 to 7 minutes, until thick and the pear is tender.
Stir in the maple syrup. Serve topped with pecans if you like.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk.

items.title: Stone Fruit Crisp
items.subtitle: snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Peaches, plums and cherries baked under a crunchy oat and almond topping. Summer in a pan.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Rinse the fruit.
Toss the peaches, plums and cherries with the sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice and vanilla. Spread in the baking dish.
Mix the oats, flour, brown sugar, almonds, cinnamon and salt. Work in the butter with your fingers until clumpy.
Scatter the topping over the fruit. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until golden and bubbling in the center.
Cool at least 10 minutes before serving.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the almonds.
swaps.dairy_free: Use cold coconut oil.

items.title: Peach Cobbler
items.subtitle: snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Juicy cinnamon peaches under a tender, golden batter that bakes up around the fruit. A Southern favorite.

ingredients.prep: peeled and sliced (about 6 cups), or 3 cans sliced peaches, drained

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Put the butter in the baking dish and set it in the oven to melt.
Simmer the peaches, 1/2 cup sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a saucepan over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Whisk the flour, 3/4 cup sugar, baking powder and salt. Whisk in the milk and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the batter over the melted butter. Do not stir. Spoon the peaches and their juice evenly over the batter.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the top is golden and the batter is set. Cool 15 minutes before serving.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free butter.

items.title: Grilled Chicken with Peach Salsa
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 chicken breast with salsa
items.body: Simple grilled chicken topped with a fresh salsa of peaches, red onion, jalapeño, cilantro and lime.

steps: Rinse the peaches, cilantro and jalapeño. Stir the salsa ingredients together and set aside.
Rub the chicken with the oil, salt, pepper, cumin and garlic powder. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Heat the grill or grill pan to medium-high. Cook the chicken 5 to 7 minutes per side, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F.
Rest 5 minutes on a clean plate, then slice and top with the salsa.

items.title: Grilled Peaches and Plums with Honey Yogurt
items.subtitle: snack,side · about 3 fruit halves with yogurt
items.body: Halved peaches, nectarines and plums grilled until caramelized, served with honey yogurt.

steps: Heat the grill or grill pan to medium. Rinse the fruit before cutting.
Brush the cut sides of the fruit with oil.
Grill cut side down 4 to 5 minutes, until marked and starting to soften, then turn and grill 2 minutes more.
Stir the yogurt with half the honey and the cinnamon. Serve the fruit warm with the yogurt and a drizzle of the rest of the honey.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Plum Kuchen
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 square
items.body: A German-style plum cake: a soft butter cake topped with rows of plums and cinnamon sugar.

ingredients.prep: halved, pitted and cut in quarters

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease and flour the pan.
Beat the butter and sugar until fluffy. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Add to the butter mixture in two parts, alternating with the milk, mixing just until smooth.
Spread the batter in the pan. Press the plum pieces into the top, skin side down, in tight rows.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over. Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until a toothpick in the cake part comes out clean. Cool 20 minutes before cutting.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free butter and a plant milk.

items.title: Roasted Plums with Yogurt and Granola
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 cup yogurt with plums
items.body: Plums roasted with honey and cinnamon until syrupy, spooned over yogurt with granola.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Rinse the plums.
Set the plum halves cut side up in the dish. Drizzle with honey and orange juice and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Roast 15 to 20 minutes, until soft and juicy.
Spoon the yogurt into bowls, top with the warm or cold plums and their syrup, and finish with granola.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Sheet-Pan Plum Ginger Chicken
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 thighs with plums
items.body: Chicken thighs roasted with plums, red onion, ginger and a soy-honey glaze. Sweet, savory and one pan.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Stir the glaze ingredients together.
Toss the plums and onion with the oil on the baking sheet and push to the edges.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper, set it in the middle of the pan and brush with half the glaze. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Roast 15 minutes. Brush the chicken with the rest of the glaze and stir the plums. Roast 10 to 15 minutes more, until a thermometer in the thickest thigh reads 165°F.
Rest 5 minutes, then serve with the plums and pan juices spooned over.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.

items.title: Cherry Almond Overnight Oats
items.subtitle: breakfast · 1 jar (about 1 cup)
items.body: Oats, chia and milk soaked overnight with sweet cherries and almonds. Grab a jar and go.

ingredients.prep: pitted and halved, fresh or thawed frozen

steps: Stir the oats, chia, milk, yogurt, maple syrup and vanilla together.
Fold in 1 cup of the cherries. Divide among the jars and top with the rest of the cherries.
Cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight. Sprinkle with almonds before eating.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free yogurt.
swaps.nut_free: Use pumpkin seeds instead of almonds.

items.title: Chocolate Cherry Smoothie
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Frozen cherries, banana, cocoa and milk blended into a thick, not-too-sweet chocolate smoothie.

steps: Pour the milk into the blender and add the yogurt, banana, cherries, cocoa and vanilla.
Blend until smooth, about 1 minute. Serve right away.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Pork Tenderloin with Cherry Sauce
items.subtitle: dinner · about 4 ounces pork with sauce
items.body: Seared and roasted pork tenderloin with a quick pan sauce of sweet cherries, balsamic and thyme.

ingredients.prep: about 1 1/4 pounds each, silver skin trimmed
pitted and halved, fresh or frozen

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the pork dry and season with salt and pepper. Wash your hands after handling raw pork.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the tenderloins on all sides, about 6 minutes.
Move the skillet to the oven and roast 12 to 15 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F. Move the pork to a cutting board and rest at least 3 minutes.

Set the skillet over medium heat (the handle is hot; use a mitt). Cook the shallot 1 minute. Add the cherries, vinegar, honey, broth and thyme and simmer 5 to 7 minutes, until the cherries soften and the sauce thickens.
Remove the thyme stems and stir in the butter. Slice the pork and spoon the sauce over.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the butter.

items.title: Cherry Clafoutis
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 wedge
items.body: A French country dessert: cherries baked in a puffy, custardy pancake batter. Simple and lovely warm.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter the pie plate and spread the cherries in it.
Blend or whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, flour, vanilla and salt until smooth.
Pour the batter over the cherries.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until puffed, golden and set in the center (160°F).
Cool 15 minutes; it settles as it cools. Dust with powdered sugar if you like and cut into wedges.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and oil for the dish.

items.title: Crispy Baked Buffalo Wings
items.subtitle: snack,dinner · about 8 wing pieces
items.body: Wings tossed with a little baking powder and salt and baked on racks until the skin turns crisp, without a pot of oil, then coated in classic butter-and-hot-sauce Buffalo sauce.

ingredients.prep: not baking soda; it helps the skin crisp

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Line the baking sheets with foil and set the wire racks on them.
Pat the wings very dry with paper towels. Toss them in a large bowl with the baking powder, salt and garlic powder until lightly coated. Wash your hands.
Spread the wings in one layer on the racks, skin side up, with a little space between them.
Bake 25 minutes. Flip the wings, swap the pans between racks, and bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until deep golden and crisp.
Check a few of the biggest wings with a food thermometer, not touching bone: they are safe at 165°F (USDA). Wings get more tender and render more fat if you keep going, up to about 175 to 185°F.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a small saucepan with the hot sauce and honey, whisking until smooth. Toss the hot wings with the sauce in a clean bowl.
Serve with celery and carrot sticks and blue cheese or ranch dip. Set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate it or swap in a fresh batch from the kitchen (USDA).

swaps.mild: Use half hot sauce and half melted butter, or toss in barbecue sauce.
swaps.dairy_free: Melt the hot sauce with 3 tablespoons olive oil instead of butter.

items.title: Fried Buffalo Wings
items.subtitle: snack,dinner · about 8 wing pieces
items.body: The original bar-style wing: fried unbreaded until crackly, then tossed in butter and hot sauce. Fry in small batches with a thermometer, and follow the frying safety steps.

ingredients.prep: flats and drumettes, tips removed, patted very dry
or peanut or canola oil, for frying

steps: Frying safety: use a deep, heavy pot with plenty of room above the oil, clip on a deep-fry thermometer, and never leave hot oil alone. Keep a lid or sheet pan beside the stove; if the oil catches fire, turn off the burner and slide the lid over it. Never pour water on a grease fire. Keep children well back from the stove.
Pat the wings very dry; water makes hot oil spatter. Sprinkle with the salt.

Pour oil into the pot to a depth of about 2 inches, keeping at least 3 to 4 inches of room above it. Heat over medium to 375°F, watching the thermometer. If the oil starts to smoke, turn off the heat.

Lower about a third of the wings into the oil gently with the spider, away from you. Fry 10 to 12 minutes, stirring now and then, until deep golden and crisp. Adjust the heat to keep the oil near 350 to 375°F.
Lift the wings onto the rack to drain. Let the oil come back to 375°F before the next batch.
Check a few of the biggest wings with a food thermometer, not touching bone: they are safe at 165°F (USDA). Wings get more tender and render more fat if you keep going, up to about 175 to 185°F.

Melt the butter with the hot sauce and honey and toss the wings in a clean bowl. Turn off the burner and let the oil cool completely, for hours, before straining or throwing it away (in a sealed container, not down the drain).
equipment: large, heavy, deep pot or Dutch oven (at least 5 quarts)
sheet pan with a wire rack
a lid or sheet pan that covers the pot

swaps.baked: For less mess and no hot oil, make the crispy baked wings instead.
swaps.peanut_allergy: Many people with peanut allergies avoid peanut oil; fry in canola or vegetable oil and tell your guests.

items.title: Sticky Honey-Garlic Wings
items.subtitle: snack,dinner · about 8 wing pieces
items.body: Crisp oven wings glazed with a sweet and savory honey, soy and garlic sauce, sprinkled with sesame seeds and green onions. The wing for people who don’t like heat.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line the pans with foil and set the racks on them. Pat the wings dry, toss with the baking powder and salt, and spread them out on the racks. Wash your hands.
Bake 25 minutes, flip and swap the pans, then bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until golden and crisp.
Check a few of the biggest wings with a food thermometer, not touching bone: they are safe at 165°F (USDA). Wings get more tender and render more fat if you keep going, up to about 175 to 185°F.
Meanwhile, simmer the honey, soy sauce, garlic, ginger and vinegar for 2 minutes. Stir in the cornstarch mix and simmer 1 minute more, until glossy and thick.
Toss the hot wings with the glaze, then put them back on the racks and bake 5 minutes so the glaze sets. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.

items.title: Lemon-Pepper Wings
items.subtitle: snack,dinner · about 8 wing pieces
items.body: Crisp baked wings tossed in melted butter with lots of fresh lemon zest and cracked black pepper. Bright, salty and not spicy.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F and set wire racks in two foil-lined baking sheets. Pat the wings dry, toss with the baking powder and 1 teaspoon of the salt, and spread them out on the racks. Wash your hands.
Bake 25 minutes, flip and swap the pans, and bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until crisp and golden.
Check a few of the biggest wings with a food thermometer, not touching bone: they are safe at 165°F (USDA). Wings get more tender and render more fat if you keep going, up to about 175 to 185°F.
Stir the melted butter, lemon zest, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, pepper, garlic powder and the remaining salt in a large bowl. Toss in the hot wings and sprinkle with parsley.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

items.title: Homemade Blue Cheese Dip
items.subtitle: snack,side · 2 tablespoons (makes about 1½ cups)
items.body: Chunky, tangy blue cheese dressing for wings and celery, made from sour cream, mayonnaise, buttermilk and crumbled blue cheese. Better than bottled, and ready in ten minutes.

ingredients.prep: or milk with a squeeze of lemon
adds depth; it usually contains anchovies

steps: Whisk the sour cream, mayonnaise, buttermilk, lemon juice, Worcestershire (if using), garlic powder and pepper until smooth.
Fold in the blue cheese, mashing a little of it with a fork so it streaks through. Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed.
Refrigerate at least 30 minutes so the flavors blend. Set it out in a bowl over ice. Set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate it or swap in a fresh batch from the kitchen (USDA).

swaps.ranch: Not a blue cheese family? Use our buttermilk ranch.
swaps.vegetarian: The Worcestershire is optional. It usually contains anchovies, so leave it out for vegetarians and anyone avoiding fish.

items.title: Stovetop Queso Dip
items.subtitle: snack · about ¼ cup (makes about 2½ cups)
items.body: Silky, scoopable cheese dip from real cheese: evaporated milk and a little cornstarch keep it smooth, and tomatoes with green chiles give it a little kick.

steps: Toss the shredded cheeses with the cornstarch in a bowl. Shred your own; bagged cheese has an anti-caking coating that can make the dip grainy.
