Warm the evaporated milk in a saucepan over medium-low heat until steaming, not boiling.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, whisking until each addition melts before adding more. Keep the heat low; high heat makes cheese stringy.
Stir in the drained tomatoes and chiles, cumin, garlic powder and jalapeño. If it’s too thick, whisk in a splash of milk.
Serve warm with chips. To keep it hot through the game, hold it in a slow cooker on warm or low, at 140°F or above (USDA). Stir now and then, and add a splash of milk if it thickens.
equipment: slow cooker or small pot for keeping warm (optional)

swaps.beefy: Stir in ½ lb browned, drained ground beef or chorizo (cooked to 160°F).
swaps.mild: Use plain diced tomatoes and skip the jalapeño.

items.title: Baked Buffalo Chicken Dip
items.subtitle: snack · about ⅓ cup
items.body: All the flavor of Buffalo wings in a hot, creamy dip: shredded chicken with cream cheese, hot sauce, ranch and cheddar, baked until bubbling. Serve with celery, crackers or chips.

steps: Put the chicken in a saucepan, cover with water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover and simmer gently 15 to 18 minutes, until a food thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F (USDA). Cool a little and shred with two forks.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Stir the cream cheese, hot sauce and ranch until smooth, then mix in the chicken and 1 cup of the cheddar.
Spread in the baking dish and top with the rest of the cheese. Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges and hot in the center (165°F). Sprinkle with green onions.

Serve hot. To keep it hot through the game, hold it in a slow cooker on warm or low, at 140°F or above (USDA). Set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate it or swap in a fresh batch from the kitchen (USDA).

swaps.rotisserie: Use 3 cups shredded rotisserie chicken and skip step 1.
swaps.slow_cooker: Mix everything in a slow cooker and cook on low 2 hours, stirring once, until 165°F.

items.title: Loaded Sheet-Pan Nachos
items.subtitle: snack,dinner · about ⅛ of the pan
items.body: Tortilla chips spread on a sheet pan and layered twice with seasoned beef, black beans and melted cheese, then piled with fresh toppings so every chip gets some.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line the baking sheet with foil or parchment.

Brown the beef in a skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains and a food thermometer reads 160°F (USDA). Drain the fat. Stir in the taco seasoning and water and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until saucy.
Spread half the chips on the pan. Top with half the beef, half the beans and half the cheese. Repeat the layers.
Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Top with salsa, avocado, dollops of sour cream, jalapeños, green onions and cilantro. Serve right away, on the pan.

swaps.vegetarian: Skip the beef and use two cans of beans, one of them pinto, warmed with the taco seasoning.
swaps.chicken: Use shredded cooked chicken, or leftover buffalo chicken dip, in place of the beef.

items.title: Sheet-Pan Cheeseburger Sliders
items.subtitle: snack,dinner · 1 slider
items.body: One big seasoned patty baked in a pan, topped with cheese and tucked into a whole sheet of soft rolls, then brushed with butter and baked again. Twelve sliders with no flipping.

ingredients.prep: or other slider rolls, in one sheet

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line the baking sheet with parchment.
Mix the beef with the salt, pepper, onion powder and Worcestershire gently. Press it into an even rectangle on the pan, about the size of the sheet of rolls. Wash your hands.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until a food thermometer in the center reads 160°F (USDA). Carefully pour off the fat. Lay the cheese over the top and bake 1 minute to melt.

Slice the sheet of rolls in half sideways without separating them. Set the bottoms in the pan or on a clean sheet, spread with the sauce, and lift the cheesy patty onto them with two wide spatulas. Add the pickles and the tops.
Brush the tops with butter, sprinkle with sesame seeds and bake 5 to 8 minutes, until toasted. Cut into 12 sliders.

swaps.turkey: Use ground turkey and cook it to 165°F.

items.title: Meatball Sliders
items.subtitle: snack,dinner · 1 slider
items.body: Tender homemade meatballs simmered in marinara and tucked into soft rolls with melted mozzarella and a garlic-butter top. Make the meatballs ahead and the sliders take 15 minutes.

ingredients.prep: in one sheet, or slider buns

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet. Mix the meatball ingredients gently with your hands, then roll 12 balls, about 1½ inches. Wash your hands.
Bake the meatballs 15 to 18 minutes, until browned and a food thermometer in the center of one reads 160°F (USDA).
Warm the marinara in a saucepan and add the meatballs; simmer 5 minutes.

Lower the oven to 350°F. Slice the sheet of rolls in half sideways and set the bottoms in the baking dish. Space the meatballs on top with a little sauce, cover with the mozzarella and add the roll tops.
Stir the butter, garlic powder and parsley and brush it on the tops. Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the cheese melts and the tops are golden. Cut apart and serve with extra sauce.

swaps.shortcut: Use 24 small frozen cooked meatballs, heated in the sauce to 165°F.
swaps.turkey: Use ground turkey and bake the meatballs to 165°F.

items.title: Loaded Potato Skins
items.subtitle: snack,side · 2 skins
items.body: Baked potato halves scooped out, brushed with butter and baked crisp, then filled with cheddar and bacon and finished with sour cream and green onions.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Prick the potatoes with a fork and bake directly on the rack 50 to 60 minutes, until tender. Cool 10 minutes.
Meanwhile cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain and crumble.
Halve the potatoes lengthwise and scoop out most of the flesh, leaving a ¼-inch shell. (Save the flesh for mashed potatoes or potato soup.)
Raise the oven to 450°F. Brush the skins inside and out with butter, season with salt and pepper, and bake cut side up on a baking sheet 10 to 12 minutes, until crisp.
Fill with cheese and bacon and bake 5 minutes more, until melted. Top with sour cream and green onions.

swaps.vegetarian: Skip the bacon; add sautéed peppers and onions or chopped broccoli.

items.title: Puff Pastry Pigs in a Blanket
items.subtitle: snack · 3 pieces
items.body: Bite-size pieces of hot dog rolled in strips of flaky puff pastry, brushed with egg and baked golden. Serve with mustard and ketchup.

ingredients.prep: a 17-oz box, thawed in the refrigerator

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line the baking sheets with parchment.
Unfold each pastry sheet on a lightly floured counter and cut it into 18 strips, about 1½ inches wide and 3 inches long.
Roll a strip around each hot dog piece, seam side down on the sheet. Brush with egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until puffed and deep golden; the hot dogs will be steaming hot (165°F).
Cool 5 minutes and serve with mustard and ketchup. Set it out for no more than 2 hours, then refrigerate it or swap in a fresh batch from the kitchen (USDA).

swaps.dough: Use our from-scratch pizza dough or biscuit dough, cut in strips.
swaps.egg_free: Brush with milk instead of egg.

items.title: Baked Homemade Tortilla Chips
items.subtitle: snack · about 1 oz (8 chips)
items.body: Corn tortillas cut into wedges, brushed with a little oil and baked crisp. Lighter than fried and they taste of real corn.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds.
Brush both sides of the tortillas lightly with oil. Stack and cut into 6 wedges each.
Spread in one layer on the baking sheets and sprinkle with salt (and lime zest).
Bake 10 to 15 minutes, turning the chips and swapping the pans halfway, until crisp and lightly golden. They crisp more as they cool. Watch closely at the end; they go from golden to burnt quickly.

swaps.flour: Flour tortillas work too and bake a few minutes faster; they contain wheat.

items.title: Savory Oven Snack Mix
items.subtitle: snack · about ½ cup (makes 8 cups)
items.body: Crunchy oat and corn cereals, pretzels and cheese crackers tossed in seasoned butter and baked low until toasty. Nut-free as written, so it works for most crowds.

steps: Heat the oven to 250°F.
Put the cereals, pretzels and crackers in a large bowl. Stir the butter with the soy sauce and seasonings, drizzle it over and toss gently until everything is coated.
Spread in the roasting pan and bake 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.
Spread on paper towels to cool; it crisps as it cools. Store airtight.
equipment: large roasting pan or 2 rimmed baking sheets

swaps.nuts: If no one is allergic, add 1 cup peanuts or mixed nuts.
swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free cereals, pretzels and crackers, and tamari labeled gluten-free.

items.title: Tabbouleh
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 3/4 cup
items.body: The Lebanese parsley salad: lots of chopped parsley and mint with a little bulgur, tomatoes, cucumber and lemon.

steps: Pour the boiling water over the bulgur in a small bowl, cover and let stand 20 minutes, until tender. Drain off any extra water and fluff.
Wash and dry the herbs well; wet herbs make a soggy salad. Chop them finely.
Toss the bulgur, parsley, mint, green onions, tomatoes and cucumber with the lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper. Taste and add more lemon if you like.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 1 cup cooked quinoa instead of bulgur.

items.title: Beef and Barley Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Tender beef, pearl barley, mushrooms and vegetables in a rich broth. A cold-weather classic that feeds a crowd.

steps: Pat the beef dry and season with the salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in 2 batches, 5 minutes per batch. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion, carrots, celery and mushrooms 8 minutes, until the mushrooms brown. Add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Return the beef. Add the broth, thyme and bay leaves, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 1 hour.
Stir in the barley and simmer partly covered 35 to 45 minutes, until the beef and barley are tender. Remove the herb stems and bay leaves and stir in the parsley.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

swaps.gluten_free: Use brown rice instead of barley (add it for the last 40 minutes) and check the broth.

items.title: Mushroom Barley Risotto
items.subtitle: dinner,side · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: Pearl barley cooked slowly like risotto with browned mushrooms, shallots and Parmesan. Creamy, chewy and filling.

steps: Warm the broth in a small pot and keep it hot over low heat.

Heat 1 tablespoon butter and the oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms 8 to 10 minutes, until browned and the liquid is gone. Add the shallots, garlic and thyme and cook 2 minutes.

Stir in the barley for 1 minute. Add 1 cup hot broth and simmer, stirring often, until mostly absorbed. Keep adding broth 1 cup at a time, stirring often, until the barley is tender and creamy, 35 to 40 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the remaining butter, the Parmesan, salt, pepper and parsley.

swaps.gluten_free: Use arborio rice instead of barley; cook about 20 minutes.
swaps.dairy_free: Use oil instead of butter and skip the Parmesan.

items.title: Tomato Bulgur Pilaf
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: A Turkish-style side of bulgur cooked with onion, pepper and tomato paste. Quicker than rice and full of whole grain.

steps: Heat the oil and butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes, until soft. Stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the bulgur and paprika and stir 1 minute. Add the broth and salt and bring to a boil.
Cover, lower the heat and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed. Take off the heat, lay a towel under the lid and let stand 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork and stir in the parsley.

swaps.dairy_free: Use all olive oil.

items.title: Mediterranean Quinoa Salad
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: Quinoa, chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes and feta with parsley, mint and a lemon dressing. A meal-prep lunch that keeps for days.

steps: Rinse the quinoa well in a strainer. Bring it and the water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes, fluff and spread on a plate to cool.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the cooled quinoa with the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, feta, parsley, mint and dressing.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta and add olives.

items.title: Quinoa Black Bean Salad with Lime
items.subtitle: lunch,side · about 1 cup
items.body: Quinoa with black beans, corn, red pepper and lots of cilantro in a lime and cumin dressing.

steps: Bring the quinoa and water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes, fluff and cool.
Whisk the lime juice, oil, cumin, honey and salt in a large bowl.
Add the quinoa, beans, corn, pepper, onion, jalapeño and cilantro and toss.

items.title: Turkey and Quinoa Stuffed Peppers
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 pepper halves
items.body: Bell pepper halves filled with ground turkey, quinoa and marinara, topped with mozzarella and fresh basil.

ingredients.prep: halved through the stem, seeds removed

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Simmer the quinoa covered in the water 15 minutes.

Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the turkey and onion, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the turkey reaches 165°F. Add the garlic, Italian seasoning and salt for 30 seconds.
Stir in the quinoa, 1 1/2 cups marinara and the basil. Spread the rest of the sauce in the baking dish, set the peppers in it cut side up and fill them.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Uncover, top with the mozzarella and bake 10 to 15 minutes, until the peppers are tender and the filling is 165°F.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Use a can of black beans or white beans instead of the turkey.

items.title: Warm Cinnamon Quinoa Breakfast Bowls
items.subtitle: breakfast · about 1 cup
items.body: Quinoa simmered in milk with cinnamon and vanilla, like a hot cereal, then topped with berries and a drizzle of maple.

steps: Bring the quinoa, water, milk, cinnamon and salt to a simmer in a saucepan, watching that the milk does not boil over.
Cover and cook on low 15 to 18 minutes, until the quinoa is tender and creamy. Stir in the vanilla and maple syrup.
Spoon into bowls and top with berries and nuts if you like.

swaps.dairy_free: Use an unsweetened plant milk.

items.title: Edamame Quinoa Crunch Salad
items.subtitle: lunch,side · about 1 cup
items.body: Quinoa, edamame, red cabbage, carrots and cilantro in a ginger-sesame dressing. Crunchy and colorful, and it holds up all week.

steps: Bring the quinoa and water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes, fluff and cool.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the quinoa with the edamame, cabbage, carrots, pepper, green onions, cilantro and dressing.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

items.title: Moroccan-Spiced Chickpea Stew with Couscous
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/4 cups stew with 2/3 cup couscous
items.body: Chickpeas, sweet potatoes and carrots in a warmly spiced tomato broth with ginger and cinnamon, spooned over fluffy couscous.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and spices for 1 minute.
Add the sweet potatoes, carrots, tomatoes, chickpeas, broth, salt and raisins. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 20 to 25 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
For the couscous, bring the water, butter and salt to a boil. Stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork.
Stir the cilantro into the stew and serve over the couscous.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve over rice or quinoa instead of couscous.
swaps.dairy_free: Use oil instead of butter in the couscous.

meta.servings: about 1 1/4 cups stew with 2/3 cup couscous

items.title: Lemon Herb Couscous
items.subtitle: side · about 2/3 cup
items.body: Fluffy couscous with butter, lemon, parsley and mint. Ready in about 10 minutes.

steps: Bring the broth, butter and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and stir in the lemon zest, 2 tablespoons lemon juice, parsley, mint and green onions.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

items.title: Greek Chicken Couscous Bowls
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 bowl
items.body: Lemon-oregano chicken over couscous with cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, feta and a cool homemade tzatziki.

steps: Toss the chicken with the oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper. Refrigerate 30 minutes (or up to 8 hours).
Stir the tzatziki ingredients together and chill.
Bring the water and salt to a boil, stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side, until it reaches 165°F. Rest 5 minutes and slice.
Build bowls with couscous, chicken, cucumber, tomatoes, onion, feta and a spoon of tzatziki.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice or quinoa instead of couscous.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta and use a dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Roasted Vegetable Couscous
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 1 cup
items.body: Couscous tossed with roasted zucchini, eggplant, peppers and red onion, a little balsamic and fresh parsley.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the vegetables with the oil, salt and cumin and spread on 2 baking sheets. Roast 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once, until tender and browned at the edges.
Bring the water to a boil, stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff.
Toss the couscous with the vegetables, vinegar, oil and parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature.

swaps.gluten_free: Use quinoa instead of couscous.

items.title: Salmon with Lemon Dill Couscous
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 fillet with 3/4 cup couscous
items.body: Salmon baked with lemon and garlic, served on couscous loaded with fresh dill, lemon and peas.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Set the salmon on it, brush with the oil and garlic, season with salt and pepper and top with lemon slices.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 145°F in the thickest part.
Meanwhile, bring the broth, peas and butter to a boil. Stir in the couscous, cover, take off the heat and let stand 5 minutes. Fluff and stir in the dill and lemon juice.
Serve the salmon over the couscous.

swaps.gluten_free: Use quinoa instead of couscous and check the broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

items.title: Creamy Tuscan Chicken with Brown Rice
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 1/2 thighs with sauce and 3/4 cup rice
items.body: Browned chicken thighs in a garlicky cream sauce with spinach, roasted red peppers, rosemary, thyme and Parmesan, over brown rice.

steps: Bring the rice and water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 40 to 45 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken 4 minutes per side. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic, rosemary and thyme for 30 seconds, then the peppers and broth, scraping up the browned bits. Stir in the cream.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes, until it reaches 165°F. Pull out the herb stems.
Stir in the Parmesan and spinach until the spinach wilts and the sauce is creamy. Serve over the rice.

swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut milk instead of cream and skip the Parmesan.

meta.servings: 1 1/2 thighs with sauce and 3/4 cup rice

items.title: Wild Rice Pilaf with Cranberries and Pecans
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: A holiday-style side of wild and brown rice with shallots, thyme, dried cranberries and toasted pecans.

steps: Bring the wild rice, brown rice, broth and salt to a boil. Cover and simmer on low 45 to 50 minutes, until tender. Let stand 10 minutes, then drain off any extra liquid.
Meanwhile, toast the pecans in a dry skillet over medium heat 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. Move them to a plate.
Melt the butter in the skillet. Cook the shallots, celery and thyme 5 minutes, until soft.
Toss the rice with the shallot mixture, cranberries, pecans and parsley.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

items.title: Beef Stroganoff
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 cup over 1 cup noodles
items.body: Strips of sirloin and mushrooms in a creamy sour cream sauce over buttered egg noodles. Comfort food in 45 minutes.

ingredients.prep: trimmed and sliced thin across the grain

steps: Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over high heat. Sear the beef in 2 batches, about 1 minute per side, until browned outside and pink inside. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the butter. Cook the shallots and mushrooms 8 minutes, until browned. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the flour for 1 minute.

Whisk in the broth, Worcestershire and mustard and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until thick. Return the beef and its juices and simmer 2 minutes, until the beef reaches 145°F. Let it rest off the heat 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in boiling salted water by the package directions. Drain and toss with butter.
Stir the sour cream into the sauce off the heat (boiling makes it curdle). Add the parsley and serve over the noodles.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Use cornstarch instead of flour, gluten-free noodles, and check the Worcestershire label.
swaps.meatless: Skip the beef and use 1 1/2 pounds mushrooms with vegetable broth.

items.title: Chicken Paprikash
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 1/2 thighs with sauce and 1 cup noodles
items.body: The Hungarian favorite: chicken thighs simmered with onions and sweet paprika in a sour cream sauce, served over egg noodles.

steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken 3 minutes per side. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onions and pepper 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, paprika and flour and stir 1 minute; do not let the paprika scorch.
Add the tomatoes and broth and return the chicken. Cover and simmer 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in boiling salted water. Drain.
Move the chicken to a plate. Off the heat, stir a little hot sauce into the sour cream, then stir it all into the skillet. Return the chicken, sprinkle with parsley and serve over the noodles.

swaps.gluten_free: Use cornstarch instead of flour and serve over rice.
swaps.dairy_free: Use 1/2 cup coconut milk instead of sour cream.

meta.servings: 1 1/2 thighs with sauce and 1 cup noodles

items.title: Buttered Parsley Noodles
items.subtitle: side · about 1 cup
items.body: Egg noodles tossed with butter, fresh parsley and Parmesan. A simple side kids ask for.

steps: Cook the noodles in a large pot of boiling salted water by the package directions. Save 1/4 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Return the noodles to the pot with the butter and toss until melted. Add the parsley, Parmesan, pepper and a splash of cooking water and toss until glossy.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil and skip the Parmesan.

items.title: Tamale Pie
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 square (about 1/8 of the pan)
items.body: A chili-style beef and pinto bean filling baked under a golden buttermilk cornbread crust.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. In a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat, cook the beef, onion and pepper, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Drain extra fat.

Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and salt for 30 seconds, then the beans, tomatoes, corn and tomato sauce. Simmer 5 minutes. (Move it to a 9-by-13-inch dish now if your skillet cannot go in the oven.)
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. Stir in the buttermilk, egg and butter just until mixed, then fold in half the cheese.
Spoon the batter over the hot filling and spread it toward the edges. Sprinkle with the rest of the cheese.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until the topping is golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Let stand 5 minutes.
equipment: large ovenproof skillet or 9-by-13-inch baking dish

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend in the topping.
swaps.meatless: Use a second can of beans instead of the beef.

items.title: Shrimp and Cheddar Grits
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 cup grits with about 5 ounces shrimp
items.body: The Lowcountry favorite: creamy cheddar grits topped with garlicky shrimp, bacon and green onions.

steps: Bring the water, milk and salt to a simmer in a saucepan. Slowly whisk in the grits. Cook on low 5 to 7 minutes, whisking often, until thick. Stir in the cheese and butter; cover to keep warm.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 6 minutes. Lift out and leave 1 tablespoon fat in the pan.

Toss the shrimp with the paprika and pepper. Cook in the hot pan over medium-high heat 2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque all the way through. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the lemon juice, most of the green onions, the bacon and hot sauce.
Spoon the grits into bowls, top with the shrimp and sprinkle with the rest of the green onions.

swaps.dairy_free: Cook the grits in water and broth and skip the cheese and butter.

meta.servings: 1 cup grits with about 5 ounces shrimp

items.title: Creamy Polenta with Garlicky Mushrooms
items.subtitle: dinner,side · about 1 cup polenta with mushrooms
items.body: Soft, cheesy cornmeal polenta topped with mushrooms browned in butter with garlic and fresh thyme.

steps: Bring the water, milk and salt to a simmer in a heavy saucepan. Slowly whisk in the cornmeal. Lower the heat and cook 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often and scraping the bottom, until thick and creamy. Stir in the Parmesan and butter.

Meanwhile, heat the oil and butter in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms without stirring for 3 minutes, then stir and cook 5 minutes more, until browned. Add the garlic, thyme, salt and pepper for 1 minute. Stir in the parsley.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with the mushrooms.

swaps.dairy_free: Use water and olive oil and skip the cheese.

items.title: Jalapeño Cheddar Skillet Cornbread
items.subtitle: side · 1 wedge
items.body: Buttermilk cornbread baked in a hot skillet for crisp edges, with sharp cheddar and a little jalapeño.

steps: Put 1 tablespoon of the butter in the skillet and set it in the oven as it heats to 425°F.

Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt. In another bowl whisk the buttermilk, eggs and remaining melted butter. Stir into the dry ingredients just until mixed, then fold in the cheese and jalapeños.
Using oven mitts, take out the hot skillet, swirl the butter and pour in the batter. It should sizzle.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes before slicing.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.

items.title: Classic Potato Latkes
items.subtitle: side,dinner · 4 latkes (makes about 24)
items.body: Crisp, lacy-edged potato pancakes fried in oil, the best-known Hanukkah food in many Ashkenazi Jewish homes. Serve with applesauce, sour cream, or both.

ingredients.prep: for frying; about ¼ inch in the pan

steps: Heat the oven to 200°F and set a wire rack in a baking sheet. Frying safety: use a heavy pan, keep the oil below smoking (350 to 375°F), and never leave hot oil alone. Keep a lid or sheet pan beside the stove; if the oil catches fire, turn off the burner and slide the lid over it. Never pour water on a grease fire. Keep children back from the stove.
Grate the potatoes and onion on the large holes of a box grater or in a food processor, alternating them; the onion helps keep the potatoes from turning gray.

Squeeze the grated potatoes hard in a clean kitchen towel, a handful at a time, over a bowl. Dry potatoes make crisp latkes, and less water means less spattering oil. Let the squeezed-out liquid sit 5 minutes, pour off the water and keep the white potato starch at the bottom of the bowl.
Mix the potatoes and onion with the starch, eggs, flour, salt, pepper and baking powder.
Heat about ¼ inch of oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until a shred of potato sizzles right away (about 350 to 375°F).

Drop in heaping 2-tablespoon mounds, a few at a time without crowding, and flatten them to about 3 inches. Fry 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and crisp. Lower the heat if they brown too fast.

Drain briefly on paper towels, then move to the rack in the oven. Keep finished latkes warm and crisp in one layer on a wire rack set in a baking sheet in a 200°F oven while you fry the rest. Stir the batter between batches and add oil as needed, letting it heat back up.
Serve hot with applesauce and sour cream. When you’re done, turn off the burner and let the oil cool completely before throwing it away in a sealed container.
equipment: box grater or food processor with a grating disk
large heavy skillet (cast iron is ideal)
baking sheet with a wire rack

swaps.gluten_free: Use potato starch or a gluten-free flour in place of the flour or matzo meal.
swaps.egg_free: Leave out the eggs and add 2 more tablespoons flour; handle them gently.
swaps.kosher_meat_meal: For a meat meal, serve with applesauce instead of sour cream.

items.title: Sweet Potato Latkes
items.subtitle: side · 4 latkes (makes about 24)
items.body: Orange, slightly sweet latkes from grated sweet potato with a little cinnamon and green onion. They brown faster than potato latkes, so fry them over medium heat.

steps: Heat the oven to 200°F and set a wire rack in a baking sheet. Frying safety: use a heavy pan, keep the oil below smoking (350 to 375°F), and never leave hot oil alone. Keep a lid or sheet pan beside the stove; if the oil catches fire, turn off the burner and slide the lid over it. Never pour water on a grease fire. Keep children back from the stove.
Grate the sweet potatoes on the large holes. Squeeze them lightly in a towel; they hold less water than white potatoes.
Mix with the green onions, eggs, flour, salt, cinnamon and pepper.

Heat ¼ inch of oil over medium heat. Fry heaping 2-tablespoon mounds, flattened, 3 minutes per side, until browned and crisp at the edges. Sweet potatoes have more sugar and burn faster; turn the heat down if needed.
Drain on paper towels, then keep warm on the rack in the oven. Serve with sour cream and a drizzle of honey.
equipment: baking sheet with a wire rack

swaps.savory: Leave out the cinnamon and add ½ teaspoon cumin and some chopped cilantro.
swaps.gluten_free: Use potato starch instead of flour.

items.title: Zucchini and Carrot Latkes
items.subtitle: side,lunch · 3 latkes (makes about 18)
items.body: Light vegetable fritters with zucchini, carrot, a little potato and fresh dill. A colorful latke for a dairy meal with a yogurt dip.

steps: Toss the zucchini with 1 teaspoon of the salt in a colander and let it drain 10 minutes. Then squeeze the zucchini, carrot and potato very dry in a towel.

Frying safety: use a heavy pan, keep the oil below smoking (350 to 375°F), and never leave hot oil alone. Keep a lid or sheet pan beside the stove; if the oil catches fire, turn off the burner and slide the lid over it. Never pour water on a grease fire. Keep children back from the stove.
Mix the vegetables with the green onions, dill, eggs, flour, pepper and the remaining salt.
Heat ¼ inch of oil over medium-high. Fry 2-tablespoon mounds, flattened, 3 minutes per side until golden. Drain on paper towels and keep warm in a 200°F oven.
Stir the yogurt, garlic and lemon juice together for dipping.

swaps.dairy_free: Serve with applesauce instead of the yogurt dip.

items.title: Oven-Baked Sheet-Pan Latkes
items.subtitle: side · 4 latkes (makes about 24)
items.body: Latkes baked in a very hot oven on oiled pans: less oil, no spattering, and every batch done at once. Crisp edges with a softer middle.

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Pour 2 tablespoons of oil onto each baking sheet and tilt to coat. Heat the pans in the oven 5 minutes.
Grate the potatoes and onion. Squeeze the grated potatoes hard in a clean kitchen towel, a handful at a time, over a bowl. Dry potatoes make crisp latkes, and less water means less spattering oil.
Mix with the eggs, flour, salt and pepper.
Carefully take out the hot pans. Drop 2-tablespoon mounds on them, flatten to 3 inches, and brush the tops with the remaining oil.
Bake 15 minutes, until browned underneath. Flip, swap the pans between racks and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until crisp and golden.

swaps.gluten_free: Use potato starch instead of flour.

items.title: Sufganiyot (Jelly Doughnuts)
items.subtitle: snack · 1 doughnut (makes about 16)
items.body: Soft, yeasted doughnuts fried golden, filled with jam and dusted with powdered sugar. In Israel they are the Hanukkah treat; they take an afternoon, mostly waiting for the dough to rise.

steps: Stir the warm milk, yeast and 1 tablespoon of the sugar together; let stand 5 to 10 minutes until foamy.

Mix in the remaining sugar, the flour, salt, eggs, butter and vanilla. Knead 6 to 8 minutes (or 5 minutes with a dough hook) until soft, smooth and slightly tacky. Add a spoonful of flour only if it’s very sticky.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot 1 to 1½ hours, until doubled.
Roll the dough ½ inch thick on a floured counter and cut rounds. Set them on floured parchment, cover loosely and let rise 30 to 45 minutes, until puffy. Reroll the scraps once.

Frying safety: use a heavy pan, keep the oil below smoking (about 350°F), and never leave hot oil alone. Keep a lid or sheet pan beside the stove; if the oil catches fire, turn off the burner and slide the lid over it. Never pour water on a grease fire. Keep children back from the stove. Use a deep pot with oil about 2 inches deep and at least 3 inches of room above it.

Heat the oil to 350°F. Fry 3 or 4 doughnuts at a time, lowering them in gently by hand-holding the parchment edge or with the spider, 1½ to 2 minutes per side, until deep golden. Hotter oil browns the outside before the inside cooks; keep it near 350°F.
Drain on a rack. Tear the first one open to check that the center is cooked through, not doughy; fry the rest a little longer if needed.
When cool enough to handle, poke a hole in the side of each with a skewer or chopstick, wiggle it to make a pocket, and pipe in about 2 teaspoons of jam. Dust with powdered sugar.
Turn off the burner and let the oil cool completely before straining or throwing it away in a sealed container.
equipment: stand mixer with dough hook, or a large bowl
2½- to 3-inch round cutter or a glass
large heavy pot or Dutch oven
piping bag with a round tip, or a zip-top bag
a lid or sheet pan that covers the pot

swaps.baked: For a lower-oil version, bake the risen rounds at 375°F for 10 to 12 minutes, brush with melted butter and roll in sugar before filling; they’ll be softer and more like rolls.
swaps.fillings: Try lemon curd, chocolate spread or a thick vanilla custard.
swaps.dairy_free: Use water or oat milk and oil instead of milk and butter.

items.title: Bimuelos (Honey Fritters)
items.subtitle: snack · 4 fritters (makes about 32)
items.body: Light, puffy yeasted fritters drizzled with warm honey syrup and cinnamon, eaten at Hanukkah in many Sephardic Jewish families. No rolling or cutting: the batter goes straight into the oil by the spoonful.

steps: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt. Stir in the warm water to make a thick, sticky batter. Cover and let rise in a warm place about 1 hour, until doubled and bubbly.

Frying safety: use a heavy pan, keep the oil below smoking (about 365°F), and never leave hot oil alone. Keep a lid or sheet pan beside the stove; if the oil catches fire, turn off the burner and slide the lid over it. Never pour water on a grease fire. Keep children back from the stove. Use a deep pot with oil about 2 inches deep and plenty of room above it.
Heat the oil to 365°F. Wet two spoons and drop walnut-size blobs of batter into the oil, a few at a time. Fry 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until puffed and golden all over. Drain on the rack.
Warm the honey, water and lemon juice until runny. Drizzle over the fritters and dust with cinnamon. Serve warm.
Turn off the burner and let the oil cool completely before throwing it away.
equipment: a lid or sheet pan that covers the pot

swaps.sugar_syrup: Use simple syrup with a strip of orange peel instead of honey, or roll them in cinnamon sugar.

items.title: Onion-Braised Brisket
items.subtitle: dinner · about 4 oz sliced brisket with onions and gravy
items.body: A beef brisket browned and braised slowly on a thick bed of onions with tomato, garlic and broth until fork-tender. Like many braises, it tastes best made a day ahead, chilled, sliced and reheated in its gravy.

ingredients.prep: first cut (flat), with a thin layer of fat

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Pat the brisket dry and rub it all over with the salt, pepper and paprika. Wash your hands.
Heat the oil in the Dutch oven over medium-high and brown the brisket well, 5 to 6 minutes per side (cut it in half to fit if needed). Set it aside on a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the onions and cook, stirring and scraping up the browned bits, 12 to 15 minutes, until soft and golden. Stir in the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Stir in the broth, tomatoes, brown sugar, vinegar, bay leaves and thyme. Set the brisket fat side up on the onions, tuck the carrots around, and spoon some onions over the top.
Cover tightly and braise 3½ to 4 hours, until a fork slides in with almost no resistance. Beef is safe at 145°F (USDA); brisket is cooked far beyond that, near 200°F, to become tender.

Make it ahead (the usual way): cool the brisket in its liquid for up to an hour, then refrigerate it, covered, overnight. The next day lift off the hardened fat, slice the cold meat across the grain about ¼ inch thick, and lay the slices back in the gravy.
Reheat covered at 325°F for 45 to 60 minutes, until the gravy bubbles and the center slices reach 165°F. Pull out the bay leaves and thyme stems and serve with the onions and gravy.
Serving it the same day instead: rest the brisket 20 minutes, skim the fat from the gravy, then slice across the grain.
equipment: large Dutch oven or roasting pan with a tight lid (or heavy foil)

swaps.slow_cooker: Brown the meat and onions, then cook everything in a slow cooker on low 8 to 10 hours.
swaps.sweet_and_sour: Use ½ cup ketchup in place of the crushed tomatoes and add ¼ cup more brown sugar.

meta.servings: about 4 oz sliced brisket with onions and gravy

items.title: Crispy Potato Kugel
items.subtitle: side · 1 square (1/10 of a 9x13 pan)
items.body: A golden baked pudding of grated potatoes and sweet sautéed onions, crisp on top and at the edges and tender inside. Like latkes, but all in one pan.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Cook the chopped onion in 2 tablespoons of the oil until golden, about 10 minutes.
Pour 2 tablespoons of oil into the baking dish and put it in the oven to heat while you grate.
Grate the potatoes and the second onion. Squeeze them dry in a towel, a handful at a time.
Mix the potatoes with the cooked onion, eggs, flour, salt, pepper and the remaining oil.

Carefully take out the hot dish and spread the potato mixture in it; it should sizzle. Bake 60 to 75 minutes, until deep golden and crisp on top and a knife slides easily into the center (it reaches well past 160°F, done for an egg dish).
Let it rest 10 minutes and cut into squares.

swaps.gluten_free: Use potato starch instead of flour.

items.title: Carrot and Sweet Potato Tzimmes
items.subtitle: side · about ¾ cup
items.body: Carrots and sweet potatoes baked with dried apricots and raisins in orange juice and honey until glazed and tender. A sweet side that sits happily beside brisket.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Toss everything together in the baking dish.
Cover with foil and bake 40 minutes. Uncover, stir, and bake 20 to 25 minutes more, stirring once, until the vegetables are tender and glazed.

swaps.prunes: Prunes are a traditional addition; use them in place of the apricots.

items.title: Cheese Blintzes
items.subtitle: breakfast,dinner · 2 blintzes (makes 12)
items.body: Thin crepes wrapped around a lightly sweet ricotta and cream cheese filling, browned in butter. A favorite for a dairy meal at Hanukkah, served with sour cream and berries or applesauce.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the pan

steps: Blend the crepe ingredients until smooth and let the batter rest 30 minutes (or overnight in the refrigerator).

Heat the skillet over medium and brush with butter. Pour in about 3 tablespoons batter and swirl to coat the bottom thinly. Cook about 1 minute, until the top is set and the edge lifts; cook on one side only. Slide it out, browned side up, and repeat, stacking the crepes.
Mix the filling ingredients until smooth.
Spoon 2 tablespoons filling onto the browned side of each crepe near one edge. Fold in the sides, then roll up like a little package.

Heat the oven to 375°F. Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat and brown the blintzes seam side down first, 2 minutes per side. Move them to the baking dish and bake 10 to 12 minutes, until the filling is hot, 160°F, since it contains raw egg (USDA).
Serve warm with sour cream and berries or applesauce.

swaps.cottage_cheese: Use small-curd cottage cheese, drained and pressed through a strainer, in place of the ricotta.
swaps.fruit: Fill with thick cooked apples or cherries instead of cheese.

items.title: Leftover Brisket Sandwiches on Challah
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1 sandwich
items.body: The next day’s best meal: brisket slices warmed in their gravy and piled on thick slices of challah with a little horseradish and the sweet braised onions.

ingredients.prep: leftover onion-braised brisket, sliced, with ½ cup of its gravy and onions

steps: Warm the brisket slices in their gravy and onions in a covered pan over medium-low heat, 6 to 8 minutes, until steaming and 165°F (USDA).
Toast the challah lightly if you like. Spread with horseradish.
Pile on the brisket and onions, add greens or pickles, and close the sandwiches. Spoon a little gravy on top for dipping.

swaps.latke_sandwich: Use two latkes instead of bread for a latke-brisket sandwich.

items.title: Homemade Buttermilk Ranch
items.subtitle: snack,side · 2 tablespoons
items.body: Creamy ranch from buttermilk, sour cream and mayonnaise with fresh parsley, chives and dill. A dressing and a dip.

steps: Whisk the sour cream and mayonnaise until smooth, then whisk in the buttermilk.
Stir in the parsley, chives, dill, garlic, onion powder, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Chill at least 30 minutes so the flavors blend. Thin with more buttermilk for a dressing, or use less for a thick dip.
equipment: jar with lid or medium bowl

items.title: Garden Herb Cream Cheese Spread
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 2 tablespoons
items.body: Whipped cream cheese with fresh dill, chives, parsley and lemon. Spread it on bagels, crackers or cucumber sandwiches.

steps: Beat the cream cheese and yogurt with a spatula until smooth and fluffy.
Stir in the dill, chives, parsley, garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Chill 30 minutes before serving so the herbs flavor the spread.

items.title: Creamy Dill Potato Salad
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Red potatoes and hard-cooked eggs in a creamy sour cream and mayonnaise dressing with plenty of fresh dill.

steps: Put the potatoes in a pot, cover with cold water by an inch and add the salt. Bring to a boil and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain, toss with the vinegar while warm and cool 15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cover the eggs with water in a small pot, bring to a boil, then cover, take off the heat and let stand 12 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Cool in ice water, peel and chop.
Whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream, mustard, dill, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Fold in the potatoes, eggs, celery and onion. Chill at least 1 hour. Keep it cold; do not leave it out more than 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F).

items.title: Greek Lemon Chicken and Rice Soup (Avgolemono)
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Chicken and rice soup made silky with eggs and lemon, finished with fresh dill. Cozy and bright at the same time.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 minutes.

Add the broth, chicken, rice, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer covered 18 to 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the chicken reaches 165°F. Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice in a bowl. Slowly whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth, a little at a time, so the eggs warm without scrambling.
Turn the heat to low and stir the egg mixture into the pot. Cook, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes, until the soup thickens slightly and reaches 160°F. Do not let it boil. Stir in the dill.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.

items.title: Potato Leek Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A velvety blended soup of leeks, Yukon Gold potatoes, thyme and a little cream, topped with chives.

ingredients.prep: white and light green parts, sliced and well rinsed

steps: Leeks hide grit: slice them, then swish the slices in a big bowl of cold water and lift them out, leaving the sand behind.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the leeks 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until soft but not brown. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes, broth, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer 20 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender.
Remove the herbs. Blend until smooth (let it cool a bit first if using a countertop blender, and fill it only halfway). Stir in the cream and heat through. Top with chives.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil and skip the cream; the potatoes make it creamy.
swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.

items.title: Split Pea Soup with Ham
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A thick, smoky pot of green split peas, carrots and diced ham. It tastes even better the next day.

ingredients.prep: low-sodium if you can find it

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 to 8 minutes, until soft. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.

Add the split peas, ham, broth, water, thyme, bay leaf and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 60 to 75 minutes, stirring now and then so the peas do not stick, until they fall apart.
Pull out the thyme stems and bay leaf. For a smoother soup, mash some of the peas against the side of the pot. Taste, then add salt only if needed; the ham is salty.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the ham and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Skip the ham, use vegetable broth and add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika.

items.title: Yellow Split Pea Dal
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 cup dal with 3/4 cup rice
items.body: Golden split peas simmered soft with turmeric, then finished with onion, garlic, ginger and cumin. Mild enough for kids.

steps: Put the split peas, 5 cups water and turmeric in a large pot. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then simmer partly covered 40 to 45 minutes, stirring often, until the peas are very soft. Add water if it gets too thick.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in 2 1/4 cups water for 15 minutes. Let it stand off the heat 10 minutes.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 8 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander and cayenne for 1 minute.
Stir the onion mixture, tomatoes and salt into the peas and simmer 5 minutes. Add the lemon juice and cilantro. Serve over the rice.

swaps.dairy_free: Use oil instead of butter.

meta.servings: about 1 cup dal with 3/4 cup rice

items.title: Greek Yellow Split Pea Dip (Fava)
items.subtitle: snack,side · about 1/3 cup
items.body: A smooth, lemony spread made from yellow split peas, the way it is served in Greece. Eat it warm or cold with pita.

ingredients.prep: plus a little for the top

steps: Put the split peas, onion, garlic and water in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer partly covered 40 to 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and most of the water is absorbed.
Cool 10 minutes. Blend with the olive oil, lemon juice and salt until smooth. It thickens as it cools; blend in warm water a spoonful at a time if needed.
Spread in a shallow bowl. Top with red onion, parsley, capers if you like and a drizzle of oil.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with vegetables or gluten-free crackers instead of pita.

items.title: Split Pea and Barley Vegetable Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A hearty meatless soup of green split peas, pearl barley and vegetables. Thick, cheap and filling.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic, thyme and paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the split peas, barley, broth, water, bay leaf and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 60 to 70 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas break down and the barley is tender.
Remove the bay leaf, stir in the parsley and taste for salt. Add water if it is thicker than you like.

swaps.gluten_free: Use brown rice instead of barley and add it for the last 40 minutes.

items.title: Curried Split Pea and Sweet Potato Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Yellow split peas and sweet potatoes simmered with curry powder, ginger and coconut milk. Creamy without any cream.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the split peas and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered 30 minutes.
Add the sweet potatoes and simmer 15 to 20 minutes more, until the peas and potatoes are very soft.
Stir in the coconut milk. Blend or mash part of the soup for a thicker texture. Add the lime juice, salt and cilantro.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth and curry powder labels.

items.title: Chickpea Curry (Chana Masala)
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 cup curry with 3/4 cup rice
items.body: Chickpeas simmered in a spiced tomato and onion sauce, served over brown rice. Pantry staples, big flavor.

steps: Bring the rice and water to a boil, cover, lower the heat and simmer 40 to 45 minutes, until tender. Let stand 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 8 to 10 minutes, until deep golden. Add the garlic, ginger and jalapeño for 1 minute, then the cumin, coriander, paprika and turmeric for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, water and salt. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. Mash a few chickpeas to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the lemon juice and cilantro. Serve over the rice with yogurt if you like.

swaps.gluten_free: Already gluten-free; check spice labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the yogurt.

meta.servings: about 1 cup curry with 3/4 cup rice

items.title: Crispy Roasted Chickpeas
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/3 cup
items.body: Chickpeas roasted until crunchy and tossed with a little salt and smoked paprika. A crunchy snack with protein and fiber.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Pat the chickpeas very dry with a towel and pull off any loose skins.
Toss with the oil and spread in one layer on a baking sheet. Roast 25 to 30 minutes, shaking the pan every 10 minutes, until deep golden and crunchy.
Toss the hot chickpeas with the salt, paprika and garlic powder. Cool on the pan; they crisp more as they cool.

items.title: Smashed Chickpea Salad Sandwiches
items.subtitle: lunch · 1 sandwich
items.body: Mashed chickpeas with yogurt, celery and lemon, like a tuna salad without the tuna. Ready in 15 minutes.

steps: Mash the chickpeas in a bowl until mostly broken but still chunky.
Stir in the yogurt, mayonnaise, lemon juice, mustard, celery, onion, dill, salt and pepper.
Spread on 4 slices of bread, add lettuce and top with the other slices.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread or lettuce cups.
swaps.dairy_free: Use all mayonnaise instead of the yogurt.

items.title: Italian White Bean and Tuna Salad
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: Creamy white beans and canned tuna tossed with red onion, celery, parsley and a lemon vinaigrette. A pantry lunch with lots of protein.

steps: Shake the oil, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper in a jar.
In a large bowl, toss the beans, onion, celery, tomatoes and parsley with most of the dressing. Gently fold in the tuna in large flakes.
Serve over the greens with the rest of the dressing.

swaps.meatless: Use a third can of beans or chickpeas instead of tuna.

items.title: Garlicky White Bean and Herb Dip
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/4 cup
items.body: White beans blended with lemon, garlic, parsley and a little rosemary. Serve with vegetables, crackers or bread.

steps: Blend the beans, garlic, lemon juice, olive oil and water until smooth, scraping down the sides.
Add the parsley, rosemary, salt and pepper and pulse until the herbs are finely chopped. Add water if it is too thick.
Spoon into a bowl. It tastes best after 30 minutes in the fridge.

items.title: Creamy White Chicken Chili
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Chicken and white beans in a mild green chile broth, made creamy with sour cream and Monterey Jack.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and jalapeño 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add the green chiles, broth, chicken breasts and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the thickest part of the chicken reaches 165°F.
Lift out the chicken and shred it with 2 forks. Mash 1 can of the beans with a fork and add both cans of beans to the pot. Simmer 5 minutes.
Return the chicken. Off the heat, stir in the sour cream and cheese until melted. Add the cilantro and lime juice.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream and cheese and stir in 1/2 cup coconut milk.

items.title: Pasta e Fagioli
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: The Italian-American pasta and bean soup, with a little ground beef, two kinds of beans and small pasta in a tomato broth.

steps: Brown the beef in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Spoon off extra fat.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 minutes. Add the garlic and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, broth and both beans. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the pasta and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until tender. Add the pepper, taste for salt and stir in the basil. Serve with Parmesan.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta and check the broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.
swaps.meatless: Skip the beef and use vegetable broth.

items.title: Garden Minestrone
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A big pot of vegetables, beans and small pasta with fresh basil. Use whatever vegetables you have.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 to 8 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the zucchini, green beans, Italian seasoning, tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes.
Add both beans and the pasta. Simmer 8 to 10 minutes, until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Add the pepper, taste for salt and stir in the basil. Serve with Parmesan.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.

items.title: Red Beans and Rice
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 cup beans with 3/4 cup rice
items.body: A weeknight version of the Louisiana classic: red beans, smoked sausage, the "holy trinity" of onion, pepper and celery, and white rice.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the sausage 5 minutes; lift it out.
Cook the onion, pepper and celery in the drippings 8 minutes. Add the garlic, thyme, paprika and cayenne for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, broth, bay leaves, pepper and sausage. Simmer uncovered 30 to 35 minutes, stirring often and mashing some beans against the pot, until thick and creamy.
Meanwhile, bring the rice, water and salt to a boil, cover and simmer 18 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves. Stir in the green onions and parsley. Serve over rice with hot sauce at the table.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage, use vegetable broth and add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika.

meta.servings: about 1 cup beans with 3/4 cup rice

items.title: Three-Bean Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 3/4 cup
items.body: The picnic classic: green beans, kidney beans and chickpeas in a sweet-tart vinaigrette. It gets better as it sits.

ingredients.prep: drained (or 3 cups cooked fresh green beans)

steps: Put the beans, chickpeas, green beans, onion, pepper and parsley in a large bowl.
Shake the vinegar, oil, sugar, salt and pepper in a jar until the sugar dissolves.
Pour over the beans and toss. Cover and chill at least 1 hour, stirring once or twice.

items.title: Lentils and Rice with Caramelized Onions (Mujadara)
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: A Middle Eastern home dish of lentils and rice, piled with sweet browned onions and served with cool yogurt.

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onions and 1/4 teaspoon salt and cook 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown. Lower the heat if they brown too fast.
Meanwhile, put the lentils in a pot with water to cover by 2 inches. Boil 15 minutes, until just tender, then drain.
Return the lentils to the pot with the rice, cumin, salt, pepper, 3 3/4 cups water and half the onions. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low 18 to 20 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Fluff and top with the remaining onions and the parsley. Serve with yogurt.

swaps.dairy_free: Serve with a dairy-free yogurt, or skip it.

items.title: Seasoned Lentil Tacos
items.subtitle: dinner · 3 tacos
items.body: Lentils cooked with taco spices until they look and taste like a taco filling. Set out toppings and let everyone build.

steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and salt for 30 seconds, then stir in the tomato paste.

Add the lentils and broth. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are tender and most of the liquid is gone. Uncover and cook a few minutes more if it is soupy, mashing a little.
Spoon into warm tortillas and top with cheese, lettuce, tomato and cilantro.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream.
swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are usually gluten-free; check the label and the broth.

items.title: Lentil Salad with Feta and Herbs
items.subtitle: lunch,side · about 1 cup
items.body: Firm lentils tossed with cucumber, feta, parsley and mint in a shallot and mustard dressing. Packs well for lunch.

steps: Cover the lentils and bay leaf with water by 2 inches. Boil, then simmer 18 to 22 minutes, until tender but not mushy. Drain and remove the bay leaf.
While the lentils cook, shake the shallot, vinegar, mustard, oil, salt and pepper in a jar.
Toss the warm lentils with the dressing and let them cool 15 minutes; they soak it up.
Fold in the cucumber, tomatoes, feta, parsley and mint.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta or use a dairy-free crumble.

items.title: Lentil Sloppy Joes
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 sandwich
items.body: The sweet and tangy sandwich filling kids love, made with lentils instead of beef.

steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 6 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils and water. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 20 minutes, until the lentils are almost tender.
Stir in the tomato sauce, ketchup, sugar, vinegar, soy sauce, chili powder, mustard and salt. Simmer uncovered 10 to 12 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Spoon onto toasted buns.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns and tamari instead of soy sauce.

items.title: Black Bean Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: Canned black beans simmered with peppers, cumin and garlic, partly blended and topped with sour cream and cilantro.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, pepper and jalapeño 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add the beans, broth and salt. Simmer 10 minutes.
Blend about half the soup (or mash it well) so it is thick but still has whole beans. Stir in the lime juice.
Top each bowl with sour cream and cilantro.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream or use a dairy-free one.

items.title: Black Bean Burgers
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 burger
items.body: Hearty bean patties held together with oats and egg, browned in a skillet and finished in the oven.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Spread the beans on a baking sheet and bake 10 minutes to dry them a little. Cool slightly.

Mash the beans in a bowl, leaving some pieces. Pulse the oats in a blender until coarse and add with the egg, pepper, onion, garlic, cilantro, cumin, chili powder and salt. Mix well and shape into 6 patties.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Brown the patties 3 minutes per side.
Move to the baking sheet and bake 8 to 10 minutes, until firm and 160°F in the center. Serve on buns with lettuce and salsa.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free and gluten-free buns.

items.title: Charro Beans
items.subtitle: side,dinner · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Pinto beans simmered with bacon, onion, tomato and jalapeño in a savory broth, the way they are served at Tex-Mex cookouts.

steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, about 6 minutes. Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of fat.
Add the onion and jalapeño and cook 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes for 2 minutes.
Add the beans, broth, cumin, oregano and salt. Simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the broth is flavorful and a little thick. Stir in the cilantro.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.meatless: Skip the bacon, cook the onion in oil and use vegetable broth with 1/2 teaspoon smoked paprika.

items.title: Seven-Layer Bean Dip
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/2 cup
items.body: Refried beans, seasoned sour cream, guacamole, salsa, cheese, tomatoes and green onions in layers. A party favorite.

steps: Spread the refried beans in the dish.
Stir the sour cream and taco seasoning together and spread over the beans.
Mash the avocados with the lime juice and salt and spread on next. Spoon the salsa over, then sprinkle with cheese, tomato, green onions and olives.
Serve right away with chips, or cover and chill up to 4 hours.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the taco seasoning label; most corn tortilla chips are gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free sour cream and skip the cheese.

items.title: Edamame Succotash
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: A bright, colorful side of edamame, sweet corn and red pepper in butter with fresh basil. A new take on the Southern classic.

steps: Heat the butter and oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the edamame, corn and water. Cook, stirring, 5 to 6 minutes, until heated through and tender.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice. Stir in the basil.

swaps.dairy_free: Use all olive oil.

items.title: Sesame Garlic Edamame
items.subtitle: snack,side · about 1/2 cup
items.body: Shelled edamame warmed in a skillet with garlic, sesame oil and a splash of soy sauce. A snack ready in 10 minutes.

steps: Cook the edamame in a skillet with 1/4 cup water over medium-high heat, stirring, until the water is gone and they are hot, 4 to 5 minutes.
Add the sesame oil and garlic and stir 1 minute.
Add the soy sauce and sesame seeds and toss. Serve warm or cold.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

items.title: Peanut Noodles with Edamame
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Spaghetti tossed in a creamy peanut sauce with edamame, carrots, cucumber, green onions and cilantro. Eat warm or cold.

steps: Cook the spaghetti in a large pot of boiling salted water by the package directions. Add the edamame for the last 3 minutes. Drain and rinse with cool water.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and warm water until smooth.
Toss the noodles and edamame with the sauce, carrots, cucumber, green onions and cilantro.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice noodles or gluten-free spaghetti and tamari.

items.title: Teriyaki Tofu Rice Bowls
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 bowl
items.body: Golden pan-fried tofu in a homemade ginger teriyaki sauce over brown rice with edamame and broccoli.

ingredients.prep: firm, pressed and cut in 1-inch cubes

steps: Bring the rice and water to a boil, cover and simmer on low 40 to 45 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Wrap the tofu in a towel and press with something heavy for 15 minutes. Cut in cubes and toss with 2 tablespoons cornstarch.
Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning, 8 to 10 minutes, until golden on all sides. Move to a plate.
Add the broccoli, edamame and 1/4 cup water to the skillet, cover and steam 4 minutes. Move to the plate.
Whisk the sauce ingredients, pour into the skillet and simmer 1 minute, until glossy. Return the tofu and toss. Serve over rice with the vegetables and green onions.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

items.title: Crispy Baked Tofu Bites
items.subtitle: dinner,snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Tofu cubes tossed with soy, oil and cornstarch and baked until crisp. Dip them, toss them in sauce or add them to bowls.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Wrap the tofu in a towel and press under something heavy for 15 minutes, then cut into 3/4-inch cubes.
Toss the tofu with the soy sauce and oils, then sprinkle with the cornstarch and garlic powder and toss until coated.
Spread in one layer, not touching. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

items.title: Veggie Tofu Scramble
items.subtitle: breakfast · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Crumbled tofu cooked with onion, peppers and spinach and tinted gold with turmeric. A hearty egg-free breakfast.

steps: Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 5 minutes.
Crumble the tofu into the pan with your hands, in small and large pieces. Sprinkle with the turmeric, garlic powder, salt and pepper and cook, stirring, 5 minutes, until hot and a little dry.
Stir in the spinach until wilted. Top with cheese if you like and serve with toast.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with gluten-free toast.

items.title: Mapo-Style Tofu with Pork
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 cup with 3/4 cup rice
items.body: A family-friendly take on the Sichuan dish: soft tofu and ground pork in a savory garlic, ginger and bean sauce. Mild unless you add heat.

ingredients.prep: sliced, white and green parts separated

steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in 2 1/4 cups water for 15 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F.
Add the garlic, ginger, white parts of the green onions and pepper flakes and stir 1 minute. Stir in the hoisin, soy sauce and broth.
Slide in the tofu and simmer gently 5 minutes, spooning sauce over it without stirring hard. Mix the cornstarch and water, stir it in gently and simmer 1 minute, until glossy.
Drizzle with sesame oil, sprinkle with the green onion tops and serve over rice.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari and a gluten-free hoisin sauce.
swaps.meatless: Skip the pork and add 8 ounces chopped mushrooms.

items.title: Garlic Ginger Tofu and Broccoli Stir-Fry
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups with 3/4 cup rice
items.body: Browned tofu, broccoli and peppers in a quick garlic-ginger sauce over jasmine rice.

steps: Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered in 2 1/4 cups water for 15 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes.
Toss the pressed tofu with 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Heat 1 1/2 tablespoons oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the tofu on all sides, 8 minutes. Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, the broccoli, pepper and 2 tablespoons water. Cover and cook 3 minutes, then uncover and stir-fry 2 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Whisk the sauce ingredients, pour in and stir until thick, about 1 minute. Return the tofu, toss and serve over rice.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari instead of soy sauce.

items.title: Pork and Napa Cabbage Dumplings (Jiaozi)
items.subtitle: dinner · about 8 dumplings
items.body: Juicy pork and cabbage dumplings, folded together around the table and boiled or pan-fried as potstickers. In northern China they are the dish of New Year’s Eve.

ingredients.prep: about half a head, finely chopped
to draw water from the cabbage

steps: Toss the chopped cabbage with the salt and let it sit 15 minutes. Squeeze it hard in a towel, a handful at a time, to wring out as much water as you can. Dry cabbage keeps the filling from going soggy.
Mix the pork, cabbage, green onions, ginger, garlic, soy sauce, sesame oil, pepper and broth, stirring in one direction for a minute until sticky. Wash your hands and anything the raw pork touched.

Fold (see the folding guide on the Lunar New Year page): put a scant tablespoon of filling in the center of a wrapper, wet half the edge with water, fold it into a half moon and pinch the top. Make 3 or 4 pleats along one side, pressing each against the flat side, and seal well. Set them on the floured sheets, not touching. Keep unused wrappers covered.

To boil: bring a big pot of water to a rolling boil. Add 12 to 15 dumplings and stir gently so they don’t stick. When the water returns to a boil, add 1 cup cold water; do this twice more. When they float, puff and the wrappers turn glossy, about 6 to 8 minutes, they’re done. Lift one out and cut it open: the pork should be no longer pink and read 160°F.

For potstickers: heat 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium-high. Set the dumplings in flat side down and fry 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden. Add ⅓ cup water, cover right away (it spatters), and steam 6 to 8 minutes, until the water is gone and the filling reaches 160°F. Uncover and fry 1 more minute to recrisp.
Serve hot with dumpling dipping sauce.
equipment: large pot (to boil) or a nonstick skillet with a lid (for potstickers)

swaps.chicken: Use ground chicken or turkey; cook to 165°F.
swaps.shrimp: Use half pork and half chopped raw shrimp (adds shellfish).
swaps.homemade_wrappers: Make wrappers: stir 2 cups flour with about ¾ cup water to a firm dough, rest 30 minutes, roll into a rope, cut 24 pieces, and roll each into a 3½-inch circle. Double for this recipe.

items.title: Vegetable and Tofu Dumplings
items.subtitle: dinner · about 8 dumplings
items.body: A meatless filling of napa cabbage, mushrooms, carrots, tofu and rice noodles, seasoned with ginger and sesame. Most families make a vegetable batch alongside the pork one.

ingredients.prep: about half a head, finely chopped
to draw water from the cabbage
thin, soaked and chopped (optional but traditional)

steps: Salt the cabbage, wait 15 minutes, and squeeze it very dry in a towel.
Heat the oil and cook the mushrooms and carrots until their liquid cooks off, 6 to 8 minutes. Cool.
Mix the cabbage, mushrooms, carrots, tofu, noodles, green onions, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil and pepper.
Fold, then boil or pan-fry exactly as for the pork dumplings. These are done when the wrappers are tender and the filling is steaming hot, 5 to 6 minutes of boiling.
equipment: large pot or nonstick skillet with a lid

swaps.egg: Scramble 2 eggs, chop and mix in for a richer filling (adds eggs).
swaps.gluten_free: Use rice-paper or gluten-free wrappers and tamari.

items.title: Dumpling Dipping Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 2 tablespoons
items.body: Soy sauce, vinegar, a little sesame oil, ginger and garlic, with chili flakes if you like heat. Everyone mixes their own dish to taste.

steps: Stir the soy sauce, vinegar, water, sesame oil and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Add the ginger, garlic, chili flakes and green onion. Let it stand 10 minutes. Serve in little dishes.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari.

items.title: Longevity Noodles
items.subtitle: dinner,side · about 1½ cups
items.body: Long wheat noodles stir-fried with mushrooms, cabbage and green onions in a savory soy sauce. The noodles stay uncut: long strands stand for a long life.

ingredients.prep: dried, the longest you can find

steps: Cook the noodles as the package says, until just tender. Drain, rinse briefly with cold water so they don’t stick, and toss with a few drops of the sesame oil. Don’t cut or break them.
Stir the sauce ingredients together.
Heat the oil in the wok over high heat. Stir-fry the mushrooms 3 minutes, then the cabbage and carrot 2 minutes, then the garlic, ginger and green onions 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss with tongs, lifting high, until hot and evenly coated, 2 minutes. Serve the long strands piled on a platter.

swaps.chicken: Stir-fry ¾ lb thin-sliced chicken first, to 165°F, and take it out; add it back with the noodles.
swaps.gluten_free: Use rice noodles and tamari; check the hoisin label.

items.title: Steamed Whole Fish with Ginger and Scallions
items.subtitle: dinner · about ¼ of the fish
items.body: A whole fish steamed over ginger, topped with fresh scallions and cilantro, and finished with sizzling oil and soy sauce. The word for fish sounds like the word for “surplus,” so it’s served whole for a year of plenty.

ingredients.prep: 1½ lb, scaled and cleaned, head and tail on
2-inch piece, half sliced thin and half cut in fine shreds
2 cut in 3-inch lengths, 4 cut in fine shreds

steps: Rinse the fish inside and out under cold water and pat it dry. Cut 3 diagonal slashes, down to the bone, on each side so it cooks evenly. Rub with the salt.
Lay the ginger slices and the 3-inch green onion pieces on the plate and set the fish on top; tuck a few slices inside the belly. Bring 2 inches of water to a boil in the wok under the rack.

Set the plate on the rack, cover, and steam over high heat 10 to 14 minutes for a 1½-lb fish (about 8 minutes per inch at the thickest part). It’s done when the flesh at the thickest slash is opaque and flakes easily from the bone, 145°F on a thermometer (FDA). Lift the plate out carefully with a towel; the steam is very hot.

Pour off the steaming liquid and discard the cooked onion and ginger slices. Heat the soy sauce, water and sugar until the sugar dissolves and pour it around the fish. Pile the shredded ginger, shredded green onions and cilantro on top.
Heat the oil in the small saucepan until it shimmers. Standing back, pour it slowly over the green onions and ginger; it will sizzle and spit a little. Serve right away.

At the table, lift the top fillet off in pieces, then pull out the backbone in one piece to reach the bottom fillet, rather than flipping the fish (many families consider flipping it unlucky). Watch for small bones.
equipment: wok or wide pot with a lid
steaming rack, and a heatproof plate that fits inside with room around it

swaps.fillets: Use 1½ lb thick white fish fillets; steam 6 to 8 minutes, to 145°F.
swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari.

items.title: White Cut Chicken with Ginger-Scallion Sauce
items.subtitle: dinner · about ⅙ of the chicken, with sauce
items.body: A whole chicken poached gently until silky, chilled in ice water, cut into pieces and served with a fragrant ginger and scallion oil. Served whole on the table, it stands for family togetherness.

ingredients.group: For the poaching water (mostly not eaten)
For the poaching water (mostly not eaten)
For the poaching water (mostly not eaten)

steps: Take the giblets out of the chicken. Bring enough water to cover it to a boil in the stockpot with the ginger slices, green onions and salt.

Holding the chicken by the wings with tongs, lower it in, lift it out to drain the hot water from the cavity, and lower it again; do this twice so the inside heats evenly. Then submerge it, breast side down.

When the water returns to a gentle simmer, turn the heat to low and keep it just below a simmer, small bubbles only, for 40 to 50 minutes. Check the thickest part of the thigh and breast with a food thermometer: every spot must reach 165°F (USDA). If not, keep poaching and check every 5 minutes.

Lift the chicken into the ice water and chill 15 to 20 minutes; this tightens the skin and gives it its silky bite. Drain, brush with sesame oil, and refrigerate if not serving soon. Save the poaching liquid as broth.
For the sauce, put the chopped green onions, grated ginger and salt in a heatproof bowl. Heat the oil until it shimmers and pour it over carefully; it will sizzle. Stir.
Cut the chicken into pieces with a cleaver: legs, wings, then the breast through the bone into strips. Arrange it as a whole bird on the platter and serve at room temperature with the sauce.
equipment: large stockpot that holds the chicken covered with water

swaps.parts: Poach 3 lb bone-in thighs and breasts instead: about 25 to 30 minutes at a bare simmer, to 165°F.

meta.servings: about ⅙ of the chicken, with sauce

items.title: Lion’s Head Meatballs with Napa Cabbage
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 large meatball with cabbage and broth
items.body: Big, tender pork meatballs browned and then braised on a bed of napa cabbage. A dish from eastern China, often served at family celebrations; the round shape stands for reunion.

steps: Mix the pork, water chestnuts, green onions, ginger, egg, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, cornstarch, sugar and salt, stirring in one direction until sticky. Wet your hands and shape 6 large balls, tossing each from hand to hand to firm it.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat and brown the meatballs on all sides, about 8 minutes. They will still be raw inside.
Put half the cabbage in the pot, set the meatballs on top, and cover with the rest of the cabbage. Pour in the broth and 1 tablespoon soy sauce.
Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer gently 40 minutes, until the cabbage is silky and the center of a meatball reads 160°F.
Serve each meatball on a pile of cabbage with some of the broth.
equipment: Dutch oven or wide pot with a lid

swaps.egg_free: Leave out the egg and add 2 tablespoons water.

meta.servings: 1 large meatball with cabbage and broth

items.title: Garlic Stir-Fried Lettuce
items.subtitle: side · about ¾ cup
