items.body: Romaine hearts flashed in a hot wok with garlic until just wilted. In Cantonese the word for lettuce sounds like “growing wealth,” so it’s a New Year favorite.

ingredients.prep: or 1 head iceberg, cut in wide ribbons

steps: Wash the lettuce and dry it well; water makes the oil spatter.
Heat the oil in the wok over high heat. Add the garlic and stir 15 seconds until fragrant.
Add the lettuce and toss 1 to 2 minutes, just until it wilts but still has some crunch.
Add the soy sauce, sesame oil and sugar, toss, and serve at once.

swaps.oyster_sauce: Use 1 tablespoon oyster sauce instead of soy (adds shellfish).
swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari.

items.title: Buddha’s Delight (Vegetable Braise)
items.subtitle: dinner,side · about 1½ cups
items.body: A braise of napa cabbage, mushrooms, tofu, carrots, snap peas, water chestnuts and glassy noodles. Many Buddhist families eat it on the first day of the New Year, when some avoid meat.

ingredients.prep: firm, pressed and cut in cubes
about half a head, cut in 2-inch pieces

steps: Soak the noodles in hot water 10 minutes, drain and cut into shorter lengths with scissors.
Stir the sauce ingredients together.
Heat the oil in the wok and brown the tofu on two sides, 5 minutes; set aside. Stir-fry the mushrooms 3 minutes, then the garlic, ginger and carrot 1 minute.
Add the cabbage and water chestnuts, then the sauce. Cover and simmer 5 minutes until the cabbage wilts.
Add the snap peas, tofu and noodles and simmer 2 to 3 minutes, until the sauce thickens and everything is hot.
equipment: wok or large skillet with a lid

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari and check the hoisin label.

items.title: Crispy Vegetable Spring Rolls
items.subtitle: snack,side · 2 spring rolls
items.body: Thin, golden rolls filled with cabbage, carrots, mushrooms and rice noodles. Fried until crisp, they look like little gold bars, a wish for wealth in the new year.

ingredients.prep: thawed, kept under a damp towel
for frying (most stays in the pot)
about what the rolls soak up

steps: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the wok and stir-fry the cabbage, carrots and mushrooms 4 to 5 minutes, until wilted and dry. Add the green onions, ginger, soy sauce and sesame oil, then the noodles. Spread on a tray to cool completely; a warm filling tears the wrappers.

Lay a wrapper with a corner pointing at you. Put 2 tablespoons filling near that corner, fold the corner over, fold in the sides, and roll up firmly. Seal the last corner with a dab of the cornstarch paste. Keep finished rolls covered.

Heat 2 inches of oil in the heavy pot to 350°F. Fry safely: use a heavy pot no more than one-third full of oil, stay with it the whole time, and slide food in gently away from you. If the oil ever catches fire, slide a lid over the pot and turn off the burner; never use water (Los Angeles Fire Department).
Fry 4 or 5 rolls at a time, turning, 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden. Drain on paper towels. Let the oil come back to 350°F between batches.
Oven option, no deep frying: brush the rolls with oil and bake on a rack set on a sheet pan at 425°F for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once. They’re a little less crisp.
Serve with dumpling dipping sauce.
equipment: heavy pot for frying, and a deep-fry thermometer

swaps.pork: Add ½ lb ground pork, cooked to 160°F, to the filling.

items.title: Nian Gao (Brown Sugar Sticky Rice Cake)
items.subtitle: snack · 1 wedge (or 3 pan-fried slices)
items.body: A chewy, glossy cake of glutinous rice flour and brown sugar, steamed for an hour. Its name sounds like “higher year,” a wish for a better year ahead. Eat it in slices, or pan-fry them.

ingredients.prep: packed, dark if you have it
sweet rice flour, not regular rice flour

steps: Heat the brown sugar and water, stirring, until the sugar dissolves. Cool until just warm.
Put the rice flour in a bowl and slowly whisk in the syrup and the oil to a smooth, thick batter with no lumps.
Line the pan with oiled parchment. Pour in the batter and smooth it. Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

Set the pan on a rack in the wok over boiling water, cover, and steam 50 to 60 minutes, adding boiling water to the wok as needed. It’s done when a chopstick in the center comes out clean and the cake looks translucent.
Cool completely, then let it firm at least 4 hours or overnight before cutting. Oil your knife.

To pan-fry: cut into ¼-inch slices, dip in beaten egg if you like, and fry in a little oil until crisp outside and soft inside. Glutinous rice is very sticky and chewy. Cut it into small pieces for young children, and eat slowly.
equipment: wok or large pot with a rack and lid for steaming

swaps.dates: Press pitted red dates or chopped dates into the top before steaming.

items.title: Tangyuan: Black Sesame Rice Balls in Ginger Syrup
items.subtitle: snack · 4 rice balls with syrup
items.body: Soft, chewy glutinous rice balls filled with a sweet black sesame paste, served warm in ginger syrup. Their name sounds like “reunion”; families eat them on the Lantern Festival, the fifteenth day of the New Year.

ingredients.prep: softened, or lard or coconut oil
warm, plus a little more if needed

steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium-low, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes until fragrant. Cool, then grind with the sugar to a fine, damp powder. Mix in the butter to make a paste. Chill 30 minutes, then roll into 24 small balls (about 1 teaspoon each) and chill again.
Stir the warm water into the rice flour and knead to a smooth dough like soft clay. Add water by teaspoons if it cracks, or flour if sticky.
Roll the dough into a log and cut 24 pieces. Flatten one into a cup, set a ball of filling in it, pinch the dough closed, and roll smooth between your palms. Keep finished balls on the tray, covered.
Simmer the syrup water, ginger and brown sugar 10 minutes.
In another pot, bring water to a gentle boil. Add the balls and stir so they don’t stick. When they float, cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until soft all the way through.
Spoon them into bowls with the hot ginger syrup. Let them cool a minute: the filling is very hot. Glutinous rice is very sticky and chewy. Cut it into small pieces for young children, and eat slowly.

swaps.plain: Make small plain balls (no filling), tinted with a drop of food coloring, and serve in the syrup.
swaps.dairy_free: Use lard or coconut oil in the filling.
swaps.peanut: Use ground roasted peanuts instead of sesame (adds peanuts).

items.title: Sunflower Butter Banana Roll-Ups
items.subtitle: lunch,snack · 1 roll-up (cut in 4 pieces)
items.body: A tortilla spread with sunflower seed butter, rolled around a whole banana and sliced into pinwheels. Peanut-free and tree-nut-free, so it suits nut-free schools.

ingredients.prep: or peanut butter where nuts are allowed

steps: Spread 2 tablespoons of sunflower seed butter over each tortilla, almost to the edge. Drizzle with a teaspoon of honey and a pinch of cinnamon if you like.
Peel the bananas and cut each one in half crosswise. Lay a banana half near one edge of each tortilla.
Roll the tortilla up tightly around the banana. The spread holds it closed.
Slice each roll into 4 pinwheels with a sharp knife, or leave it whole and cut it in half. Pack the pieces snugly in a container so they don’t unroll.

swaps.nut_free: Sunflower seed butter is free of peanuts and tree nuts. Check the label for “made in a facility” warnings if your school asks.
swaps.apple: Use thin apple slices instead of banana.
swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free tortillas.

items.title: Ranch Chicken Lunch Wraps
items.subtitle: lunch · 1 wrap
items.body: Shredded chicken tossed with ranch, rolled up with crisp lettuce and cheddar. A good use for leftover roast or rotisserie chicken.

ingredients.prep: meat only, shredded (or leftover roast chicken)

steps: Use chicken that has been kept in the refrigerator and is no more than 3 to 4 days old (USDA). Toss the shredded chicken with the ranch.
Lay a lettuce leaf down the middle of each tortilla. Top with a quarter of the chicken, the cheddar and the tomatoes.
Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly from the bottom. Wrap each one in plastic wrap or foil, seam side down, and cut it in half on a slant.

Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free dressing and skip the cheese.
swaps.veggie: Use a drained can of chickpeas, lightly mashed, instead of chicken.

items.title: Pizza Pinwheels
items.subtitle: lunch,snack · 2 pinwheels (makes 12)
items.body: Pizza dough rolled up with sauce, mozzarella and pepperoni, sliced and baked. Good cold, which makes them a lunch box favorite.

ingredients.prep: about 1 lb, thawed in the refrigerator (or homemade)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment.
On a lightly floured counter, roll the dough into a rectangle about 10 by 14 inches. If it springs back, let it rest 5 minutes and try again.
Spread the sauce over the dough, leaving a 1-inch strip bare along one long edge. Sprinkle with the cheese and seasoning, and lay the pepperoni on top.
Starting from the long edge with sauce, roll the dough up tightly. Pinch the bare edge to seal it.
Cut the roll into 12 slices with a sharp knife and set them cut side up on the baking sheet. Brush the tops with oil.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until golden and the cheese bubbles. Cool on the pan.

Refrigerate within 2 hours. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).

swaps.veggie: Use diced bell peppers and spinach instead of pepperoni.
swaps.from_scratch: Use half a batch of the from-scratch pizza dough.

items.title: Cracker Stacker Lunch Box
items.subtitle: lunch · 1 lunch box
items.body: A homemade version of the store-bought cracker kits: crackers, cheese and turkey to stack, with cucumber and grapes on the side.

ingredients.prep: cut into squares the size of the crackers

steps: Slice the cheese into thin squares about the size of the crackers. Cut each turkey slice into 4 squares.
Slice the cucumber into rounds. For toddlers and preschoolers, cut grapes and cherry tomatoes into small pieces; whole, they are a choking hazard for young children (CDC).
In each divided container, put 6 crackers in one section (to keep them crisp, away from the wet foods), the cheese and turkey in another, and the cucumber and grapes in the rest.

Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice crackers.
swaps.veggie: Use hummus and extra cheese instead of turkey.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and add a dip such as hummus or white bean dip.

items.title: Nut-Free Sunflower Oat Energy Bites
items.subtitle: snack · 2 bites (makes 24)
items.body: No-bake oat bites held together with sunflower seed butter and honey, with mini chocolate chips. Made for nut-free classrooms.

steps: Stir the sunflower butter, honey and vanilla together in a bowl until smooth.
Add the oats, ground flaxseed, chocolate chips and salt. Stir until everything is coated. If it’s too sticky to roll, add a spoonful more oats.
Chill the bowl 20 to 30 minutes so the mixture firms up.
Roll into 24 balls about 1 inch across, with damp hands. Keep them in a covered container in the refrigerator.

swaps.nut_free: Sunflower seed butter keeps these free of peanuts and tree nuts. Check the chocolate chip label too.
swaps.dairy_free: Use dairy-free chocolate chips, or raisins.
swaps.honey: Use maple syrup; for children under 1 year, don’t use honey.

items.title: Mini Corn Dog Muffins
items.subtitle: lunch,snack · 3 mini muffins (makes 24)
items.body: Sweet cornbread batter baked around rounds of hot dog in a mini muffin pan. All the fun of a corn dog, no frying.

ingredients.prep: plus a little for the pan

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Grease the mini muffin cups well.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl. In another bowl, whisk the milk, egg and oil. Stir the wet into the dry just until no flour shows.
Spoon a tablespoon of batter into each cup and press a round of hot dog into the center of each.
Bake 13 to 15 minutes, until golden and a toothpick in the cornbread comes out clean. The hot dog in the center should reach 165°F (USDA).

Cool 5 minutes, then loosen with a butter knife. Refrigerate within 2 hours. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).

swaps.veggie: Use plant-based hot dogs, or corn kernels and cheddar instead.
swaps.dairy_free: Use any unsweetened plant milk.

items.title: Black Bean and Corn Quesadilla Triangles
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1 quesadilla (4 triangles)
items.body: Crisp tortillas folded around cheese, black beans and corn. Good warm for dinner and good cold in a lunch box the next day.

steps: Mash about half the beans with a fork, then stir in the rest of the beans, the corn and cumin.
Spread a quarter of the beans over 4 tortillas. Sprinkle with cheese and top with the other tortillas.
Heat a skillet over medium heat and brush it with a little oil. Cook one quesadilla at a time, 2 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts.

Cut each into 4 triangles. For lunches, cool them on a rack, refrigerate within 2 hours, and pack with a little salsa. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).

swaps.gluten_free: Use corn tortillas.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free cheese, or mash in avocado instead.

items.title: Hard-Cooked Eggs for the Week
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 egg
items.body: Six eggs cooked until the whites and yolks are firm, cooled fast and kept in the refrigerator for the week’s lunches.

steps: Set the eggs in a single layer in a saucepan and add cold water to cover them by 1 inch.
Bring to a full boil over high heat. Cover the pan, take it off the heat, and let the eggs stand 12 minutes for large eggs (15 for extra-large).
Lift the eggs into a bowl of ice water and leave them 5 minutes, until cool enough to hold.
Refrigerate them within 2 hours. Use hard-cooked eggs within 1 week, in or out of the shell (USDA). Peel them under running water when you need them.

Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).

swaps.deviled: Halve and fill them with the yolks mashed with mayonnaise and mustard; keep these cold too.

items.title: Strawberry Yogurt Bark
items.subtitle: snack · 2 pieces
items.body: Greek yogurt sweetened with a little honey, spread on a pan with strawberries, frozen and broken into pieces.

steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment. Stir the yogurt, honey and vanilla together.
Spread the yogurt on the parchment about ¼ inch thick. Scatter the strawberries and chocolate chips over it and press them in lightly.
Freeze at least 3 hours, until firm, then break it into about 16 pieces. Keep them in a freezer bag.
Pack a few pieces in a small container, frozen, next to the other cold foods. They soften by lunchtime; this is a cold food, not an ice pack, so still use two cold sources (USDA).

swaps.berries: Use blueberries, raspberries or diced mango.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a thick dairy-free yogurt.

items.title: Applesauce Oat Muffins
items.subtitle: snack,breakfast · 1 muffin
items.body: Soft, lightly sweet muffins made with applesauce, oats and cinnamon. Nut-free, and sturdy enough to ride in a backpack.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line a 12-cup muffin pan.
Whisk the flour, oats, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the applesauce, egg, oil and milk. Stir them into the dry ingredients just until combined, then fold in the raisins.
Divide among the cups and bake 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool on a rack.

swaps.dairy_free: Use any plant milk.
swaps.egg_free: Use 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed stirred into 3 tablespoons water, left 5 minutes.

items.title: Cucumber Cream Cheese Sandwiches
items.subtitle: lunch · 1 sandwich
items.body: Whole wheat bread with herby cream cheese and thin cucumber slices, cut into strips or triangles. Cool and crunchy.

steps: Stir the cream cheese with the dill.
Slice the cucumber thin and lay the slices on paper towels for a few minutes to soak up extra water, so the bread doesn’t get soggy.
Spread the cream cheese on all 8 slices of bread, edge to edge (it keeps the cucumber from wetting the bread). Layer cucumber on 4 slices, sprinkle with a little salt, and close the sandwiches.

Cut into triangles or strips. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).

swaps.dairy_free: Use hummus instead of cream cheese.
swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.

items.title: Mini Chicken Meatball Bites
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 5 mini meatballs (makes about 30)
items.body: Small, tender chicken meatballs with Parmesan and herbs. Pack them cold with a dip, or hot in a preheated insulated container.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment. Brush it with the oil.
Mix the chicken, breadcrumbs, egg, Parmesan, garlic powder, Italian seasoning and salt with your hands or a fork, just until combined. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Roll into about 30 balls, 1 inch across (wet hands help), and set them on the pan.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until lightly browned and a food thermometer reads 165°F in the center of a meatball (USDA).

Cool, then refrigerate within 2 hours. For a cold lunch, pack them with the marinara as a dip. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).
For a hot lunch, reheat them in sauce to 165°F, fill an insulated food jar that you have warmed with boiling water for a few minutes, and keep it closed until lunch (USDA).

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free breadcrumbs or quick oats.

items.title: Turkey, Apple and Cheddar Sandwiches
items.subtitle: lunch · 1 sandwich
items.body: Sliced turkey and sharp cheddar with thin, crisp apple slices on whole wheat. Sweet, salty and crunchy.

steps: Toss the apple slices with the lemon juice so they don’t turn brown.
Spread mayonnaise or mustard on 4 slices of bread. Layer 3 slices of turkey, a slice of cheddar and a few apple slices on each, and close with the other bread.

Cut in half and wrap. Pack it cold: in an insulated lunch bag with at least two cold sources, such as two frozen gel packs, or one gel pack and a frozen juice box or water bottle, one on top of the food and one under it (USDA).

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and add lettuce.
swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.

items.title: Hot Thermos Ravioli
items.subtitle: lunch · about 1 cup
items.body: Cheese ravioli in tomato sauce, packed piping hot in a preheated insulated food jar so it’s still warm at lunch.

steps: Cook the ravioli the night before as the package directs, drain, toss with the sauce, and refrigerate it within 2 hours. (Or cook it fresh in the morning.)
In the morning, fill each insulated food jar with boiling water, put the lid on, and let it stand a few minutes (USDA).
Meanwhile, reheat the ravioli and sauce on the stove until it is steaming hot and reads 165°F on a food thermometer.
Pour the water out of the jar, fill it with the hot ravioli, sprinkle with Parmesan and close the lid tightly. Keep it closed until lunch so the food stays at 140°F or above (USDA).
equipment: insulated food jar for each child
kettle or pot for boiling water

swaps.soup: The same thermos steps work for soup, chili or mac and cheese.

items.title: Beef and Broccoli
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups with rice
items.body: Takeout-style beef and broccoli in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce, on the table in half an hour.

steps: Toss the beef strips with 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 tablespoon soy sauce. Set aside while you make the sauce.
Whisk the sauce ingredients (soy sauce, broth, brown sugar, oyster sauce, cornstarch, sesame oil, garlic and ginger) in a bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the broccoli and water, cover and steam 3 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Move it to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil to the hot pan. Sear the beef in a single layer, in two batches if needed, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until browned. Thin strips cook fast and reach 145°F in this time.
Wash your hands and any board that held the raw beef. Return all the beef and the broccoli to the pan, whisk the sauce again and pour it in. Simmer 1 to 2 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Serve right away over rice.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce and a gluten-free oyster sauce and broth (check labels).
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces extra-firm tofu, pressed, cubed and browned, in place of the beef.

items.title: Philly-Style Cheesesteaks
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 sandwich
items.body: Thin-sliced steak, soft onions and peppers and melted provolone piled into toasted rolls.

steps: Wrap the steak and freeze it 20 minutes so it firms up. Slice it as thin as you can across the grain, trimming off large pieces of fat.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and pepper 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and lightly browned. Move them to a bowl.

Raise the heat to medium-high and add the rest of the oil. Add the steak in a single layer (in batches if needed) and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Cook 3 to 4 minutes, turning and chopping with the spatula, until browned with no pink left. Thin slices pass 145°F quickly; check a thicker piece with a thermometer.

Wash your hands and the board that held the raw steak. Stir the vegetables back in and divide the filling into 4 piles in the pan. Lay 2 slices of provolone over each pile and let it melt, about 1 minute.
Butter the cut sides of the rolls and toast them in a second pan or under the broiler. Slide a spatula under each pile and turn it into a roll.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Serve the filling over rice or in gluten-free rolls.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the cheese and butter.

items.title: Grilled Steak with Chimichurri
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 ounces steak with sauce
items.body: Sirloin seared hot and topped with a bright Argentine-style parsley, garlic and vinegar sauce.

steps: Stir together the parsley, garlic, oregano, vinegar, olive oil, pepper flakes and 1/4 teaspoon salt. Let it stand while you cook so the flavors blend.
Pat the steak dry and season both sides with the kosher salt and pepper. Rub with the oil.
Heat the grill or a heavy skillet over high heat. Cook the steak 4 to 6 minutes per side, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reads at least 145°F.
Move the steak to a clean board and let it rest 3 minutes or more before slicing. Slice across the grain.
Spoon the chimichurri over the sliced steak.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.meatless: Grill thick slices of portobello mushroom or cauliflower and spoon the chimichurri over them.

items.title: Country-Fried Steak with Cream Gravy
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 steak with gravy
items.body: Crisp breaded cube steaks and a peppery milk gravy, a Southern diner classic made at home.

steps: In one shallow dish, mix the flour, salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika. In another, beat the eggs with 1/2 cup milk.
Pat the steaks dry. Dip each in the flour, then the egg, then the flour again, pressing so the coating sticks. Wash your hands.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat until it shimmers. Fry the steaks 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and an instant-read thermometer reads 145°F. Move them to a rack over a baking sheet and let them rest at least 3 minutes; keep them warm in a 200°F oven if you like.
Pour off all but about 3 tablespoons of the fat, keeping the browned bits. Whisk in 3 tablespoons flour and cook 1 minute over medium heat.
Slowly whisk in 2 cups milk. Simmer 3 to 5 minutes, whisking, until thick. Season with pepper and salt.
Serve the steaks with the gravy spooned over.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Use a 1-to-1 gluten-free flour blend for the coating and the gravy.

items.title: Beef Bulgogi Rice Bowls
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 bowl
items.body: Korean-style sweet and savory marinated beef, seared fast and served over rice with crunchy vegetables.

steps: Firm the steak in the freezer for 20 minutes, then slice it as thin as you can.
In a bowl, mix the soy sauce, brown sugar, grated pear, sesame oil, garlic, ginger, half the green onions and the pepper. Add the beef, toss and marinate in the fridge 30 minutes or up to 8 hours.
Cook the rice while the beef marinates.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat. Add the beef in a single layer, in batches, letting extra marinade drip off. Cook 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until browned and caramelized at the edges. Thin slices pass 145°F quickly; check a thicker piece with a thermometer.
Throw away the leftover marinade. Wash your hands and the board that held the raw beef.
Fill bowls with rice, beef, cucumber and carrot. Top with the rest of the green onions and the sesame seeds.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.
swaps.meatless: Marinate and sear thin slices of extra-firm tofu or mushrooms instead.

items.title: Slow Cooker Beef Barbacoa
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1/2 cup meat
items.body: Chuck roast slow-cooked in a tangy chile and spice sauce until it shreds, for tacos, burritos and bowls.

steps: Season the beef chunks with the salt and put them in the slow cooker.
Blend the onion, garlic, green chiles, vinegar, lime juice, chili powder, cumin, oregano, cloves and broth until smooth. Pour over the beef and tuck in the bay leaves.
Cover and cook on low 8 to 9 hours or high 5 to 6 hours. The beef is safe at 145°F, but chuck shreds only after long cooking, when a fork twists through it easily.
Remove the bay leaves. Shred the beef with two forks right in the cooker and stir it into the juices.
Warm the tortillas and serve the beef with cilantro, onion and lime wedges.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are naturally free of wheat; check the broth label.

items.title: Braised Beef Short Ribs
items.subtitle: dinner · about 2 short ribs with sauce
items.body: Short ribs browned and slow-braised in broth with vegetables until the meat falls off the bone.

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Pat the ribs dry and season with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the ribs well on all sides in batches, 8 to 10 minutes per batch. Move them to a plate and pour off all but 2 tablespoons of fat.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery 5 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir 1 minute.

Stir in the broth, vinegar and Worcestershire, scraping up the browned bits. Return the ribs, bone side up, with any juices. Add the thyme and bay leaves. The liquid should come most of the way up the ribs.
Cover and bake 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the meat is very tender and pulls from the bone. The ribs pass 145°F early; the long cook is for tenderness.
Lift out the ribs. Skim the fat from the sauce and simmer it on the stove 5 to 10 minutes to thicken. Remove the thyme stems and bay leaves and spoon the sauce over the ribs.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free Worcestershire sauce and broth (check labels).

items.title: Vegetable Beef Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: An old-fashioned pot of tender beef, potatoes and garden vegetables in a tomato broth.

steps: Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in two batches, about 5 minutes per batch. Wash your hands after handling the raw meat.
Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, broth, water, thyme and bay leaves and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover and simmer 1 hour, until the beef is starting to get tender. It passes 145°F early; the simmer is for tenderness.
Add the potatoes and simmer 20 minutes. Add the green beans, corn and peas and simmer 10 minutes more, until everything is tender.
Remove the bay leaves, taste and add salt if needed.
equipment: large soup pot or Dutch oven

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label; everything else is naturally free of wheat.

items.title: Bacon-Wrapped Pork Tenderloin
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 ounces
items.body: Two lean tenderloins wrapped in bacon and brushed with a brown sugar and mustard glaze.

ingredients.prep: about 1 1/4 lb each, silver skin trimmed

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a rack on it if you have one.
Pat the tenderloins dry and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder. Wrap each one in 4 strips of bacon, overlapping slightly, and tuck the ends underneath. Wash your hands.
Stir the brown sugar and mustard together and brush it over the bacon.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the pork reads 145°F. For crisper bacon, broil 2 to 3 minutes at the end, watching closely.
Let the pork rest 5 minutes (at least 3), then slice.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Check the mustard and bacon labels.

items.title: Smothered Pork Chops
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 chop with gravy
items.body: Bone-in pork chops browned, then simmered in a rich onion and mushroom gravy.

steps: Pat the chops dry. Season with the salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder, then dredge lightly in 1/4 cup flour. Wash your hands.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chops 3 minutes per side. Move them to a plate; they finish cooking later.
Lower the heat to medium and add the butter, onions and mushrooms. Cook 10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in 2 tablespoons flour and stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth and milk, add the thyme and simmer until it starts to thicken.
Nestle the chops and their juices into the gravy. Cover and simmer gently 12 to 15 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part away from the bone reads 145°F.
Let the chops rest 3 minutes in the pan, then serve with plenty of gravy.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Use cornstarch: skip the dredge, and stir 1 tablespoon cornstarch into the milk to thicken the gravy.

items.title: Crispy Pork Schnitzel
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 cutlet
items.body: Boneless chops pounded thin, breaded and pan-fried golden, served with lemon in the German style.

steps: Lay each chop between sheets of plastic wrap and pound to about 1/4 inch thick. Season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Set out three shallow dishes: flour; the eggs beaten with the water; and breadcrumbs. Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing lightly. Wash your hands.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until a pinch of crumbs sizzles. Fry 2 cutlets at a time, 2 to 3 minutes per side, until deep golden and an instant-read thermometer reads 145°F.
Drain on a rack or paper towels and let rest 3 minutes. Repeat with the rest, adding a little oil if the pan looks dry.
Serve with lemon wedges for squeezing and a sprinkle of parsley.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free flour and crushed gluten-free crackers or crumbs.

items.title: Crispy Pork Carnitas
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1/2 cup meat
items.body: Pork shoulder slow-cooked with orange, lime and spices, then shredded and broiled until the edges crisp.

steps: Mix the salt, cumin, oregano and pepper and rub it all over the pork. Put the pork in the slow cooker with the onion, garlic and bay leaves. Wash your hands.

Pour the orange juice, lime juice and broth over the pork and drop in the squeezed orange halves. Cover and cook on low 8 to 10 hours or high 5 to 6 hours. Pork is safe at 145°F, but shoulder shreds only after long cooking, when a fork twists through it easily.
Lift out the pork and throw away the orange halves and bay leaves. Shred the meat with two forks, discarding large pieces of fat. Skim the fat from the juices.

Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below it. Spread the pork on a rimmed baking sheet and drizzle with 1/2 cup of the juices. Broil 5 to 8 minutes, until the edges are browned and crisp. Stir, add a little more juice and broil a few minutes more if you like.
Serve in warm tortillas with cilantro, onion, lime and salsa.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas are naturally free of wheat; check the broth label.

items.title: Oven Baby Back Ribs
items.subtitle: dinner · about 4 ribs
items.body: Low and slow in the oven with a sweet dry rub, then brushed with barbecue sauce and broiled sticky.

steps: Heat the oven to 275°F. Line two baking sheets with foil.
Pat the ribs dry. On the bone side, slide a butter knife under the thin membrane at one end, grab it with a paper towel and pull it off. This step is optional but makes the ribs more tender.
Mix the rub and pat it all over both racks. Set each rack meaty side up on a baking sheet and cover tightly with foil. Wash your hands.
Bake 2 1/2 hours, until the meat is tender and pulling back from the bone ends. Ribs pass 145°F long before they are tender.
Uncover and carefully pour off the juices. Heat the broiler. Brush the ribs with barbecue sauce and broil 3 to 5 minutes, watching closely, until sticky and browned in spots.
Rest 3 minutes, then cut between the bones and serve with more sauce.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Check the barbecue sauce label.

items.title: Garlic Herb Pork Loin Roast
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 ounces with vegetables
items.body: A garlic, rosemary and mustard crusted pork loin roasted over potatoes and carrots for an easy Sunday dinner.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Pat the pork dry.
Mix the garlic, rosemary, thyme, mustard, 2 tablespoons oil, salt and pepper into a paste and rub it over the pork. Wash your hands.
Toss the potatoes, carrots and onion with 1 tablespoon oil and 1/2 teaspoon salt in the roasting pan. Set the pork in the middle, fat side up.
Roast 60 to 75 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the center of the roast reads 145°F. Stir the vegetables halfway through.
Move the roast to a board and let it rest 10 minutes (at least 3). If the vegetables need more color, keep roasting them while the meat rests.
Slice the pork and serve with the vegetables and pan juices.
equipment: large roasting pan or rimmed baking sheet

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Check the mustard label.

items.title: Pressed Cuban Sandwiches
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1 sandwich
items.body: Roast pork, ham, Swiss cheese, pickles and mustard pressed in a hot skillet until crisp. A great use for leftover pork roast.

ingredients.prep: or a loaf of Cuban or French bread cut in 4
cooked and thinly sliced (leftover roast works well)

steps: Split the rolls and spread mustard on both cut sides.
Layer each sandwich with a slice of cheese, the pork, the ham, the pickles and another slice of cheese. Close the sandwiches and butter the outsides.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Set the sandwiches in the pan and press them down with a second heavy pan. Cook 4 to 5 minutes per side, pressing firmly, until the bread is crisp, the cheese melts and the center reaches 165°F.
Cut each sandwich in half on the diagonal and serve hot.
equipment: second heavy pan or foil-wrapped brick for pressing

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free rolls and check the ham and mustard labels.

items.title: Pork Meatball Banh Mi
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 sandwich
items.body: Vietnamese-style sandwiches: juicy pork meatballs, quick-pickled carrots, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño in a crusty roll.

steps: Stir the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved. Add the carrots and set aside at least 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with foil.
Mix the pork, green onions, garlic, ginger, fish sauce, sugar and panko with your hands just until combined. Roll into 16 balls about 1 1/2 inches across and set them on the sheet. Wash your hands.
Bake 15 to 18 minutes, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center of a meatball reads 160°F.
Toast the bread lightly and spread the insides with mayonnaise. Fill each with 4 meatballs (halve them if you like), drained pickled carrots, cucumber, cilantro and jalapeño.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs, fish sauce and bread, or serve the meatballs over rice.

items.title: Egg Roll in a Bowl
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: All the flavor of an egg roll filling, made in one skillet with ground pork and shredded cabbage.

steps: Cook the pork in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, about 7 minutes. Spoon off extra fat.
Add the sesame oil, onion, garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the coleslaw mix and carrot. Cook 4 to 5 minutes, tossing, until the cabbage wilts but still has some crunch.
Stir in the soy sauce and vinegar. Top with green onions, and hot sauce for anyone who wants it.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari or a gluten-free soy sauce.
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces crumbled extra-firm tofu, browned in 1 tablespoon oil.

items.title: Swedish Meatballs over Egg Noodles
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 meatballs with noodles
items.body: Tender beef and pork meatballs with a hint of allspice in a creamy gravy, spooned over buttered noodles.

steps: In a large bowl, soak the panko in the milk for 5 minutes. Add the beef, pork, egg, onion, salt, pepper, allspice and nutmeg and mix gently with your hands. Roll into about 30 balls, 1 1/4 inches across. Wash your hands.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the meatballs in batches, turning, about 8 minutes per batch, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F. Move them to a plate.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in salted boiling water by the package directions. Drain and toss with 1 tablespoon butter and the parsley.
Pour off the fat from the skillet. Melt 3 tablespoons butter, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth and simmer 3 minutes, until thickened.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the sour cream and Worcestershire. Return the meatballs and warm gently over low heat, without boiling, until hot.
Serve the meatballs and gravy over the noodles.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs, flour and Worcestershire, and serve over rice or mashed potatoes.

items.title: Thai-Style Pork Lettuce Wraps
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 3 to 4 wraps
items.body: Inspired by Thai larb: ground pork tossed with lime, fish sauce, shallot and lots of fresh mint and cilantro.

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, 6 to 7 minutes.
Add the shallots and garlic and cook 1 minute. Take the pan off the heat.
Stir the lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and pepper flakes together and pour over the pork. Toss in the cilantro, mint and green onions.
Spoon into lettuce leaves and serve with cucumber slices.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the fish sauce label.

items.title: Loaded Baked Potato Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Creamy potato soup topped like a baked potato with bacon, cheddar, sour cream and green onions.

steps: Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Lift it out onto paper towels, leaving about 2 tablespoons of fat in the pot.
Add the onion and cook 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth, then add the potatoes. Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are very tender.
Mash some of the potatoes right in the pot for a thick, chunky soup. Stir in the milk, salt and pepper and heat until steaming; do not let it boil hard.
Ladle into bowls and top with bacon, cheddar, sour cream and green onions.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed into the milk in place of the flour; check the broth and bacon labels.

items.title: Ham and Cheddar Quiche
items.subtitle: breakfast,lunch,dinner · 1 wedge
items.body: A creamy custard filled with diced ham and sharp cheddar in a flaky crust. Good warm or at room temperature.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Fit the crust into the pie plate and crimp the edge. Set it on a baking sheet.
Whisk the eggs, half-and-half, salt, pepper and nutmeg in a bowl.
Scatter the ham, cheese and green onions in the crust. Pour the egg mixture over.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until the center is just set and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F. If the crust edge browns too fast, cover it with strips of foil.
Let the quiche stand 10 minutes before cutting.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free crust, or bake it crustless in a greased pie plate for about 35 minutes.

items.title: Scalloped Potatoes and Ham
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: Thin-sliced potatoes and diced ham baked in a creamy cheddar sauce. A smart way to use up holiday ham.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter the baking dish.

Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion 4 minutes. Whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in the milk. Simmer, whisking, until thickened, about 5 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the salt, pepper, mustard and 1 cup of the cheese.
Layer half the potatoes in the dish, scatter the ham over and pour on half the sauce. Repeat with the rest of the potatoes and sauce.
Cover with foil and bake 50 minutes. Uncover, sprinkle with the rest of the cheese and bake 20 to 25 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the top is golden. The center should reach 165°F.
Let stand 10 minutes before serving.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3 tablespoons cornstarch in place of the flour, whisked into cold milk; check the ham label.

items.title: Brown Sugar Glazed Spiral Ham
items.subtitle: dinner · about 4 ounces
items.body: A fully cooked spiral ham warmed slowly and finished with a brown sugar, mustard and orange glaze. Plenty for a crowd and for leftovers.

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F. Set the ham cut side down in the pan and add the water. Cover tightly with foil so it does not dry out.
Bake 12 to 14 minutes per pound, about 1 1/2 hours for a 7-pound ham, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part, not touching bone, reads 120°F.
Meanwhile, simmer the glaze ingredients in a small saucepan 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until slightly thick.

Raise the oven to 400°F. Uncover the ham, brush it all over with half the glaze, letting some run between the slices, and bake 10 minutes. Brush with the rest and bake 5 to 10 minutes more, until glossy and the ham reaches 140°F.
Let it rest 10 minutes, then cut along the bone to release the slices. Spoon the pan juices over.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the ham and mustard labels.

items.title: Herb-Roasted Turkey Breast
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 ounces
items.body: A bone-in turkey breast with garlic herb butter under the skin. Thanksgiving flavor without the whole bird, and plenty of leftovers.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. If the turkey was frozen, thaw it in the fridge, allowing about 1 day per 4 to 5 pounds.
Mash the butter with the garlic, rosemary, thyme, sage, salt and pepper.
Pat the turkey dry. Gently loosen the skin with your fingers and spread half the butter under it, right on the meat. Rub the rest over the skin. Wash your hands.
Scatter the onion in the pan, set the turkey on top (on a rack if you have one) and pour in the broth.
Roast 1 3/4 to 2 1/4 hours, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part, not touching bone, reads 165°F. If the skin browns too fast, tent it loosely with foil.
Let the turkey rest 15 minutes before carving so the juices settle. Slice the meat off the bone, then across the grain.
equipment: roasting pan with rack, or a 9-by-13-inch pan

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil in place of butter.

items.title: Creamy Turkey Wild Rice Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A Minnesota-style creamy soup with nutty wild rice, vegetables and leftover roast turkey.

ingredients.prep: cooked, skin and bone removed, diced (about 3 cups; leftover roast turkey works)

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots, celery and mushrooms 8 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth, then add the wild rice, thyme and pepper.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, cover and simmer 45 to 55 minutes, until the rice is tender and some grains have split open.
Stir in the turkey and half-and-half and heat until the soup is steaming and reaches 165°F. Do not let it boil hard after the cream goes in. Taste and add salt if needed.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into the half-and-half in place of the flour; check the broth label.

items.title: Turkey Tetrazzini
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A creamy, cheesy baked spaghetti with turkey, mushrooms and peas, the classic answer to holiday leftovers.

ingredients.prep: cooked, skin and bone removed, diced (about 3 cups; leftover roast turkey works)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and butter the baking dish. Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water 2 minutes less than the package says; drain.
Melt 4 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion 8 minutes, until browned and soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth and milk and simmer, whisking, until thick, about 5 minutes. Season with salt, pepper and thyme.
Off the heat, stir in the turkey, peas, 1/2 cup Parmesan and the spaghetti. Spread in the dish.
Mix the panko, melted butter and the rest of the Parmesan and sprinkle over. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until bubbling, golden on top and 165°F in the center.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free spaghetti, flour and crumbs, and check the broth.

items.title: Turkey Club Sandwiches
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · 1 triple-decker sandwich
items.body: Triple-decker toast stacked with roast turkey, ham, crisp bacon, lettuce and tomato.

ingredients.prep: cooked and thinly sliced (leftover roast turkey works well)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Lay the bacon on a foil-lined baking sheet and bake 15 to 18 minutes, until crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread and spread one side of each slice with mayonnaise.
For each sandwich: top a slice of toast with turkey and ham, then a second slice, mayo side up. Add 2 strips of bacon, lettuce and tomato, and finish with a third slice, mayo side down.
Push 4 toothpicks into each sandwich and cut it into 4 triangles with a serrated knife. Remove the toothpicks before giving it to young children.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread and check the bacon and ham labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Mayonnaise has no milk; check the bread label.

items.title: Turkey Cobb Salad
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · about 3 cups
items.body: Rows of turkey, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese over crisp romaine with a mustard vinaigrette.

ingredients.prep: cooked, skin and bone removed, diced (leftover roast turkey works well)

steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 12 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Cool in ice water, then peel and chop.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain and crumble.
Shake the vinegar, mustard, salt, pepper and oil in a jar.
Spread the romaine on a platter. Arrange the turkey, bacon, eggs, avocado, tomato and blue cheese in rows on top. Sprinkle with chives.
Drizzle with some of the dressing and pass the rest.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the bacon and mustard labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the blue cheese.

items.title: Lamb Kofta Pitas with Yogurt Sauce
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 2 kofta in a pita
items.body: Middle Eastern-style spiced lamb skewers or patties with fresh herbs, tucked into warm pita with cucumber yogurt sauce.

steps: Stir the yogurt, cucumber, garlic, lemon juice and salt together and chill.

Mix the lamb, onion, garlic, parsley, mint, spices, salt and pepper with your hands until well combined. Shape into 8 long ovals about 4 inches long (around skewers if you have them). Wash your hands.
Heat the grill or broiler to medium-high. Cook the kofta 10 to 12 minutes, turning a few times, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Tuck 2 kofta into each warm pita with tomato, onion and a big spoonful of yogurt sauce.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve over rice or salad instead of pita.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt, or hummus, for the sauce.
swaps.meatless: Use falafel or grilled vegetables in the pitas.

items.title: Greek Lamb Burgers with Feta
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 burger
items.body: Juicy lamb patties seasoned with oregano and garlic, topped with feta, cucumber and a lemony yogurt spread.

steps: Stir the yogurt, lemon juice and dill together.
Mix the lamb, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper gently with your hands. Shape into 4 patties about 3/4 inch thick with a dimple in the center. Wash your hands.
Heat the grill or skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Toast the buns. Spread with the yogurt sauce and build the burgers with lettuce, a patty, feta, cucumber and onion.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns or wrap in lettuce.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta and use mayonnaise with lemon and dill for the spread.

items.title: Moussaka
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 square (about 3 by 4 inches)
items.body: The Greek layered bake: roasted eggplant, a cinnamon-scented lamb and tomato sauce, and a thick golden white sauce on top.

ingredients.prep: about 1 pound each, sliced 1/3 inch thick

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Brush the eggplant slices with the oil, lay them on two baking sheets and sprinkle with salt. Roast 20 to 25 minutes, turning once, until soft and browned. Lower the oven to 350°F.

Meanwhile, cook the lamb and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off the fat. Add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, oregano, cinnamon, salt and pepper and simmer 15 minutes, until thick.

For the white sauce, melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer, whisking, until thick, about 5 minutes. Off the heat, whisk in the nutmeg and salt, then the egg, quickly so it does not scramble, and half the Parmesan.
Layer half the eggplant in the baking dish, then all the meat sauce, then the rest of the eggplant. Spread the white sauce over the top and sprinkle with the rest of the Parmesan.
Bake 40 to 45 minutes, until golden on top and 165°F in the center. Let it rest 20 minutes before cutting so the layers set.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into the cold milk in place of the flour.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans of drained lentils in place of the lamb.

items.title: Lamb Keema with Peas
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 cup with rice
items.body: A homey South Asian-style dish of spiced ground lamb, tomato and green peas, ready for rice or warm naan.

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 6 to 8 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the lamb and raise the heat to medium-high. Cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F, about 7 minutes. Spoon off extra fat.
Stir in the curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cayenne and salt and cook 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and water. Cover and simmer 10 minutes. Stir in the peas and simmer 3 minutes more.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the yogurt. Top with cilantro and serve with rice or naan.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with rice.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the yogurt or use a dairy-free one.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans of drained lentils or chickpeas in place of the lamb.

items.title: Rosemary Garlic Lamb Chops
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 chops
items.body: Loin chops marinated in rosemary, garlic and lemon, then seared hot for a special but easy dinner.

steps: Mix the oil, garlic, rosemary, lemon juice and mustard in a shallow dish. Add the chops and turn to coat. Let stand 30 minutes at room temperature, or refrigerate up to 8 hours.
Season the chops with the salt and pepper.
Heat a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chops 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 145°F.
Move them to a clean plate and let rest 3 minutes. Serve with lemon wedges.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

swaps.gluten_free: Check the mustard label.

items.title: Baked Turkey Meatballs
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 meatballs
items.body: Tender, Parmesan-flecked turkey meatballs baked on a sheet pan. Serve with marinara over pasta or in subs.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with foil and oil it lightly.
In a large bowl, soak the panko in the milk 5 minutes. Add the turkey, egg, Parmesan, garlic, parsley, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper and mix gently with your hands.
Roll into about 30 balls, 1 1/2 inches across (wet hands help), and set them on the sheet. Wash your hands.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until browned and an instant-read thermometer in the center of a meatball reads 165°F.
Warm the marinara in a large pot, add the meatballs and simmer a few minutes. Serve over pasta or in rolls.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs and check the marinara label.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the Parmesan and use unsweetened plant milk.

items.title: Turkey White Bean Chili
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A mild green chili with ground turkey, white beans, corn and cumin, topped with cheese and a squeeze of lime.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook the turkey, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 165°F, about 8 minutes.
Add the onion and jalapeño and cook 5 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, oregano, chili powder and salt and stir 1 minute.
Add the green chiles, beans and broth. Mash some of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the chili. Bring to a boil, lower the heat and simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the corn and simmer 5 minutes more. Stir in the lime juice.
Top bowls with cheese and cilantro.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese; top with avocado.

items.title: Juicy Turkey Burgers
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 burger
items.body: Lean ground turkey kept moist with grated onion and Worcestershire, grilled or pan-cooked.

steps: Mix the turkey, grated onion, Worcestershire, panko, garlic powder, salt and pepper gently with your hands. The mixture will be soft.
Shape into 4 patties about 3/4 inch thick with a dimple in the center. Wash your hands.

Brush the grill grate or skillet with the oil and heat over medium. Cook the patties 6 to 7 minutes per side, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 165°F. Turkey needs a little more cooking than beef, so go by the thermometer.
Add the cheese for the last minute and cover to melt. Toast the buns and build the burgers.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free crumbs, Worcestershire and buns.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the cheese.

items.title: Homemade Nut and Seed Granola
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · about 1/2 cup
items.body: Crunchy oven granola with almonds, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, flax and dried cranberries.

steps: Heat the oven to 325°F and line the baking sheet with parchment.
Mix the oats, almonds, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, flaxseed, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
Warm the maple syrup and oil together for 20 seconds, stir in the vanilla, and pour over the oats. Stir until everything is coated.
Spread on the sheet and press down lightly. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once halfway, until golden.
Cool completely on the pan without stirring, about 30 minutes, so it forms clusters. Break up and stir in the cranberries.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.nut_free: Use more pumpkin and sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

items.title: Homemade Trail Mix
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/3 cup
items.body: Peanuts, cashews, almonds, seeds and raisins, mixed your way. A sturdy snack for hikes and car trips.

steps: Stir everything together in a bowl.
Portion into snack bags or keep in a jar.

swaps.nut_free: Use only sunflower and pumpkin seeds, plus pretzels and dried fruit.

items.title: Oatmeal Raisin Walnut Cookies
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie
items.body: Chewy, cinnamon-spiced oatmeal cookies loaded with raisins and walnuts.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line the baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter and both sugars until creamy. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt, then the oats, raisins and walnuts.
Scoop rounded tablespoons 2 inches apart on the sheets. Bake one sheet at a time, 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centers look a little soft.
Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then move to a rack. Do not taste the raw dough; it has raw egg and flour.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend and oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.nut_free: Leave out the walnuts.

items.title: Moroccan-Style Chicken with Apricots and Chickpeas
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups with couscous
items.body: Chicken thighs simmered with warm spices, dried apricots and chickpeas, served over couscous with toasted almonds.

steps: Season the chicken with the salt. Heat the oil in the pan over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in two batches, about 5 minutes each. Move to a plate. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion 5 minutes, then the garlic, ginger, cumin, cinnamon, paprika and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth, chickpeas and apricots and scrape up the browned bits. Return the chicken with its juices.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes, until the chicken is tender and a thermometer reads 165°F. Stir in the lemon juice.
Meanwhile cook the couscous. Serve the chicken over couscous, topped with almonds and cilantro.
equipment: large deep skillet or Dutch oven with lid

swaps.gluten_free: Serve over rice or quinoa instead of couscous, and use gluten-free broth.
swaps.nut_free: Leave off the almonds.

items.title: Date and Cashew Energy Bites
items.subtitle: snack · 1 bite
items.body: No-bake bites of dates, cashews, oats, chia and flax rolled in coconut. Naturally sweet.

steps: Check the dates for pits. If they are dry, soak them in hot water 10 minutes, then drain.
Pulse the cashews and oats in the food processor until finely chopped.
Add the dates, chia, flax, cocoa, vanilla and salt. Process until the mixture holds together when pressed, adding a teaspoon of water if needed.
Roll into 1-inch balls and roll in coconut if you like. Chill 30 minutes to firm up.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of cashews.

items.title: Cashew Chicken
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/4 cups with rice
items.body: Tender chicken, bell pepper and roasted cashews in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce, faster than takeout.

steps: Start the rice. Whisk the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.

Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, stirring, 5 to 6 minutes, until browned and a thermometer reads 165°F. Move to a plate. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Add the rest of the oil. Stir-fry the pepper and onion 3 minutes, then the garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce, add it with the chicken and cook 1 to 2 minutes, until thick. Stir in the cashews and green onions. Serve over rice.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari and a gluten-free hoisin.
swaps.nut_free: Use roasted sunflower seeds or leave the nuts out.

items.title: Curry Chicken Salad with Grapes and Cashews
items.subtitle: lunch · about 2/3 cup
items.body: Shredded chicken in a light curry yogurt dressing with grapes, celery and cashews. Great in a wrap or on greens.

steps: Stir the yogurt, mayonnaise, curry powder, lemon juice, honey and salt in a large bowl.
Add the chicken, grapes, celery and green onions and stir to coat.
Fold in the cashews just before serving. Eat on greens, in wraps or on bread.

swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of cashews.
swaps.gluten_free: Serve on greens or gluten-free bread.

items.title: Asian Chicken Salad with Mandarins and Almonds
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner · about 2 1/2 cups
items.body: Crunchy cabbage and romaine with chicken, mandarin oranges, toasted almonds and sesame seeds in a sesame-ginger dressing.

steps: Toast the almonds and sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes, until golden. Cool.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the cabbage, romaine, carrots, chicken and green onions with the dressing.
Top with the mandarin oranges, almonds and sesame seeds.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari.
swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

items.title: Homemade Hummus
items.subtitle: snack,side · about 1/4 cup
items.body: Smooth, lemony hummus from canned chickpeas and tahini in 10 minutes. Better than store-bought and cheaper.

steps: Process the tahini and lemon juice 1 minute, until thick and pale.
Add the garlic, cumin and salt and process 30 seconds.

Add the chickpeas and process 1 minute. With the machine running, add the cold water a tablespoon at a time until very smooth, about 2 minutes. Add a splash of the saved chickpea liquid if it is too thick.
Spread in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and dust with paprika. Serve with vegetables or pita.

items.title: Cold Sesame Noodles
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner,side · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Chilled noodles in a creamy tahini, soy and ginger sauce with crisp cucumber, carrots and sesame seeds.

steps: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water according to the package. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and warm water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, then add the cucumber, carrots and green onions.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds. Serve cold or at room temperature.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice noodles and tamari.
swaps.meatless: It is already meatless; add cubed tofu or shredded chicken for more protein.

items.title: Roasted Cauliflower with Lemon Tahini Sauce
items.subtitle: side · about 1 cup
items.body: Deeply browned cauliflower drizzled with a creamy lemon-garlic tahini sauce and parsley.

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F.
Toss the cauliflower with the oil, cumin, salt and pepper and spread on the baking sheet with space between the pieces.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until deeply browned at the edges and tender.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt. Whisk in water until it pours like thick cream.
Drizzle the sauce over the warm cauliflower and sprinkle with parsley.

items.title: Pecan-Crusted Chicken Tenders
items.subtitle: dinner · about 4 tenders
items.body: Chicken tenders coated in ground pecans and panko and baked crisp. Serve with honey mustard.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Set the rack on the baking sheet and coat it with cooking spray.
Pulse the pecans in the food processor until they look like coarse crumbs. Mix with the panko, paprika and garlic powder in a shallow dish.
Put the flour in a second dish. Whisk the eggs and 1 tablespoon mustard in a third.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Dip each tender in flour, then egg, then press into the pecan mix. Set on the rack and spray the tops lightly. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until golden and a thermometer in the thickest tender reads 165°F.
Stir the honey, mustard and mayonnaise (if using) together for dipping.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free flour and gluten-free panko.
swaps.nut_free: Use all panko and add 2 tablespoons parmesan.

items.title: Sweet Potato Casserole with Pecan Topping
items.subtitle: side · about 2/3 cup
items.body: Creamy mashed sweet potatoes under a crunchy brown sugar pecan streusel. A holiday side for any time.

steps: Cover the sweet potatoes with water in the pot and boil 15 to 18 minutes, until very tender. Drain well.
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease the baking dish.
Mash the sweet potatoes, then beat in the butter, brown sugar, eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until smooth. Spread in the dish.
Mix the pecans, brown sugar, flour and melted butter and sprinkle over the top.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the topping is golden and the center reaches 165°F.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend in the topping.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free butter.
swaps.nut_free: Use rolled oats instead of pecans.

items.title: Pumpkin Oat Muffins with Pumpkin Seeds
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 muffin
items.body: Spiced pumpkin muffins with oats and ground flax, topped with crunchy pumpkin seeds.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line the muffin tin.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, oil, brown sugar and vanilla in a large bowl.
In another bowl mix the flour, oats, flax, baking soda, baking powder, spice and salt. Stir into the pumpkin mixture just until combined.
Fill the cups and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds and sugar, pressing lightly.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend and oats labeled gluten-free.

items.title: Sunflower Crunch Chopped Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Romaine, red cabbage, carrots and cucumber chopped small with sunflower and pumpkin seeds in a lemon-parmesan dressing.

steps: Rinse and dry the romaine, cabbage and cucumber.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Chop the vegetables into small, even pieces and put them in a large bowl.
Toss with the dressing and top with the seeds just before serving.

swaps.dairy_free: Leave out the parmesan.

items.title: Peanut Sweet Potato Stew
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A West African-style stew of sweet potatoes, chickpeas and greens in a creamy tomato and peanut butter broth.

steps: Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander and cayenne and cook 1 minute.
Add the sweet potatoes, tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of the hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pot with the chickpeas.
Add the kale and simmer 5 minutes, until wilted. Stir in the salt and lime juice.
Serve over rice if you like, topped with chopped peanuts.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free broth.

items.title: Classic Peanut Butter Cookies
items.subtitle: snack · 1 cookie
items.body: Soft, chewy peanut butter cookies with the classic fork crisscross on top.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line the baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the peanut butter, butter and both sugars until creamy. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking soda and salt until a soft dough forms.
Roll into 1-inch balls and set 2 inches apart. Press each with a fork twice to make a crisscross.
Bake one sheet at a time, 9 to 11 minutes, until just set at the edges. Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then on a rack. Do not taste the raw dough; it has raw egg and flour.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seed butter; the cookies may turn a little green inside, which is harmless.

items.title: Lemon Cod with Rice and Asparagus
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 fillet, 1 cup of rice and a quarter of the asparagus
items.body: Mild white fish and asparagus roasted on one pan while the rice cooks. The simplest fish plate there is.

ingredients.prep: about 6 oz each, thawed if frozen
half juiced, half cut in wedges

steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer. Bring it to a boil with the water and ¼ teaspoon of the salt, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it stand, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment or foil.
Toss the asparagus with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a pinch of salt and spread it on one side of the pan. Roast 5 minutes.

Pat the cod dry and set it on the other side of the pan. Mix the butter, the rest of the oil, the garlic and the lemon juice and spoon it over the fish. Sprinkle the fish with the rest of the salt and the pepper.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork and the thickest part reads 145°F on a food thermometer.
Divide the rice, cod and asparagus among 4 plates. Add a lemon wedge and parsley.

swaps.dairy_free: Use 1 more tablespoon of olive oil instead of butter.
swaps.other_fish: Any mild white fish works: haddock, pollock, tilapia or halibut. Thin fillets cook faster.

meta.servings: 1 fillet, 1 cup of rice and a quarter of the asparagus

items.title: Chicken, Sweet Potato and Broccoli Sheet Pan
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 piece of chicken with a quarter of the vegetables
items.body: Seasoned chicken breast, sweet potato cubes and broccoli roasted together. A classic plate for packing lunches.

ingredients.prep: boneless, skinless, cut into 4 pieces of even thickness
peeled or scrubbed, in ¾-inch cubes

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with racks in the upper and lower thirds.
Toss the sweet potatoes with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a little of the salt on one baking sheet. Roast on the lower rack 15 minutes.
Mix the garlic powder, paprika, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Rub the chicken with 1 tablespoon of oil and the spice mix. Toss the broccoli with the last of the oil.

Stir the sweet potatoes. Put the chicken and broccoli on the second sheet on the upper rack. Roast 18 to 22 minutes, until the chicken reads 165°F in the thickest part on a food thermometer and the sweet potatoes are tender.
Wash your hands, the cutting board and the knife after handling raw chicken. Let the chicken rest 5 minutes, slice it, and divide everything among 4 plates.

swaps.thighs: Use boneless chicken thighs; they also need 165°F and stay juicy.
swaps.potato: Use white potatoes instead of sweet potatoes.

meta.servings: 1 piece of chicken with a quarter of the vegetables

items.title: Sirloin Steak, Baked Potato and Green Beans
items.subtitle: dinner · about 5 oz of steak, 1 potato and a quarter of the beans
items.body: A steakhouse plate at home: seared top sirloin, a fluffy baked potato and buttery green beans.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Prick each potato a few times with a fork and set them on a baking sheet. Bake 50 to 60 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
About 20 minutes before the potatoes are done, pat the steak dry and season it with ¾ teaspoon of the salt and the pepper. Let it sit while the skillet heats.

Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the steak 4 to 5 minutes per side, until it reads at least 145°F in the center on a food thermometer. Move it to a board and let it rest 3 minutes (USDA).
Meanwhile, steam the green beans over simmering water 5 to 7 minutes, until bright green and tender. Toss them with the butter, garlic and the rest of the salt.
Slice the steak across the grain. Split the potatoes and top with sour cream and green onions if you like. Divide everything among 4 plates.
equipment: saucepan with a steamer basket or lid

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil on the beans and skip the sour cream.
swaps.spinach: Serve a spinach salad instead of green beans.

meta.servings: about 5 oz of steak, 1 potato and a quarter of the beans

items.title: Eggs, Oatmeal and Berries
items.subtitle: breakfast · 2 eggs, 1 cup of oatmeal and ½ cup of berries
items.body: A warm breakfast plate: creamy oatmeal with berries and two eggs on the side. Ready in under 20 minutes.

ingredients.prep: or sliced strawberries, fresh or frozen

steps: Bring the milk, water and salt just to a simmer in the saucepan. Stir in the oats and cinnamon and cook over medium-low heat 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and creamy.

While the oats cook, melt the butter in the skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs and cook them the way your family likes (fried, scrambled or over easy) until the whites and yolks are firm. Scrambled eggs and egg dishes are done at 160°F (USDA).
Spoon the oatmeal into bowls, top with the berries and a drizzle of honey if you like, and serve the eggs alongside with a little pepper.

swaps.dairy_free: Make the oatmeal with water or soy milk and cook the eggs in oil.
swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.

meta.servings: 2 eggs, 1 cup of oatmeal and ½ cup of berries

items.title: Ground Beef, Rice and Pepper Plates
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1½ cups of beef and peppers with 1 cup of rice
items.body: Lean ground beef browned with sweet peppers and onion, mildly spiced, over white rice. Freezes well in single plates.

steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer. Bring it to a boil with the water and ¼ teaspoon of the salt, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it stand, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the peppers and onion 5 to 6 minutes, until they soften and brown at the edges. Move them to a plate.
Add the beef to the skillet and break it up. Cook 6 to 8 minutes, until no pink remains and it reads 160°F on a food thermometer. Spoon off extra fat.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika, the rest of the salt and the pepper and cook 1 minute. Return the peppers and onion and toss to heat through.
Serve over the rice.

swaps.turkey: Use ground turkey; cook it to 165°F.
swaps.brown_rice: Use brown rice; simmer it about 40 minutes with a little more water.

meta.servings: about 1½ cups of beef and peppers with 1 cup of rice

items.title: Salmon, Quinoa and Garlic Spinach
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 fillet, ¾ cup of quinoa and a quarter of the spinach
items.body: Baked salmon with fluffy quinoa and spinach wilted with garlic and lemon. Rich in protein and good fats.

steps: Rinse the quinoa well in a fine strainer. Bring it to a boil with the water, cover, and simmer on low 15 minutes. Let it stand, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff it.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Set the salmon skin side down on a lined baking sheet, brush with 1 tablespoon of oil and season with the salt and pepper.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest part reads 145°F on a food thermometer and flakes easily. Squeeze the lemon juice over it.

Meanwhile, warm the remaining oil and the garlic in the skillet over medium heat until the garlic sizzles, about 1 minute. Add the spinach a handful at a time and toss until just wilted, 2 to 3 minutes. Season with the salt.
Divide the quinoa, salmon and spinach among 4 plates with lemon wedges.

swaps.rice: Use rice or couscous instead of quinoa.
swaps.greens: Use kale or chard; cook them a few minutes longer.

meta.servings: 1 fillet, ¾ cup of quinoa and a quarter of the spinach

items.title: Garlic Chicken, Rice and Broccoli
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · a quarter of the chicken, 1 cup of rice and 1 cup of broccoli
items.body: Pan-seared chicken with a little garlic, white rice and steamed broccoli. The plate meal-preppers make by the dozen.

steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer. Bring it to a boil with the water and ¼ teaspoon of the salt, cover, turn the heat to low and cook 18 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it stand, covered, 5 minutes, then fluff it with a fork.
Season the chicken with the garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper. Wash your hands and the cutting board after handling raw chicken.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets 4 to 5 minutes per side, until golden and 165°F in the thickest part on a food thermometer. Let them rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Steam the broccoli over simmering water 4 to 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Toss with the soy sauce or lemon.
Divide the rice, chicken and broccoli among 4 plates or containers.
equipment: steamer basket or a pot with a lid

swaps.gluten_free: Use lemon instead of soy sauce, or a gluten-free tamari.
swaps.veg: Use green beans or asparagus instead of broccoli.

meta.servings: a quarter of the chicken, 1 cup of rice and 1 cup of broccoli

items.title: Egg and Veggie Scramble with Toast
items.subtitle: breakfast,lunch,dinner · about 1 cup of scramble and 1 slice of toast
items.body: Whole eggs and egg whites scrambled with onion, peppers and mushrooms, with whole-wheat toast. Quick, filling and cheap.

steps: Whisk the eggs, egg whites, ¼ teaspoon of the salt and the pepper in a bowl.
Heat the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, pepper and mushrooms with the rest of the salt 6 to 7 minutes, until soft and the mushroom liquid cooks off.
Pour in the eggs. Stir slowly with a spatula until they are set with no liquid egg left, 2 to 3 minutes; egg dishes are done at 160°F (USDA). Sprinkle on cheese if you like.
Serve with the toast.

swaps.whole_eggs: Use 9 whole eggs instead of eggs plus whites.
swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.

meta.servings: about 1 cup of scramble and 1 slice of toast

items.title: Shrimp Scampi with Linguine
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Shrimp in a lemon, garlic and butter sauce tossed with pasta in about 25 minutes.
