Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar. Toss the kale with 2 tablespoons of dressing and rub it with your hands for a minute to soften.
Divide the quinoa and kale among 4 bowls. Top with the roasted vegetables, chickpeas, feta and pecans, and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the feta or use avocado.
swaps.nut_free: Use pumpkin seeds instead of pecans.

items.title: Butternut Squash Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: A smooth, gently spiced squash soup with carrot and onion. A touch of cream is optional.

ingredients.prep: peeled, seeded and cut in 1-inch cubes (about 8 cups)

steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot until soft, about 6 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the squash, apple, broth, salt, nutmeg and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, until the squash is very tender.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender. If using a countertop blender, let the soup cool 5 minutes, fill the jar no more than half full, and hold the lid down with a towel.
Stir in the cream if using and taste for salt. Top with pumpkin seeds if you like.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter and coconut milk instead of cream.
swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.

items.title: Brown Sugar Roasted Acorn Squash
items.subtitle: side · 1/2 squash
items.body: Acorn squash halves baked with butter, brown sugar and a pinch of cinnamon until spoon-tender.

ingredients.prep: halved through the stem and seeded

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. To halve the squash safely, set it on a damp towel so it does not roll and cut with a large knife.
Score the flesh in a crisscross pattern without cutting through the skin. Set the halves cut side up on the pan.
Spread the butter in the halves and sprinkle with the brown sugar, cinnamon and salt.
Bake 45 to 55 minutes, until a knife slides in easily and the tops are glazed. Spoon the buttery syrup over the flesh before serving.
equipment: rimmed baking sheet or baking dish

swaps.dairy_free: Use coconut oil or olive oil instead of butter.

items.title: Baked Spaghetti Squash Marinara
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Roasted spaghetti squash strands baked in marinara under melted mozzarella.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Rub the cut sides of the squash with the oil and salt and set cut side down on the baking sheet.
Roast 35 to 40 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Let cool 10 minutes, then scrape the flesh into strands with a fork.
Spread a little marinara in the baking dish. Toss the squash strands with the rest of the sauce and the Italian seasoning and spread in the dish.
Top with the mozzarella and Parmesan. Bake 15 minutes, until bubbling and the cheese melts.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheeses and top with breadcrumbs toasted in olive oil.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; stir in 1 pound browned ground beef or turkey (to 160°F or 165°F) for a meat version.

items.title: Pumpkin Bread
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 slice
items.body: A moist, spiced quick bread made with canned pumpkin. One bowl, no mixer.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the loaf pan.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and pumpkin pie spice in a bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk the pumpkin, both sugars, oil, eggs and vanilla until smooth. Stir in the flour mixture just until no dry streaks remain.
Pour into the pan and bake 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean.
Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then turn out onto a rack. Let it cool at least 10 more minutes before slicing.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a 1-to-1 gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: It is already dairy-free.

items.title: Pumpkin Spice Pancakes
items.subtitle: breakfast · 3 pancakes (about 4 inches)
items.body: Fluffy fall pancakes with canned pumpkin and warm spices.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the pan

steps: Whisk the flour, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt and spice in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the milk, pumpkin, egg, melted butter and vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined; small lumps are fine. Let rest 5 minutes.

Heat a griddle over medium heat and brush with butter. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form and the edges look dry, 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until cooked through in the center.
Keep warm on a baking sheet in a 200°F oven while you cook the rest.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and oil instead of butter.
swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend.

items.title: Classic Pumpkin Pie
items.subtitle: snack · 1 slice
items.body: A smooth, spiced pumpkin custard in a flaky crust, the way it is served at Thanksgiving.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Fit the crust into the pie plate and crimp the edge. Set the plate on a baking sheet.
Whisk the pumpkin, evaporated milk, eggs, sugar, salt and spices until smooth. Pour into the crust.
Bake 15 minutes, then lower the oven to 350°F and bake 40 to 50 minutes more, until the edges are set, the center jiggles only slightly and a knife near the center comes out clean (at least 160°F).
Cool on a rack about 2 hours, then refrigerate. The filling finishes setting as it cools.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free pie crust.
swaps.dairy_free: Use full-fat coconut milk instead of evaporated milk and skip the whipped cream.

items.title: Turkey Pumpkin Chili
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Ground turkey and two kinds of beans in a thick tomato and pumpkin base with mild chili spices.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the turkey, onion and bell pepper and cook, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the turkey reaches 165°F, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, cinnamon and salt and cook 1 minute.
Add the pumpkin, tomatoes with their juice, beans and broth. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Taste for salt and serve with cheese and sour cream if you like.
Slow cooker: brown the turkey and vegetables first (steps 1 and 2), then put everything in the cooker and cook on low 6 hours.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

swaps.gluten_free: Check the chili powder and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream.
swaps.meatless: Skip the turkey, use vegetable broth and add a third can of beans.

items.title: Pumpkin Baked Oatmeal
items.subtitle: breakfast · 1 square
items.body: A sliceable pan of oats baked with pumpkin, milk and maple. Make it once for a week of breakfasts.

ingredients.prep: melted, plus more for the dish

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Butter the baking dish.
Stir the oats, baking powder, spice and salt together in a large bowl.
Whisk the pumpkin, milk, eggs, maple syrup, melted butter and vanilla in another bowl. Pour over the oats and stir well. Spread in the dish and sprinkle with pecans if using.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the center is set and no longer wet and the edges are golden. Let cool 5 minutes before cutting.

swaps.gluten_free: Use oats labeled gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and coconut oil.

items.title: Mushroom Barley Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A rich, old-fashioned soup of browned mushrooms, vegetables and chewy pearl barley.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook without stirring for 3 minutes, then stir and cook until browned and their liquid has cooked off, about 8 minutes total.
Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Add the barley, broth, soy sauce and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 40 to 45 minutes, until the barley is tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Season with the salt and pepper and taste.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; use beef broth and add 1 pound browned stew beef for a meat version (simmer until tender).

items.title: Mushroom and Asparagus Risotto
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Creamy stovetop risotto with browned mushrooms, asparagus, peas and Parmesan.

steps: Warm the broth in a saucepan over low heat.
Melt 1 tablespoon of the butter with the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms until browned, about 6 minutes. Lift them out onto a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the shallot and garlic 2 minutes, then add the rice and stir 1 to 2 minutes, until the edges look clear.
Add a ladle of warm broth and stir until it is mostly absorbed. Keep adding broth a ladle at a time, stirring often, for about 18 minutes.

Stir in the asparagus with another ladle of broth and cook 5 to 6 minutes more, until the rice is creamy and just tender and the asparagus is bright green. Stir in the peas and mushrooms to heat through.
Off the heat, stir in the Parmesan, the rest of the butter and the lemon juice. Season and serve right away; risotto thickens as it stands.
equipment: large heavy saucepan or Dutch oven

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter and skip the Parmesan; add 2 tablespoons nutritional yeast if you have it.

items.title: Tofu, Mushroom and Bok Choy Stir-Fry
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: Crisp tofu cubes, mushrooms and bok choy in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce.

ingredients.prep: extra-firm, pressed and cut in 3/4-inch cubes
cut in 1-inch pieces, stems and leaves separated

steps: Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.

Toss the tofu cubes with 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tofu, turning now and then, until golden on most sides, 8 to 10 minutes. Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and the mushrooms and cook 4 minutes, until browned. Add the bok choy stems and cook 2 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger and bok choy leaves and cook 1 minute, until the leaves wilt.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and cook 1 minute, until glossy. Return the tofu and toss. Serve over rice.
equipment: clean kitchen towel or paper towels

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; use 1 pound sliced chicken breast instead of tofu, cooked to 165°F, for a meat version.

items.title: Spring Vegetable Frittata
items.subtitle: breakfast,dinner,lunch · 1 wedge
items.body: A thick oven-finished omelet with asparagus, mushrooms, spinach and feta.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Heat the oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms 5 minutes, until browned. Add the asparagus and green onions and cook 3 minutes. Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Spread the vegetables evenly and pour in the eggs. Sprinkle with the feta. Cook without stirring 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges start to set.
Move the skillet to the oven and bake 12 to 15 minutes, until puffed and set in the center (160°F). Use an oven mitt; the handle is hot.
Let stand 5 minutes, then cut into wedges.

swaps.dairy_free: Use water instead of milk and skip the feta.

items.title: Lemon Parmesan Roasted Asparagus
items.subtitle: side · about 6 spears
items.body: Asparagus roasted in 10 minutes with garlic, lemon and a little Parmesan.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the asparagus with the oil, garlic, salt and pepper on the baking sheet and spread in one layer.
Roast 8 to 12 minutes, depending on thickness, until tender-crisp.
Sprinkle with the Parmesan and lemon juice while hot.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.

items.title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Garlic Salmon and Asparagus
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 fillet plus asparagus
items.body: Salmon fillets and asparagus roasted together on one pan with lemon and garlic, in about 25 minutes.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Stir the oil, garlic, lemon juice, dill, salt and pepper together.
Spread the asparagus on one side of the baking sheet and toss with about a third of the lemon-garlic oil.
Set the salmon skin side down on the other side and brush with the rest. Lay lemon slices on top if using.
Roast 12 to 15 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily with a fork and reads 145°F in the thickest part.

swaps.gluten_free: Already gluten-free.
swaps.dairy_free: Already dairy-free.

items.title: Pasta Primavera
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Penne tossed with sautéed spring vegetables, garlic, lemon and Parmesan.

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 tablespoon salt. Cook the penne by the package directions. Before draining, scoop out 1 cup of the pasta water.
While the pasta cooks, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the asparagus, zucchini and bell pepper 5 to 6 minutes, until tender-crisp.
Add the garlic, tomatoes and peas and cook 2 minutes. Season with 3/4 teaspoon salt and the pepper.
Toss the drained pasta with the vegetables, Parmesan, lemon juice and enough pasta water to make a light, glossy sauce. Top with basil if you like.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free penne.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan and add more olive oil and lemon.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; add sliced cooked chicken for a meat version.

items.title: Skillet Ratatouille
items.subtitle: side,dinner · about 1 cup
items.body: A French summer stew of eggplant, zucchini, peppers and tomatoes, simmered until soft and rich.

steps: Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant and 1/2 teaspoon of the salt and cook, stirring now and then, until browned and softened, about 8 minutes. Move to a bowl.
Add the rest of the oil, the onion and peppers and cook 5 minutes. Add the zucchini and cook 4 minutes more. Stir in the garlic for 30 seconds.

Return the eggplant to the pan with the tomatoes, thyme, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Bring to a simmer, cover partly and cook 20 to 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until everything is very tender.
Taste for salt and top with basil if you like. Serve warm or at room temperature.
equipment: large deep skillet or Dutch oven

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; serve beside roast chicken or sausages for a meat meal.

items.title: Zucchini Bread
items.subtitle: breakfast,snack · 1 slice
items.body: A moist cinnamon quick bread that uses up 2 cups of grated zucchini.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease the loaf pan.
Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt and cinnamon in a bowl.
In a large bowl, whisk both sugars, the oil, eggs and vanilla until smooth. Stir in the zucchini (no need to squeeze it).
Stir in the flour mixture just until no dry streaks remain, then fold in the walnuts if using.
Pour into the pan and bake 50 to 60 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 10 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a 1-to-1 gluten-free flour blend.
swaps.dairy_free: It is already dairy-free.

items.title: Baked Eggplant Parmesan
items.subtitle: dinner · 1 square
items.body: Crisp oven-baked eggplant slices layered with marinara and mozzarella. No frying.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Brush the baking sheets with half the oil. Sprinkle the eggplant with the salt.
Beat the eggs with the water in a shallow bowl. Mix the panko, 1/2 cup Parmesan and Italian seasoning in another.
Dip each slice in egg, then press into the crumbs. Lay on the baking sheets and brush the tops with the rest of the oil.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, flipping once, until golden and tender. Lower the oven to 375°F.
Spread 1 cup marinara in the baking dish. Layer half the eggplant, 1 cup sauce and 1 cup mozzarella. Repeat, then sprinkle with the last 1/4 cup Parmesan.
Bake 25 minutes, until bubbling and 165°F in the center. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free panko or crushed rice cereal.

items.title: Baba Ganoush
items.subtitle: snack,side · about 1/4 cup
items.body: A smoky roasted eggplant dip with tahini, lemon and garlic. Serve with pita and vegetables.

steps: Heat the oven to 450°F. Prick the eggplants all over with a fork and set on the baking sheet.
Roast 40 to 45 minutes, turning once, until collapsed and very soft. Let cool 15 minutes.
Split the eggplants and scoop the flesh into a strainer. Let it drain 5 minutes; discard the skins.
Mash the flesh with a fork (or pulse in a food processor) with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, salt and cumin. Spread in a bowl and drizzle with the oil.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with vegetables or gluten-free crackers instead of pita.

items.title: Pasta alla Norma
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A Sicilian pasta with browned eggplant in garlicky tomato sauce, topped with ricotta and basil.

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 tablespoon salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant and 3/4 teaspoon salt and cook, stirring now and then, until browned on all sides and soft, 10 to 12 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the garlic and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute. Stir in the tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes, until thickened.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta by the package directions. Save 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and most of the basil, adding pasta water if it seems dry. Serve topped with spoonfuls of ricotta, the rest of the basil and Parmesan if you like.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free penne.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the ricotta and Parmesan; finish with extra olive oil.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless.

items.title: Garlic Eggplant Stir-Fry
items.subtitle: dinner,side · about 1 cup
items.body: Silky eggplant in a sweet, savory garlic and ginger sauce, Chinese takeout style.

steps: Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant and cook, turning now and then, 5 minutes.
Add 1/4 cup water, cover and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the eggplant is very tender. Uncover and let any water cook off.
Push the eggplant aside, add the last tablespoon of oil, the garlic, ginger and green onion whites, and stir 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce again, pour it in and toss until thick and glossy, 1 minute. Top with the green onion greens and serve over rice.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free hoisin.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; brown 1/2 pound ground pork (to 160°F) before the eggplant for a meat version.

items.title: Roasted Root Vegetables
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Beets, carrots, parsnips and sweet potato roasted with rosemary until sweet and caramelized.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the beets with 1 tablespoon of the oil and a pinch of salt and keep them at one end of the baking sheet so they do not stain everything pink.
Toss the other vegetables with the rest of the oil, the rosemary, salt and pepper and spread on the rest of the pan in one layer.
Roast 35 to 40 minutes, stirring once, until everything is tender and browned at the edges.

items.title: Roasted Beet and Goat Cheese Salad
items.subtitle: side,lunch · about 2 cups
items.body: Sweet roasted beets over peppery arugula with tangy goat cheese, toasted walnuts and a balsamic dressing.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Wrap the beets in foil, set in a small baking dish and roast 50 to 60 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Let cool 20 minutes, then rub off the skins with a paper towel and cut the beets in wedges.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the arugula with half the dressing and spread on a platter. Top with the beets, goat cheese and walnuts and drizzle with the rest.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the goat cheese and add avocado.
swaps.nut_free: Use toasted pumpkin seeds instead of walnuts.

items.title: Pink Beet Hummus
items.subtitle: snack · about 1/4 cup
items.body: Classic hummus blended with roasted beet for a bright pink, slightly sweet dip.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Wrap the beets in foil and roast 50 to 60 minutes, until tender. Cool, rub off the skins and cut in chunks.
Blend the tahini and lemon juice 1 minute, until creamy.
Add the beets, chickpeas, garlic, oil, cumin and salt and blend until smooth, scraping down the sides. Add water a tablespoon at a time until it is as smooth as you like.
Taste for salt and lemon. Serve with vegetables or pita.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with vegetables or gluten-free crackers.

items.title: Vegetable Borscht
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 3/4 cups
items.body: An Eastern European beet soup with cabbage, potatoes and carrots, finished with a swirl of sour cream.

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and carrot 5 minutes. Add the beets and cook 5 minutes more, stirring.
Stir in the garlic and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the broth, potatoes and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 minutes.
Add the cabbage and simmer 10 to 15 minutes more, until the potatoes and cabbage are tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in the vinegar, salt and pepper and taste. Serve with sour cream and dill if you like.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

swaps.gluten_free: Check the broth label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the sour cream.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; use beef broth and add 1 pound stew beef simmered until tender for a meat version.

items.title: Quick Pickled Beets
items.subtitle: side,snack · about 1/3 cup
items.body: Tender beets and red onion in a sweet-tangy brine. Fridge pickles, no canning.

steps: Cover the beets with water in a pot, bring to a boil and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain and cool until you can handle them, then slip off the skins and slice 1/4 inch thick.
Bring the vinegar, water, sugar, salt and cloves to a boil in a small saucepan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Layer the beets and onion in the jar and pour the hot brine over them. Cool, then cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours before eating.

items.title: Creamy Cucumber Radish Salad
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Crisp cucumbers and radishes in a cool sour cream and dill dressing.

steps: Stir the sour cream, vinegar, sugar, dill, salt and pepper together in a large bowl.
Add the cucumbers, radishes and onion and toss to coat.
Serve right away, or chill up to 4 hours. Stir before serving.

swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free yogurt, or dress with 2 tablespoons olive oil and 2 tablespoons vinegar instead.

items.title: Butter Roasted Radishes
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Roasting turns radishes mild, juicy and a little sweet, a lot like new potatoes.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the radishes with the butter, salt and pepper on the baking sheet and turn them cut side down.
Roast 18 to 22 minutes, until tender and browned on the cut sides.
Toss with the lemon juice and parsley if using.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

items.title: Avocado Toast with Radishes and Eggs
items.subtitle: breakfast,lunch · 1 toast
items.body: Mashed avocado on toasted sourdough with crisp sliced radishes and a fried egg.

steps: Mash the avocados with the lemon juice and half the salt.
Melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat. Crack in the eggs, cover and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the whites and yolks are firm (160°F). Sprinkle with the rest of the salt.
Meanwhile, toast the bread.
Spread the avocado on the toast, top with radish slices and an egg, and add pepper flakes if you like.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread.
swaps.dairy_free: Cook the eggs in olive oil.

items.title: Quick Pickled Radishes
items.subtitle: side,snack · about 1/4 cup
items.body: Bright pink, crunchy radish slices in a tangy brine for tacos, bowls and sandwiches.

steps: Pack the radishes, garlic and jalapeño if using into the jar.
Bring the vinegar, water, sugar and salt to a boil in a small saucepan, stirring until dissolved.
Pour the hot brine over the radishes. Cool, then cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour. They turn pink overnight.

items.title: Mexican Chopped Salad
items.subtitle: lunch,side,dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Romaine, black beans, corn, avocado, tomatoes and radishes in a lime-cumin dressing.

steps: Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar until blended.
Toss the romaine, beans, corn, tomatoes, radishes, onion and cilantro in a large bowl.
Add the avocado and dressing and toss gently. Top with crushed chips if you like.

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; top with grilled chicken or shrimp for a main dish.

items.title: Fresh Guacamole
items.subtitle: snack,side · about 1/4 cup
items.body: Chunky avocado dip with lime, onion, tomato, cilantro and a little jalapeño.

steps: Halve and pit the avocados and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Add the lime juice and salt and mash to the texture you like.
Stir in the onion, tomato, jalapeño and cilantro. Taste and add more salt or lime.
Serve right away, or press plastic wrap onto the surface and chill up to 4 hours.

items.title: Cobb Salad
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · 1 large salad
items.body: A dinner-size salad with rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese.

steps: Put the eggs in a saucepan, cover with cold water by an inch and bring to a boil. Turn off the heat, cover and let stand 12 minutes, until the yolks are firm. Cool in ice water, peel and chop.
Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain on paper towels and crumble.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Spread the romaine on a platter. Arrange the chicken, bacon, eggs, avocado, tomatoes and blue cheese in rows on top. Drizzle with dressing at the table.

swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the blue cheese.
swaps.gluten_free: Check the rotisserie chicken and bacon labels.

items.title: Southern Collard Greens
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Collards simmered low and slow with bacon, onion and a splash of vinegar until silky.

ingredients.prep: stems removed, leaves cut in 1-inch ribbons

steps: Wash the collards well in a sink of cold water, lifting them out so the grit stays behind. Repeat if you see sand.
Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp, about 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes, then the garlic and pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the collards a few handfuls at a time, stirring until they wilt enough to fit. Add the broth, vinegar and brown sugar.
Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, cover and simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour, stirring now and then, until very tender.
Taste and add the salt (the bacon and broth are salty, so taste first). Serve with some of the cooking liquid.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven
large bowl or clean sink for washing greens

swaps.gluten_free: Check the bacon and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Skip the bacon, cook the onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil with 1 teaspoon smoked paprika, and use vegetable broth.

items.title: Garlicky Sautéed Swiss Chard
items.subtitle: side · about 1/2 cup
items.body: Swiss chard stems and leaves cooked quickly in olive oil with garlic and lemon.

ingredients.prep: stems sliced, leaves chopped, kept separate

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chard stems and cook 4 minutes, until starting to soften.
Add the garlic and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute, until the garlic is golden at the edges.
Add the chard leaves (with any water still clinging to them) and the salt. Cover and cook 2 minutes, then uncover and toss until wilted and tender, 2 to 3 minutes more.
Stir in the lemon juice and serve.

items.title: Caldo Verde (Potato, Greens and Sausage Soup)
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: A Portuguese soup of creamy blended potatoes, thin ribbons of collard greens and smoked sausage.

ingredients.prep: stems removed, leaves rolled and sliced in very thin ribbons

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the sausage 5 minutes and lift it out onto a plate.
Cook the onion in the same pot 5 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart when poked.
Mash or blend the potatoes right in the pot until the broth is creamy, leaving some chunks if you like.
Stir in the collards and sausage and simmer 5 to 8 minutes, until the greens are tender and the soup is steaming hot (165°F). Season with the salt and pepper and taste.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage and broth labels.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage, add 1 teaspoon smoked paprika with the garlic and use vegetable broth plus a can of white beans.

items.title: Sausage, White Bean and Chard Pasta
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Penne tossed with browned Italian sausage, white beans, wilted chard, garlic and Parmesan.

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 tablespoon salt. Cook the penne by the package directions; save 1/2 cup of the water, then drain.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the sausage, breaking it up, until browned and no pink remains (160°F), about 8 minutes.
Add the chard stems and cook 3 minutes. Add the garlic and pepper flakes for 30 seconds.
Add the chard leaves, beans and broth and simmer 4 to 5 minutes, until the leaves are tender.
Toss in the pasta and Parmesan, adding pasta water as needed for a light sauce.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free penne and check the sausage label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage, use vegetable broth and add a second can of beans.

items.title: Chard and Ricotta Lasagna Roll-Ups
items.subtitle: dinner · 2 roll-ups
items.body: Lasagna noodles rolled around a cheesy ricotta and Swiss chard filling, baked in marinara.

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the noodles in boiling salted water by the package directions. Drain and lay flat on oiled foil so they do not stick.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook the chard and garlic 4 to 5 minutes, until wilted and the liquid cooks off. Let cool a few minutes.
Stir the ricotta, 1 cup mozzarella, Parmesan, egg, Italian seasoning, salt and cooled chard together.
Spread 1 cup marinara in the baking dish. Spread about 1/4 cup filling along each noodle, roll it up and set seam side down in the dish.
Top with the rest of the sauce and 1/2 cup mozzarella. Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until bubbling and 165°F in the center.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free lasagna noodles and cook as the package says.
swaps.meatless: Already meatless; add 1/2 pound browned Italian sausage (to 160°F) to the sauce for a meat version.

items.title: Southern Fried Okra
items.subtitle: side,snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Bite-size okra coated in seasoned cornmeal and pan-fried until golden and crunchy.

steps: Toss the okra with the buttermilk in a bowl. Mix the cornmeal, flour, salt, pepper and cayenne in another.
Lift the okra out a handful at a time, let the extra buttermilk drip off, and toss in the cornmeal mix until coated.
Heat the oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers (about 350°F). Fry the okra in two batches, turning now and then, until golden brown and crisp, 5 to 7 minutes.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with a pinch of salt. Serve hot.
equipment: large heavy skillet (cast iron works well)

swaps.gluten_free: Use all cornmeal or a gluten-free flour blend instead of the flour.
swaps.dairy_free: Use 1/2 cup plant milk with 1 1/2 teaspoons lemon juice instead of buttermilk.

items.title: Okra, Corn and Tomatoes
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: A Southern summer skillet of okra, sweet corn and tomatoes with a little smoky paprika.

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper 5 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the okra and cook 5 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the tomatoes with their juice, corn, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered 12 to 15 minutes, until the okra is tender.
Taste for salt and serve, over rice if you like.

swaps.meatless: Already meatless; cook 3 strips of chopped bacon first and use the fat in place of the oil for a meat version.

items.title: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups gumbo and 1/2 cup rice
items.body: A Louisiana-style stew built on a dark roux, with chicken thighs, smoked sausage and okra, served over rice.

steps: Heat the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, stirring constantly, until the roux is the color of peanut butter or darker, 20 to 30 minutes. Lower the heat if it smokes; burned roux tastes bitter. Roux is very hot, so keep kids back from the stove.
Add the onion, bell pepper and celery and stir 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

Slowly whisk in the broth until smooth. Add the chicken, sausage, okra, paprika, thyme, cayenne and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, partly covered, 45 minutes, stirring now and then. The chicken should reach 165°F.
Meanwhile, bring the rice, water and a pinch of salt to a boil. Cover, lower the heat and simmer 18 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes.
Remove the bay leaves, taste the gumbo and add the salt if needed. Serve over the rice.
equipment: large heavy pot or Dutch oven

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend or sweet rice flour for the roux, and check the sausage label.

meta.servings: about 1 1/2 cups gumbo and 1/2 cup rice

items.title: Crispy Roasted Okra
items.subtitle: side,snack · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Whole okra pods roasted hot and fast so they turn crisp, not slippery.

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Pat the okra dry; dry okra roasts crisper.
Toss with the oil, paprika, garlic powder and salt on the baking sheet and spread cut side down in one layer.
Roast 15 to 20 minutes, turning once, until browned and crisp at the edges.

items.title: Bhindi Masala (Indian Spiced Okra)
items.subtitle: side,dinner · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Okra cooked until tender and browned with onion, tomato and warm Indian spices.

ingredients.prep: washed, dried well, sliced 1/2 inch thick

steps: Make sure the okra is completely dry before slicing; wet okra turns slippery.
Heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the okra, stirring now and then, until browned in spots and no longer sticky, 10 to 12 minutes. Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and the onion and cook 5 minutes, until golden. Stir in the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric and cayenne for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook 4 minutes, until soft and saucy. Return the okra and cook 3 minutes more. Stir in the lemon juice.
Serve with naan, roti or rice.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve with rice instead of naan.

items.title: Garlic Bok Choy
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Baby bok choy seared and steamed in a skillet with garlic, soy sauce and sesame oil in about 10 minutes.

ingredients.prep: baby bok choy, halved lengthwise and rinsed

steps: Rinse the bok choy well between the leaves, where grit hides.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Lay the bok choy cut side down and cook 2 minutes, until browned.
Add the garlic and stir 30 seconds. Add the water, cover and steam 2 to 3 minutes, until the stems are just tender.
Uncover, add the soy sauce and sesame oil and toss.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.

items.title: Ginger Chicken Noodle Soup with Bok Choy
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 2 cups
items.body: A fast, gingery chicken broth with rice noodles, bok choy and carrots.

ingredients.prep: thin rice noodles or rice sticks

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the ginger, garlic and green onion whites 1 minute.
Add the broth and soy sauce and bring to a boil. Add the chicken breasts whole, lower the heat and simmer gently 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest part reads 165°F.
Lift out the chicken onto a clean board and shred or slice it.
Add the carrots and bok choy stems to the pot and simmer 3 minutes. Add the noodles and bok choy leaves and cook 3 to 5 minutes, until the noodles are tender (check the package time).
Return the chicken, stir in the sesame oil and green onion greens, and serve.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free and check the broth label.
swaps.meatless: Use vegetable broth and cubed firm tofu instead of chicken.

items.title: Pork and Bok Choy Lo Mein
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch · about 2 cups
items.body: Takeout-style noodles stir-fried with ground pork, bok choy, cabbage and carrots in a savory sauce.

steps: Cook the spaghetti in boiling water by the package directions. Drain, rinse briefly with warm water and toss with a few drops of the sesame oil.
Stir the soy sauce, hoisin, the rest of the sesame oil and the brown sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the pork, breaking it up, until browned and no pink remains (160°F), about 7 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add the carrot, cabbage and bok choy stems and stir-fry 3 minutes. Add the bok choy leaves and green onions for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss with tongs until everything is hot and coated, about 2 minutes.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice noodles, tamari labeled gluten-free and a gluten-free hoisin.
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces cubed firm tofu, browned, instead of the pork.

items.title: Chicken, Bok Choy and Snap Pea Stir-Fry
items.subtitle: dinner · about 1 1/2 cups
items.body: Tender sliced chicken with crisp bok choy and snap peas in a honey-ginger sauce.

steps: Toss the chicken with the cornstarch and 1 tablespoon soy sauce. Stir the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken in one layer, turning once, until browned and 165°F inside, 5 to 6 minutes. Move to a clean plate.
Add the rest of the oil, the bok choy and snap peas and stir-fry 3 minutes, until bright green. Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and cook 1 minute, until thick. Return the chicken and toss. Serve over rice.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free and check the broth label.
swaps.meatless: Use pressed, cubed extra-firm tofu and vegetable broth.

items.title: From-Scratch Green Bean Casserole
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Fresh green beans in a creamy mushroom sauce under a crisp, buttery Parmesan crumb topping.

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Boil the green beans in salted water 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion 7 to 8 minutes, until browned and the liquid is gone. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk, and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, until thick. Season with the salt and pepper.
Stir in the beans and spread in the baking dish. Toss the panko with the melted butter and Parmesan and sprinkle on top.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until bubbling and the topping is golden.

swaps.gluten_free: Use cornstarch (1 1/2 tablespoons, whisked into the cold milk) and gluten-free crumbs.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil, unsweetened plant milk and skip the Parmesan.

items.title: Spring Asparagus and Radish Salad
items.subtitle: side · about 3/4 cup
items.body: Thin ribbons of raw asparagus and sliced radishes tossed with lemon, olive oil and Parmesan.

ingredients.prep: thick spears, tough ends snapped off

steps: Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar until blended.
Lay each asparagus spear flat on a cutting board and run a vegetable peeler from the base to the tip to make long ribbons. Slice the tips that are left in thin rounds.
Toss the asparagus and radishes with the dressing and let stand 5 minutes to soften a little.
Top with the Parmesan and serve.

swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan and add toasted sunflower seeds.

items.title: Butternut Squash Mac and Cheese
items.subtitle: dinner,side · about 1 1/4 cups
items.body: Creamy stovetop mac and cheese with puréed butternut squash blended into the cheddar sauce.

steps: Simmer the squash in the water in a covered saucepan 12 to 15 minutes, until very soft. Blend the squash with about 1/2 cup of its cooking water until smooth.
Meanwhile, cook the macaroni in a large pot of boiling salted water by the package directions. Drain.
In the empty pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute. Slowly whisk in the milk and simmer 3 minutes, stirring, until it thickens.
Lower the heat. Whisk in the squash purée, mustard, garlic powder, salt and pepper, then the cheese a handful at a time until melted.
Stir in the macaroni and heat through. Add a splash of milk if it seems thick.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free elbows and 1 tablespoon cornstarch whisked into the cold milk instead of the flour.

items.title: Classic Cheeseburgers
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch
items.body: Juicy, simply seasoned burgers that cook on the grill or in a skillet in about 12 minutes.

meta.name: Classic Cheeseburgers
meta.summary: Juicy, simply seasoned burgers that cook on the grill or in a skillet in about 12 minutes.
steps: Divide the beef into 4 equal portions and shape each into a patty about 3/4 inch thick and a little wider than the buns. Press a shallow dimple into the center of each so it stays flat as it cooks. Handle the meat gently.
Wash your hands after shaping. Season both sides of the patties with the salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Heat the grill or a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the patties 4 to 5 minutes per side, flipping once, until an instant-read thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Lay a slice of cheese on each patty for the last minute; cover so it melts.
Toast the buns cut side down for 30 to 60 seconds. Move the cooked burgers to a clean plate, not the one that held the raw patties.
Build the burgers with lettuce, tomato and your choice of toppings.
meta.make_ahead: Shape the patties up to 1 day ahead. Stack them with wax paper between and keep covered in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze raw patties with wax paper between them for 3 to 4 months for best quality. Thaw overnight in the fridge, or cook from frozen and add a few minutes per side.

leftovers.text: Chop a leftover patty into a quesadilla or over a salad; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Make a few small slider patties (about 2 ounces each) for little hands. They cook in about 3 minutes per side, still to 160°F.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free buns or wrap the burgers in lettuce leaves.
swaps.dairy_free: Leave off the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Cook store-bought veggie patties by the package directions and use the same toppings.

prep_day.ahead: Shape and season the patties; slice the tomato and onion.

items.title: Ground Beef Tacos
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Taco night with a homemade seasoning mix, so you know exactly what is in it.

meta.name: Ground Beef Tacos
meta.summary: Taco night with a homemade seasoning mix, so you know exactly what is in it.
steps: Cook the beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 7 minutes. Spoon off extra fat if there is a lot.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper and cook 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the tomato sauce and water. Simmer 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick enough to hold on a spoon.
Warm the tortillas: wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 30 to 45 seconds, or heat one at a time in a dry skillet.
Set out the filling and toppings so everyone can build their own.
meta.make_ahead: Cook the filling up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F, adding a splash of water.

freezer.text: Freeze the cooked filling flat in a freezer bag for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge overnight.

leftovers.text: Use leftover filling for taco salad, nachos or quesadillas the next day.

meta.kids: Set up a build-your-own bar. Younger children often like the meat, cheese and tortilla separate on the plate.

swaps.gluten_free: Corn tortillas and this homemade seasoning are naturally free of wheat; check labels on the tortillas.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream; add extra avocado.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans of black or pinto beans, drained and lightly mashed, in place of the beef. Skip the browning step.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the taco filling; shred the lettuce and dice the tomato.

items.title: Classic Meat Lasagna
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Layers of meat sauce, ricotta and mozzarella. Make it on the weekend; it reheats beautifully.

meta.name: Classic Meat Lasagna
meta.summary: Layers of meat sauce, ricotta and mozzarella. Make it on the weekend; it reheats beautifully.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the noodles 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain and lay them flat on an oiled baking sheet so they do not stick.

Meanwhile, cook the beef, sausage and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the meat reaches 160°F, 8 to 10 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, sugar, salt and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, egg, 1/2 cup Parmesan and parsley.

Spread 1 cup of meat sauce in the baking dish. Layer 4 noodles, half the ricotta mixture, a third of the mozzarella and a third of the remaining sauce. Repeat once. Finish with the last 4 noodles, the rest of the sauce, the rest of the mozzarella and 1/4 cup Parmesan.
Cover with foil (tent it or spray the underside so it does not stick to the cheese). Bake 40 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 to 20 minutes more, until bubbling and the center reaches 165°F.
Let the lasagna rest 15 minutes before cutting so the layers hold together.
meta.make_ahead: Assemble, cover tightly and refrigerate up to 1 day. Add about 15 minutes to the covered baking time, and check that the center reaches 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze assembled, unbaked lasagna wrapped well for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge 1 to 2 days, then bake as directed until 165°F in the center. Baked squares freeze well too.

leftovers.text: Squares reheat well for lunch; microwave covered until 165°F in the center.

meta.kids: Children who are wary of ricotta often like it once it is baked in. Cut small squares for younger kids; it holds heat, so let it cool a few minutes.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free lasagna noodles (cook as the package says) and check the sausage label.
swaps.meatless: Replace the meat with 1 pound chopped mushrooms and 10 ounces thawed, squeezed frozen spinach, browned in a little olive oil.

prep_day.ahead: Make the meat sauce and assemble the whole lasagna; refrigerate or freeze unbaked.

items.title: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: A weeknight meat sauce that simmers while the pasta cooks. Double the sauce and freeze half.

meta.name: Spaghetti with Meat Sauce
meta.summary: A weeknight meat sauce that simmers while the pasta cooks. Double the sauce and freeze half.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the beef, onion and carrot and cook, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, Italian seasoning, sugar, salt, pepper and pepper flakes. Bring to a simmer, then lower the heat and cook 20 minutes, stirring now and then.
While the sauce simmers, bring a large pot of water to a boil with 1 tablespoon salt. Cook the spaghetti until tender, following the package time. Save 1/2 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the pasta with about half the sauce, adding a little pasta water if it looks dry. Serve the rest of the sauce on top with Parmesan.
meta.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 3 to 4 days in the fridge. Reheat to 165°F and cook the pasta fresh.

freezer.text: Freeze the sauce (without pasta) for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Leftover sauce makes quick sloppy joes or a topping for baked potatoes; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Serve some plain buttered noodles on the side with sauce for dipping. Break the spaghetti in half before cooking for easier eating.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free spaghetti.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the Parmesan.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cups chopped mushrooms and 1 can drained lentils or white beans in place of the beef.

prep_day.ahead: Make a double batch of sauce; refrigerate one, freeze one.

items.title: Pot Roast with Carrots and Potatoes
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: A Sunday-dinner classic you can make in the slow cooker or the oven. The leftovers make great sandwiches.

meta.name: Pot Roast with Carrots and Potatoes
meta.summary: A Sunday-dinner classic you can make in the slow cooker or the oven. The leftovers make great sandwiches.
steps: Pat the roast dry and season all over with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet (or the Dutch oven) over medium-high heat. Brown the roast well on all sides, about 10 minutes total. Browning adds flavor; you can skip it on a busy morning.

Slow cooker: Put the potatoes, carrots, celery and onion in the cooker and set the roast on top. Whisk the tomato paste into the broth with the Worcestershire and pour it over. Add the garlic, thyme and bay leaves. Cover and cook on low 8 to 9 hours or high 5 to 6 hours.
Oven: Heat the oven to 325°F. In the Dutch oven, add the onion, garlic, broth mixture, thyme and bay leaves around the roast. Cover and bake 2 1/2 hours. Add the vegetables and bake 1 hour more.
The roast is safe at 145°F, but chuck becomes fork-tender only after long cooking, when it pulls apart easily. Lift out the meat and vegetables and remove the bay leaves.

For gravy, pour the cooking liquid into a saucepan and bring to a boil. Stir the cornstarch into the water, whisk it in and simmer 1 to 2 minutes until thickened. Slice or pull the beef and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

meta.make_ahead: Cook a day ahead; chill the meat in its liquid. Lift off the hardened fat, then reheat gently to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze sliced beef in gravy for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Potatoes turn grainy when frozen, so eat those first.

leftovers.text: Pile leftover beef on rolls with a little gravy for hot sandwiches, or use it in beef stew or tacos; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Shred the beef and serve with the soft carrots. Let little ones dip pieces in the gravy.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free Worcestershire sauce and broth (check labels); cornstarch is gluten-free.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables and season the roast the night before; start the slow cooker in the morning.

items.title: Simple Roast Chicken
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: A whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and herbs. Leftovers become soup, salads and quesadillas.

meta.name: Simple Roast Chicken
meta.summary: A whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic and herbs. Leftovers become soup, salads and quesadillas.
equipment: roasting pan or large oven-safe skillet
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Take the chicken out of its package and remove anything in the cavity. Do not rinse the chicken; washing raw poultry spreads germs around the sink. Pat it dry with paper towels and throw them away. Wash your hands and anything the raw chicken touched.
Lay the onion slices in the pan as a rack. Set the chicken on top, breast up.
Mix the butter, salt, pepper, thyme and garlic powder and rub it all over the chicken. Put the lemon halves and garlic cloves inside. Tie the legs together if you like.
Roast 1 hour 10 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer reads 165°F in the thickest part of the breast and the innermost part of the thigh, without touching bone.
Let the chicken rest 15 minutes before carving. Spoon the pan juices over the meat.
Within 2 hours, pull the meat off the leftover carcass and refrigerate it. Save the bones in the freezer for stock if you like.
meta.make_ahead: Rub the chicken with the seasoned butter up to 1 day ahead and keep it uncovered on a plate in the fridge; the skin dries and roasts crisper.

freezer.text: Freeze cooked, pulled chicken in portions for up to 4 months for best quality. Handy for soups, quesadillas and pot pie.

leftovers.text: Use leftover meat in chicken noodle soup, chicken quesadillas, Caesar salad or pot pie; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Many kids like the drumsticks. Pull the meat off the bone for younger children.

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Roast a chicken (or two) and pull the meat for the week.

items.title: Family Beef and Bean Chili
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch
items.body: Mild, hearty chili that feeds a crowd and freezes well. Let everyone add heat at the table.

meta.name: Family Beef and Bean Chili
meta.summary: Mild, hearty chili that feeds a crowd and freezes well. Let everyone add heat at the table.
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the beef, onion and bell pepper and cook, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 10 minutes. Spoon off extra fat.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper. Cook 1 minute, stirring.
Stir in the crushed and diced tomatoes, beans, broth and brown sugar. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 30 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Taste and add more salt or chili powder if you like. Serve with toppings.
Slow cooker: brown the beef and vegetables first (steps 1 and 2), then put everything in the cooker and cook on low 6 to 8 hours.
meta.make_ahead: Chili tastes even better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days and reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Cool, then freeze in meal-size containers for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Spoon over baked potatoes or hot dogs, or fill burritos; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Keep the pot mild and set out hot sauce for grown-ups. Kids like crushing a few tortilla chips on top.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the chili powder and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese and sour cream.
swaps.meatless: Skip the beef and add 2 more cans of beans plus 1 cup frozen corn.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the whole pot; portion some for lunches and freeze the rest.

items.title: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Tender chicken and crisp vegetables in a simple soy-ginger sauce. Have the rice cooking first.

meta.name: Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry
meta.summary: Tender chicken and crisp vegetables in a simple soy-ginger sauce. Have the rice cooking first.
steps: Whisk all the sauce ingredients together in a small bowl.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet or wok over high heat. Add the chicken in one layer, sprinkle with the salt, and cook without stirring 2 minutes, then stir and cook until no longer pink inside and the pieces reach 165°F, about 4 minutes more. Move the chicken to a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil, the broccoli and carrot, and 2 tablespoons water. Cover and cook 2 minutes. Add the bell pepper and snap peas and stir-fry 2 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Return the chicken. Stir the sauce again (the cornstarch settles), pour it in and cook, stirring, until glossy and thick, about 1 minute.
Serve over rice (see Fluffy White Rice), topped with green onions and sesame seeds.
meta.make_ahead: Cut the chicken and vegetables and mix the sauce up to 1 day ahead; keep raw chicken in its own covered container on the bottom shelf.

freezer.text: The vegetables go soft when frozen and reheated. Freeze raw cut chicken instead.

leftovers.text: Pack over rice for lunch; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Serve the sauce on the side for dipping, and let kids pick their vegetables.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free instead of soy sauce, and gluten-free broth.
swaps.meatless: Use 14 ounces firm tofu, pressed and cubed, browned in the oil.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the vegetables and chicken (separate containers); mix the sauce; cook the rice.

items.title: Sheet-Pan Sausage and Vegetables
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Smoked sausage roasted with potatoes, peppers and broccoli on one pan. Little to wash.

meta.name: Sheet-Pan Sausage and Vegetables
meta.summary: Smoked sausage roasted with potatoes, peppers and broccoli on one pan. Little to wash.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment.
Toss the potatoes with 2 tablespoons oil and half the seasonings. Spread on the pan and roast 10 minutes.

Toss the sausage, pepper, onion and broccoli with the remaining oil and seasonings. Add to the pan, spread everything in one layer, and roast 15 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the sausage is browned and steaming hot (165°F).
meta.make_ahead: Cut the vegetables and sausage up to 2 days ahead.

freezer.text: Roasted potatoes do not freeze well.

leftovers.text: Chop leftovers and scramble with eggs for breakfast; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Cut the sausage into half-moons for small children (round coins can be a choking risk).

swaps.gluten_free: Choose a sausage labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained chickpeas instead of sausage; add them with the vegetables.

prep_day.ahead: Chop everything and store the vegetables and sausage in one container.

items.title: Glazed Meatloaf
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Tender meatloaf with a sweet tomato glaze. Leftover slices make the best sandwiches.

meta.name: Glazed Meatloaf
meta.summary: Tender meatloaf with a sweet tomato glaze. Leftover slices make the best sandwiches.
equipment: 9-by-5-inch loaf pan or rimmed baking sheet
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. In a large bowl, stir the breadcrumbs into the milk and let them soak 5 minutes.
Add the eggs, 1/4 cup ketchup, Worcestershire, salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, onion and garlic and mix well. Add the beef and mix gently with your hands just until combined. Wash your hands.
Shape into a loaf about 9 by 5 inches on a lined baking sheet (it browns better than in a pan), or press into the loaf pan.
Stir the glaze ingredients together and spread half over the loaf.
Bake 45 minutes. Spread on the rest of the glaze and bake 10 to 20 minutes more, until a thermometer in the center reads 160°F.
Rest 10 minutes before slicing.
meta.make_ahead: Shape the loaf, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day before baking; add about 10 minutes to the time.

freezer.text: Freeze baked slices separated with wax paper for 2 to 3 months, or the raw shaped loaf for 3 to 4 months, for best quality. Thaw in the fridge.

leftovers.text: Cold or warmed meatloaf on bread with ketchup is a lunchbox favorite; reheat to 165°F if serving warm.

meta.kids: Bake some of the mixture in muffin tins (about 20 minutes, still to 160°F) for kid-size mini loaves.

swaps.gluten_free: Use 3/4 cup quick oats labeled gluten-free instead of breadcrumbs, and gluten-free Worcestershire.
swaps.dairy_free: Use water or unsweetened plant milk instead of milk.

prep_day.ahead: Mix and shape the meatloaf; refrigerate covered until baking night.

items.title: Cheesy Baked Ziti
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Pasta baked in marinara with ricotta and a blanket of mozzarella. Add browned meat if you like.

meta.name: Cheesy Baked Ziti
meta.summary: Pasta baked in marinara with ricotta and a blanket of mozzarella. Add browned meat if you like.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water for 2 minutes less than the package time. Drain.
If using sausage, brown it in a skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Stir it into the sauce.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta, egg, half the Parmesan, Italian seasoning and pepper.

Toss the pasta with 1 1/2 jars of sauce. Spread half in the baking dish, dot with the ricotta mixture and sprinkle with half the mozzarella. Top with the rest of the pasta, the remaining sauce, mozzarella and Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 10 to 15 minutes more, until bubbling and 165°F in the center.
meta.make_ahead: Assemble up to 1 day ahead, cover and refrigerate; add 10 to 15 minutes to the covered time and check for 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked in a foil pan, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge and bake as directed.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions covered in the microwave to 165°F for lunches.

meta.kids: Mix a portion without ricotta for picky eaters; it bakes the same.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free pasta and check the sauce label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the ricotta and Parmesan, and use a dairy-free shredded cheese.

prep_day.ahead: Assemble the ziti and refrigerate or freeze it unbaked.

items.title: Chicken Noodle Soup
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch
items.body: A comforting pot of soup with tender chicken, carrots and egg noodles.

meta.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
meta.summary: A comforting pot of soup with tender chicken, carrots and egg noodles.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 to 8 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Add the broth, chicken, thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot. Remove the bay leaf.
Bring the soup back to a boil, add the noodles and cook until tender, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir in the parsley and taste for salt.
meta.make_ahead: Make the soup base (without noodles) up to 4 days ahead. Reheat to a boil and cook the noodles in it just before serving, so they do not go mushy.

freezer.text: Freeze the soup without noodles for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Add fresh noodles when reheating.

leftovers.text: Pack hot soup in a preheated insulated food jar for school lunch: fill the jar with boiling water for a few minutes, empty it, then add soup heated to 165°F.

meta.kids: Use small noodles or broken spaghetti for little spoons.

swaps.gluten_free: Use rice or gluten-free noodles and gluten-free broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.
swaps.meatless: Use vegetable broth and 2 cans drained white beans in place of the chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Make the soup base; cook noodles when serving.

items.title: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner
items.body: A creamy tomato soup from pantry cans and golden grilled cheese for dipping.

meta.name: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
meta.summary: A creamy tomato soup from pantry cans and golden grilled cheese for dipping.
steps: Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes, broth, sugar, basil, salt and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth with an immersion blender (or carefully in a blender, filled no more than halfway with the lid vented). Stir in the half-and-half and warm through without boiling.
Butter one side of each bread slice. Put 4 slices butter side down in a skillet over medium-low heat, add 2 slices cheese each, and top with the other bread, butter side up.
Cook 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts. Cut and serve with the soup.
meta.make_ahead: The soup keeps 4 days in the fridge; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze the soup before adding the half-and-half for 2 to 3 months for best quality; stir it in when reheating.

leftovers.text: Leftover soup makes a quick sauce for pasta.

meta.kids: Cut sandwiches into strips for dipping.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free bread and broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil in the soup and skip the half-and-half (or use canned coconut milk); use dairy-free cheese and spread.

prep_day.ahead: Make the soup.

items.title: Breakfast-for-Dinner Sheet-Pan Hash
items.subtitle: dinner,breakfast
items.body: Crispy potatoes, sausage and peppers on one pan, topped with eggs. Breakfast for dinner is a weeknight win.

meta.name: Breakfast-for-Dinner Sheet-Pan Hash
meta.summary: Crispy potatoes, sausage and peppers on one pan, topped with eggs. Breakfast for dinner is a weeknight win.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes, bell pepper and onion with the oil, salt, paprika and pepper on a rimmed baking sheet. Roast 25 minutes, stirring once, until browned.
Meanwhile, brown the sausage in a skillet, breaking it up, until no pink remains and it reaches 160°F. Drain on a paper towel.

Scatter the sausage over the potatoes. Make 8 small wells and crack an egg into each. Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are firm. (USDA advises cooking eggs until the yolks and whites are firm.)
Sprinkle with cheese and green onions and serve.
meta.make_ahead: Cube the potatoes and keep them covered in water in the fridge up to 1 day; drain and pat dry before roasting.

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Wrap leftover hash and egg in a tortilla for a breakfast burrito; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Scramble the eggs separately for kids who do not like them baked.

swaps.gluten_free: Check the sausage label.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Skip the sausage and add 1 can drained black beans with the eggs.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the sausage; chop the peppers and onion.

items.title: Freezer Bean and Cheese Burritos
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner
items.body: A big batch of burritos to wrap and freeze for fast lunches and busy nights.

meta.name: Freezer Bean and Cheese Burritos
meta.summary: A big batch of burritos to wrap and freeze for fast lunches and busy nights.
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion 4 minutes. Stir in the refried beans, black beans, salsa, cumin, chili powder and salt and heat until steaming, 3 to 4 minutes. Let cool 10 minutes.
Warm the tortillas briefly so they fold without cracking.
Spread about 1/2 cup bean mixture and 1/4 cup rice down the center of each tortilla and top with 1/4 cup cheese. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
To eat now, toast seam side down in a skillet until golden. To freeze, wrap each burrito in foil or plastic and freeze in a bag.
From frozen: unwrap, wrap in a damp paper towel and microwave 2 to 3 minutes, turning halfway, until 165°F in the center. Or bake wrapped in foil at 375°F for 35 to 40 minutes.
meta.make_ahead: The filling keeps 4 days in the fridge.

freezer.text: Freeze wrapped burritos for 2 to 3 months for best quality.

meta.kids: Make a few smaller burritos in 8-inch tortillas for little appetites.

swaps.gluten_free: Use large corn or gluten-free tortillas (they crack more easily; warm them well).
swaps.dairy_free: Use a dairy-free cheese or skip it and add diced avocado when serving.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the rice and filling, roll the burritos and freeze.

items.title: Chicken Quesadillas
items.subtitle: lunch,dinner
items.body: Crisp tortillas with melted cheese and chicken. A great way to use leftover roast or rotisserie chicken.

meta.name: Chicken Quesadillas
meta.summary: Crisp tortillas with melted cheese and chicken. A great way to use leftover roast or rotisserie chicken.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cumin, chili powder and salt.
Lay a tortilla flat and sprinkle half of it with 1/4 cup cheese, 1/2 cup chicken and another 1/4 cup cheese. Fold over. Repeat with the rest.
Brush a skillet lightly with oil and heat over medium. Cook quesadillas 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese melts and the filling is hot (165°F for cooked chicken).
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and sour cream.
meta.make_ahead: Shred the chicken and mix the seasoning up to 3 days ahead (within 3 to 4 days of when the chicken was cooked).

freezer.text: Best fresh.

leftovers.text: Cold wedges are fine in a lunchbox with an ice pack.

meta.kids: Cheese-only quesadillas are a good starting point; add a few beans or corn as they get adventurous.

swaps.gluten_free: Use corn tortillas (make smaller ones) and check the rotisserie chicken label.
swaps.meatless: Use 1 can drained black beans and 1 cup corn instead of chicken.

prep_day.ahead: Shred and season the chicken.

items.title: Vegetable Fried Rice
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch
items.body: Day-old rice, eggs and frozen vegetables become dinner in 20 minutes. Add leftover ham or chicken if you have it.

meta.name: Vegetable Fried Rice
meta.summary: Day-old rice, eggs and frozen vegetables become dinner in 20 minutes. Add leftover ham or chicken if you have it.

ingredients.prep: cooked a day ahead and chilled (makes about 4 cups)

steps: Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the eggs and scramble until no liquid egg remains (egg dishes are done at 160°F). Move to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook the onion 3 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the peas and carrots (and ham, if using) and cook 2 minutes.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and cook without stirring 1 minute so it crisps a little, then stir. Repeat a few times until the rice is hot, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, pepper, eggs and green onions.
meta.make_ahead: Cook the rice a day ahead. Spread hot rice on a tray to cool quickly and refrigerate it within 2 hours.

freezer.text: Freeze cooled fried rice in portions for up to 1 month for best quality; reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Pack for lunch and reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Kids can help crack and beat the eggs and stir in the peas.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari labeled gluten-free.
swaps.meatless: It is already meatless without the ham.

prep_day.ahead: Cook a big pot of rice for the week; cool quickly and refrigerate.

items.title: Lemon-Garlic Baked Salmon
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Salmon fillets baked with butter, lemon and garlic in about 15 minutes.

meta.name: Lemon-Garlic Baked Salmon
meta.summary: Salmon fillets baked with butter, lemon and garlic in about 15 minutes.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with foil or parchment and set the fillets skin side down on it.
Mix the melted butter, lemon juice and garlic and brush over the salmon. Sprinkle with salt, pepper and paprika.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, until the thickest part reaches 145°F and the flesh flakes easily with a fork.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
meta.make_ahead: Mix the lemon-garlic butter up to 3 days ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze raw fillets instead; thaw overnight in the fridge before baking.

leftovers.text: Flake cold salmon onto a salad or into a wrap the next day.

meta.kids: Check for pin bones by running a finger along the fillet before baking. A drizzle of honey on a kid portion helps (not for babies under 12 months).

swaps.dairy_free: Use olive oil instead of butter.

prep_day.ahead: Thaw fillets in the fridge; mix the butter.

items.title: Skillet Pork Chops
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Golden, juicy boneless chops with a quick pan sauce.

meta.name: Skillet Pork Chops
meta.summary: Golden, juicy boneless chops with a quick pan sauce.
steps: Pat the chops dry. Mix the salt, pepper, garlic powder and paprika and rub on both sides.
Heat the oil in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chops 4 to 5 minutes per side, until browned and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 145°F.
Move the chops to a clean plate and let them rest at least 3 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the broth, mustard and honey to the pan and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes, then swirl in the butter. Spoon over the chops.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

meta.make_ahead: Season the chops up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate covered.

freezer.text: Freeze raw chops instead, 4 to 6 months for best quality.

leftovers.text: Slice thin for sandwiches or fried rice; reheat to 165°F.

meta.kids: Slice the chop into thin strips for younger children; 145°F pork can look slightly pink in the center and is safe after the rest.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free broth.
swaps.dairy_free: Skip the butter in the sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Season the chops.

items.title: Shepherd's Pie
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Savory beef and vegetables under a mashed-potato crust. Made with beef it is often called cottage pie; use ground lamb for the classic.

meta.name: Shepherd's Pie
meta.summary: Savory beef and vegetables under a mashed-potato crust. Made with beef it is often called cottage pie; use ground lamb for the classic.
steps: Cover the potatoes with cold salted water in a large pot, bring to a boil and cook 15 minutes, until very tender. Drain and mash with the butter, milk and salt.

Meanwhile, heat the oven to 400°F. Heat the oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the beef, onion and carrots, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F, about 8 minutes. Spoon off extra fat. Add the garlic for 1 minute.

Stir in the tomato paste and flour and cook 1 minute. Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme, salt and pepper and simmer 5 minutes, until thick. Stir in the peas and corn. (Move to a baking dish if your skillet is not oven-safe.)
Spread the mashed potatoes over the filling to the edges and rough up the top with a fork. Sprinkle with cheese if you like.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling at the edges, golden on top and 165°F in the center.
meta.make_ahead: Assemble, cool, cover and refrigerate up to 1 day. Bake about 15 minutes longer, until 165°F in the center.

freezer.text: Freeze assembled and unbaked, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Thaw in the fridge before baking.

leftovers.text: Reheat portions covered to 165°F for lunch.

meta.kids: Kids can help spread and swirl the potatoes.

swaps.gluten_free: Thicken with 1 tablespoon cornstarch mixed with 2 tablespoons cold water instead of flour; check the Worcestershire and broth labels.
swaps.dairy_free: Mash the potatoes with olive oil and some of their cooking water; skip the cheese.
swaps.meatless: Use 2 cans drained lentils and 8 ounces chopped mushrooms instead of beef, with vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Make the filling and mashed potatoes; assemble and refrigerate.

items.title: Hearty Beef Stew
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Chunks of beef simmered with potatoes and carrots until spoon-tender.

meta.name: Hearty Beef Stew
meta.summary: Chunks of beef simmered with potatoes and carrots until spoon-tender.
equipment: Dutch oven or large heavy pot (or slow cooker)
steps: Pat the beef dry, season with the salt and pepper, and toss with the flour.
Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in two batches, 5 to 6 minutes per batch, adding the last of the oil as needed. Move to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion 4 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the broth, Worcestershire, thyme and bay leaves, scraping up the browned bits. Return the beef. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently 1 1/2 hours.

Add the potatoes, carrots and celery and simmer covered 30 to 40 minutes more, until the beef and vegetables are tender. (Beef is safe at 145°F; stew meat needs this long, gentle simmer to turn tender.) Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes. Remove the bay leaves.
Slow cooker: after browning, put everything except the peas in the cooker and cook on low 8 hours. Stir in the peas at the end.

safety.food: beef, pork or lamb steaks, chops and roasts

meta.make_ahead: Stew is even better the next day. Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Potatoes soften a little after freezing.

leftovers.text: Pack in a preheated insulated food jar for lunch; reheat to 165°F first.

meta.kids: Cut the meat and vegetables a little smaller for young children.

swaps.gluten_free: Toss the beef in 2 tablespoons cornstarch instead of flour; check the broth and Worcestershire labels.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the stew start to finish; it reheats well all week.

items.title: Chicken Pot Pie
items.subtitle: dinner
items.body: Creamy chicken and vegetables under a flaky crust. Uses leftover or rotisserie chicken.

meta.name: Chicken Pot Pie
meta.summary: Creamy chicken and vegetables under a flaky crust. Uses leftover or rotisserie chicken.
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a baking sheet on the lower rack to catch drips.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and celery 5 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth, then the milk. Simmer, stirring, until thick, about 3 minutes. Add the thyme, salt, pepper, chicken and peas and carrots.
Line the pie plate with one crust, pour in the filling and top with the second crust. Pinch the edges to seal, cut 4 small slits in the top and brush with the egg.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the crust is deep golden and the filling bubbles and reaches 165°F. Let it rest 10 minutes before cutting.
meta.make_ahead: Make the filling up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Assemble with cold filling and add 10 minutes to the baking time.

freezer.text: Freeze unbaked, well wrapped, for 2 to 3 months for best quality. Bake from frozen at 400°F for about 60 to 70 minutes (cover the edges with foil if they brown too fast) until 165°F in the center.

leftovers.text: Reheat wedges in the oven or microwave to 165°F.

meta.kids: Kids can cut shapes from crust scraps to decorate the top.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free crust and thicken with 3 tablespoons cornstarch mixed into the cold milk.
swaps.meatless: Use 3 cups mixed vegetables and 1 can drained white beans instead of chicken, with vegetable broth.

prep_day.ahead: Make the filling; assemble on the night you bake.

items.title: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
items.subtitle: dinner,lunch,side
items.body: A smooth, creamy cheese sauce made in the same pot as the pasta.

meta.name: Stovetop Mac and Cheese
meta.summary: A smooth, creamy cheese sauce made in the same pot as the pasta.

ingredients.prep: for the pasta water (most is poured off, so it is left out of nutrition)

steps: Cook the macaroni in a large pot of boiling salted water until just tender. Drain and set aside.
In the same pot, melt the butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the milk. Cook, whisking, until it thickens and coats a spoon, 4 to 5 minutes. Stir in the mustard, garlic powder and salt.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the cheese a handful at a time until smooth. Add the macaroni and stir to coat.
meta.make_ahead: Best fresh. To reheat, add a splash of milk and warm gently, stirring, until hot (165°F).
